faqs.question: Is it cheaper to share a tutor with other families in my building?
faqs.answer: Usually somewhat, and not for the reason parents assume. Four one-to-one hours of home tuition in four flats are still four hours of teaching, so the saving comes from travel rather than from the lesson. A tutor who earns a whole evening in one tower has no dead time between students and will price the trip accordingly. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai also move with board, level, subject scarcity and session length, so a shared evening changes one of five inputs. Genuine group teaching costs less again and is a different product with different trade-offs.

faqs.question: My neighbour recommended her tutor. How do I check before saying yes?
faqs.answer: Treat the recommendation as evidence of reliability and likeability, which is real, and verify the teaching separately. Ask the tutor to describe how your child's course is assessed without looking it up: papers, weightings, internal components, deadlines. Ask what the first three sessions would cover. Ask how they mark a draft. If your child is on a different programme from your neighbour's, that is the most common reason a good referral turns into a mediocre arrangement, and five minutes of questions will surface it before a term does.

faqs.question: What if we want to stop but the tutor still teaches three other families here?
faqs.answer: Give notice directly, in writing, with a reason that is about fit rather than about failure, and give it at the end of a month rather than mid-draft. The awkwardness is real because you will share a lift afterwards, and it is survivable. What makes it worse is drifting: cancelling repeatedly, paying late, or letting the neighbours deliver the message. The tutor loses an hour in the middle of their evening and will manage. You owe them notice and clarity, not an apology or a justification to the building.

faqs.question: Can I ask the tutor how the other children in my building are doing?
faqs.answer: No, and the better move is to tell the tutor at the start that you will not and that you expect the same discretion about your child. Marks move through a tower faster than through a school. A tutor who answers that question for you will answer it about your child on the next floor, and the comparison it sets off damages the children before it damages anyone's relationships. Agree confidentiality out loud in the first conversation. A professional tutor will be relieved that somebody raised it.

faqs.question: Our slot is the last one of the evening and my son is exhausted. What can we do?
faqs.answer: Raise it with the tutor directly and be ready to trade something for it. Shared evenings run on seniority, so the earlier slots belong to whoever joined first, and moving yours means asking another family to move theirs. Realistic options are swapping to a different weekday where you can be earlier, taking a longer weekend morning session instead of a tired weekday hour, or moving that subject online so the time is no longer tied to the tutor's route through the building. A tired nine o'clock hour is worth less than you are paying for it.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a separate gate pass for each family in the complex?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Most large Mumbai complexes will register a recurring visitor against one resident, and once that entry exists the tutor is cleared for the building rather than for a flat, though some societies still want each resident to approve the visit in the app. Sort it out before the first session rather than at the gate, give the tutor the correct visitor gate for after seven in the evening, and tell them where to park. Ten minutes lost at a gate every week is a term of teaching over a year.

faqs.question: Should the sessions happen in our flat or in the clubhouse study room?
faqs.answer: Your flat, for one-to-one home tuition, almost always. The tutor needs to see the actual desk, the actual notes and the actual distractions, and a clubhouse room shows them a tidied child. Clubhouse rooms make sense for genuine group sessions, for families with a younger sibling making the flat impossible, or where a parent is not home and prefers a semi-public space. If you use one, book it as a standing weekly slot, because losing the room to a society event mid-term ends more arrangements than bad teaching does.

faqs.question: Does one of us need to be at home while the tutor is here?
faqs.answer: For the first two sessions, be in the flat and sit within earshot rather than in the room. You are listening for whether your child is talking or only nodding, and whether the hour has a shape. After that, a parent in the room usually makes a teenager less willing to admit confusion. If nobody can be home, say so when booking, keep the session in a common area of the flat rather than a bedroom, and ask for the written end-of-session note every time rather than sometimes.

faqs.question: Our building is in Kharghar and nobody good will travel here for one child. Is sharing the answer?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and this is where a shared evening stops being a convenience and becomes the mechanism. A specialist will cross from Nerul, Vashi or over the Atal Setu for an evening of three or four families and not for a single hour. Find the other IB and IGCSE families in your complex before you start searching, agree a weekday between you, and ask as a group. The same logic works along Ghodbunder Road in Thane and in the newer Panvel and Airoli complexes where single-family bookings rarely survive the year.

faqs.question: What if my child ends up being compared to the neighbour's child?
faqs.answer: Assume it will happen and build the defences early, because a tower compares children more intensely than a classroom does. Keep marks out of the building group. Do not discuss the tutor's feedback in the lobby. Tell your child that the tutor is not allowed to discuss them upstairs, which removes the fear that their mistakes are travelling. Then measure progress against your own child in August rather than against anyone on another floor. The comparison instinct is the main cost of a shared arrangement and it is the one fully within your control.

faqs.question: Can we start a shared arrangement from scratch rather than joining one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it tends to work better than joining a mature one, because the slots are unallocated and the expectations are set together. Find two or three families in your complex on the same board and roughly the same stage, agree one evening, and request together so the tutor sees a full evening from day one. Settle three things in advance: the slot order, the notice period if a family leaves, and confidentiality between families. Arrangements that collapse in this city almost always skipped the second and third.

sections.heading: What comes after IGCSE: the IB Diploma, A Levels or an Indian board?
paragraphs: A school that publishes an IGCSE pathway and not a sixth-form Diploma Programme puts every family in the same position at the end of Year 11: you are moving somewhere. That single fact reframes the whole of Years 9 to 11. Confirm the school's own provision and transfer guidance with the school directly rather than with us, because we do not speak for it. But if a move is on the cards, the destination should be a live conversation in Year 9, not a scramble in the January of Year 11 when application deadlines across Mumbai have already closed.

The IB Diploma Programme (DP) takes six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). It is broad and it is linear: almost nothing is dropped, every subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA), and the written work clusters in DP1 term three and DP2 term one. It suits a student who is decent across the board, writes reasonably and manages deadlines. It punishes a student who is excellent at three things and allergic to the other three.

International A Levels invert that. Cambridge International A Level and Pearson Edexcel International A Level both run on three or four subjects taken deep, with no TOK, no Extended Essay and no compulsory service component. A student who knows they want Physics, Maths and Chemistry and nothing else gets two years of exactly that. The trade-off is that the narrowing is real and early, and some overseas universities ask for a fourth subject or a particular combination. An Indian board is the third branch: CBSE or ISC Class 11 and 12, usually chosen because the family is aiming at JEE, NEET, CLAT or CUET, where the syllabus, the question style and the non-calculator convention all sit closer to the Indian boards than to Cambridge.

None of these is better. They are different machines, and the preparation that feeds them differs from Year 9 onwards. We cover all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 with a tutor in Mumbai briefed on which of the three branches your child is walking towards, because the honest answer to "should she take Additional Maths" is a question about Year 12, not about Year 10.

sections.heading: Which Year 10 subjects should an Activity High School student actually take?
paragraphs: The right Year 10 subject set depends on the destination, and that is the whole answer. Cambridge IGCSE lets a student pick across language, humanities, sciences, mathematics and the creative group, and most schools in Mumbai run eight or nine subjects. The decisions that bite later are not which subjects are enjoyable now. They are the tier decisions: Core or Extended in Mathematics 0580, Core or Extended in the sciences, and whether Additional Mathematics 0606 goes on the timetable at all.

Core tier caps the available grade. A student sitting Core Mathematics 0580 cannot reach the top grades on the Cambridge IGCSE A* to G scale, and a sixth form offering Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or Cambridge International A Level Mathematics will usually expect Extended. If the destination is the IB Diploma with Maths at HL, Extended is not a stretch goal, it is the entry condition. If the destination is Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, or a humanities-heavy A Level set, Core may be the sane choice that protects the rest of the timetable. A tutor who tells you Extended is always better has not asked where the student is going.

The sciences carry a second quiet decision. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each end with either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and that choice is made by the school rather than the family. It matters because the IB Diploma sciences are assessed partly through practical work and an Internal Assessment built on the student's own investigation, while A Level sciences carry a practical endorsement. A student who has only ever written about experiments on Paper 6 arrives in DP1 having never designed one. Three or four sessions in Year 11 on planning, variables and uncertainty closes that gap before it opens.

Languages and English behave the same way. First Language English 0500 trains a different muscle from English B at Standard Level in the IB, and a student intending an Indian board needs a second language the board will accept for Class 11. We run all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai, and a Year 10 planning session is often the single most useful hour a family buys all year: it is cheaper than a term of catching up on a subject chosen for the wrong reason.

sections.heading: The IGCSE calendar Activity High School families in Mumbai plan around
paragraphs: The Mumbai school year opens in June and closes in April, with a Diwali break around late October or early November and a shorter break at the end of December. Cambridge runs two main exam series, May and June and then October and November, with results released in August and January. Which series a cohort is entered for is a decision made by the school, so confirm it there: IB Gram is independent, not affiliated with Activity High School or any other school named on this page, and we will not guess at a calendar we have no sight of.

What is predictable is the shape of the pressure. For a Year 11 cohort sitting the May and June series, the squeeze starts in the second half of November and runs to the end of January. Mocks land in that window, coursework and school-assessed components are finalised in the same weeks, and the Diwali break that looks like breathing room is usually the last clean fortnight of the year. A student who begins tutoring in February for a May paper has about eleven usable weeks after half-terms and revision leave are removed, which is enough to fix technique and not enough to fix content.

The second pressure point is less visible and more consequential at an IGCSE-only school: sixth-form applications. Mumbai schools offering the IB Diploma or A Levels typically open applications and run assessments between November and February of Year 11, in the same weeks as the mocks. That is the collision this page exists for. A family that has not decided between the Diploma, A Levels and an Indian board by October of Year 11 is making two hard decisions at once while the child is sitting practice papers.

Working backwards from that, the sensible rhythm is a subject-choice review in Year 9 term three, a tier confirmation in Year 10 term one, a destination shortlist by the end of Year 10, and tutoring in Year 11 aimed at both the exam and the entrance requirement. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai will not run that timetable for you, but a good one will keep reminding you that it exists.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for an Activity High School student?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and it is the default for a reason. An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Activity High School students in Mumbai sitting at the dining table can see the exercise book, the half-finished past paper and the three questions the student skipped, which is information no screen share surrenders easily. For Years 9 to 11, when handwriting method, setting out working and showing steps are still being built, physical proximity does real work. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai also absorbs the small frictions: a forgotten textbook, a question from a sibling, a parent who wants two minutes at the end.

The honest cost of home tuition is scarcity and rigidity. A tutor travelling to Peddar Road on a Tuesday evening can realistically teach one, maybe two students that evening, which narrows the pool and makes the slot hard to move. If your child needs a specialist in a thinner subject, Economics 0455 at Extended level or Additional Mathematics 0606, insisting on home sessions in a narrow time window may leave you choosing between a convenient tutor and a good one.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai solves exactly that. Online opens the pool to the whole city and beyond, makes a 9pm slot possible, and removes the flyover from the equation entirely. It works best with an older, self-directed student, a document camera or even a phone propped over the page, and a subject where the working can be shown. It works badly when the student is thirteen, disorganised and alone in a room with a laptop. Be realistic about which of those describes yours.

Hybrid is what most families settle into by the second term and it is worth planning for rather than drifting into. One home session a week anchors the relationship and handles anything physical, and one shorter online session mid-week handles question practice, a homework check or a pre-test clinic. During the November to January squeeze, hybrid is also the only way to add a third contact hour without adding a third journey across South Mumbai.

sections.heading: How are IB and IGCSE tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor proposed as an IB and IGCSE tutor for Activity High School students in Mumbai is checked on four things before a family ever sees the profile: identity with a government photo document, the qualification claimed in the subject, demonstrated knowledge of the specific syllabus and tier, and references from families who have actually worked with them. The subject check is the one that filters hardest. A Physics graduate who has never looked at Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 6 will teach good Physics and poor exam technique, and at this level the two are not the same skill.

What we deliberately do not check, because we cannot, is anything internal to a school. No tutor on this platform is presented as having taught at Activity High School, as knowing its staff, as having seen its internal assessments or as having any line into its grading. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to the school, and any tutor anywhere in Mumbai who implies that kind of access is telling you something you should not want to be true.

There are four things you should check yourself, in the first session rather than the fourth. Ask the tutor which tier your child is on and what the top grade available at that tier is; a tutor who does not know is not prepared. Ask them to name the papers in the subject and say what each one tests. Ask what they would do differently if the destination were the IB Diploma rather than an Indian board, which is the question this whole page turns on. And ask what they will send you after each month. There is no single best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai, only a good fit for one student in one subject heading in one direction.

Finally, check the room before you check the credentials. A standing weekly slot in a home needs a table, a light, a door that closes and an adult somewhere in the flat. Tutors who are good at this will ask about all four in the first phone call, and the ones who do not ask are usually the ones who later complain about the television.

sections.heading: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 prepared three different ways
paragraphs: Take one concrete component: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Extended tier, which is examined across Papers 2 and 4. The paper structure has been revised in recent syllabus versions, so confirm with the school which papers the cohort sits. On Paper 4 a student may be asked to sketch the curve of a cubic such as y = x cubed minus four x, then state the coordinates of its local maximum and minimum. The expected method at IGCSE is graphical: plot it on a calculator, use the trace or maximum function, read the values off, round sensibly. A student who does that cleanly gets full marks and has learned almost nothing about why the turning points are where they are.

Now run the same student forward three ways. Heading for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the IB Diploma, that question becomes a differentiation problem: find the derivative, set it to zero, solve the resulting quadratic exactly, and justify which root is the maximum using the second derivative. The calculator answer is worth nothing without the algebra. So the Year 10 and 11 tutoring plan for that student front-loads exact surd work, factorising, index laws and completing the square, and brings in Additional Mathematics 0606 as the bridge, because 0606 introduces the derivative a full year before the Diploma does.

Heading for Cambridge International A Level Mathematics, the destination is similar but the emphasis shifts to Pure 1 fluency: transformations of graphs, the discriminant, and the habit of writing a solution as an argument rather than an answer. Heading for CBSE or ISC Class 11 and then JEE, the calculator disappears entirely. That student needs the cubic factorised by hand, surds and logarithms manipulated mentally, and trigonometric identities at recall speed, because the Indian entrance papers assume a non-calculator baseline that Cambridge IGCSE never builds. And heading for Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, the graphical method from Paper 4 is genuinely the right one, and the tutoring hours are better spent on modelling language, interpreting a result in context and writing it up.

One question, one syllabus code, four preparation plans. This is why we ask about the destination before matching an IB and IGCSE tutor for Activity High School students in Mumbai, and why a tutor whose only move is more past papers is the wrong tutor for a Year 10 student with a decision still open.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam series
paragraphs: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching. What can be promised is a sequence, and if the sequence does not appear on schedule the arrangement needs changing rather than extending. At four weeks, you should not expect a score change at all. You should expect a diagnosis you can repeat back: this student is losing marks on Paper 4 structured questions because she abandons a question after one failed attempt, not because she does not know the topic. If after four sessions nobody can tell you that sentence, the tutor is teaching content and not watching the student.

At one term, roughly twelve sessions, the measurable thing is method under time pressure. The student should be finishing papers rather than running out, writing working that an examiner can follow, and recognising question types on sight. School test scores often move in this window, sometimes a lot, sometimes not at all, because a school test samples a narrow slice of the syllabus and timing can flatter or hide real progress. A single internal test is weak evidence in both directions.

At one full exam series, the picture is honest for the first time, and it is also where expectations should be set carefully. Tutoring compounds with everything else a student does: attendance, sleep, how much they read, whether the subject was the right choice in the first place. A student who started two tiers below the target in February and sits the paper in May has not had enough time, and a tutor who says so in February is being useful rather than pessimistic. We would rather lose the enquiry than take it on a promise nobody can keep.

The limits are worth stating plainly. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai cannot fix a subject that was wrongly chosen, cannot replace school teaching, and cannot make a student want the IB Diploma if they want A Levels. What a good one does is make the next decision clearer and the next paper more survivable, which over two years is a great deal.

sections.heading: Starting home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready for session one
paragraphs: Arranging an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai takes less preparation than families expect, but the three things that speed it up are the three most often missing. First, the subject list with the tier for each one, which is on the school's entry documentation rather than in anyone's memory. Second, the last two marked assessments, including the one your child would rather you did not see, because the errors in that paper are the entire first session. Third, the two or three weekday evening slots that will still work in November, not the ones that work this week.

The first session itself runs about ninety minutes and is deliberately unglamorous. The tutor goes through the marked papers question by question with the student, stops at each lost mark and asks what happened there, sorts the losses into content gaps, method gaps and timing gaps, and then writes those three piles down. Parents are welcome for the last ten minutes, and that is usually when the useful conversation happens, because the tutor will say something about the destination question that reframes the term.

After that you should have a plan with dates on it: which topics in which weeks, which past paper components get attempted under timed conditions, and what gets reviewed before the mocks. If the destination is still open between the IB Diploma, A Levels and an Indian board, say so at the start. The plan changes depending on the answer, and a tutor who is told in January what they could have been told in July loses much of the advantage they had.

If a tutor is not working, tell us in week three rather than week eight. Replacements are routine, there is no argument about it, and the diagnostic notes transfer to the next tutor so your child does not repeat the first session from scratch.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9. Is it too early to be thinking about the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, Year 9 is exactly the right time, because the decisions that constrain the IB Diploma are made in Year 10 rather than Year 12. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches generally expects Extended tier Mathematics 0580 and benefits enormously from Additional Mathematics 0606, and both of those go on the timetable before the student has seen a Diploma subject brief. A Year 9 conversation costs one planning session. A Year 11 realisation that the Maths tier blocks the HL choice costs a year of catching up, or a changed destination.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building near Peddar Road for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the standard arrangement for this cluster. Tutors are matched from within South Mumbai rather than brought down from the suburbs, because a weekly journey from Andheri to Peddar Road at 6.30pm is not an arrangement that survives a full academic year. In practice that means tutors living around Tardeo, Worli, Malabar Hill, Grant Road or Mahalaxmi. Tell us your realistic window before the match rather than after, since a tutor who agrees to an impossible slot out of politeness is a tutor you will be replacing in October.

faqs.question: How do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai actually get set?
faqs.answer: IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on five things and we quote none of them blind. Board and level come first, since Diploma Higher Level work costs more than Year 9 support. Subject scarcity comes second: a Physics or Economics specialist at Extended level is harder to find than a general Maths tutor. Then travel distance and the time of day, because an evening slot on the island city is worth more to a tutor than an afternoon one. Then session length and frequency, and finally whether you are running home, online or hybrid sessions. Online is usually the cheaper structure.

faqs.question: Should my child take Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606?
faqs.answer: Take it if the destination is Higher Level Maths in the IB Diploma or A Level Mathematics, and think hard if it is not. Additional Mathematics 0606 introduces calculus, functions and more demanding algebra a year before a sixth form would, which makes the first term of either destination dramatically less brutal. It is also a real extra subject on an already full timetable, and a student who takes it and does badly has bought nothing. The test is not whether the student is strong at Maths. It is whether the next two years need calculus at speed.

faqs.question: Our building in Breach Candy needs a visitor gate pass. How does that work for home classes?
faqs.answer: Most societies around Breach Candy, Cumballa Hill and Napean Sea Road will issue a standing entry for a recurring weekly visitor once a resident registers the name, the slot and a photo identity document. Ask your society office in the week before the first session rather than on the evening itself, because a tutor held at the gate for twenty minutes loses a quarter of the lesson. Tutors carry photo identity to every session as a matter of course. If your building requires a fresh pass each visit, tell us, because it affects which tutors will realistically commit to the slot.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for IGCSE Physics practical papers?
faqs.answer: For the written practical papers, yes; for building genuine laboratory instinct, only partly. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is a written paper about experiments, and it responds very well to online teaching because the whole skill is reading a method, spotting the controlled variable and handling uncertainty on paper. Paper 5, the practical test, is harder to prepare remotely. If the destination is an IB Diploma science with its Internal Assessment, we would push for at least some home sessions in Year 11 spent designing investigations rather than describing them.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, with no argument and no persuasion attempt. The common signals are worth naming: no written diagnosis after four sessions, lessons that are just the next chapter of the textbook, a tutor who cannot say which tier your child sits, or a student who has started quietly dreading the slot. Replacement usually takes under a fortnight in South Mumbai and longer for scarce subjects. The diagnostic notes from the first tutor pass to the second, so your child does not spend session one of the new arrangement repeating the same past paper.

faqs.question: Are A Levels a safer choice than the IB Diploma after IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Neither is safer; they fail different students. A Levels suit a student with three clear strengths and no patience for breadth, and they remove the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and service commitments entirely. The IB Diploma suits a student who is solid across subjects, writes decently and can hold several deadlines at once. The risk with A Levels is early narrowing, since a student who picks sciences at sixteen and changes their mind at eighteen has fewer options. The risk with the Diploma is volume. Choose against your child's actual working style, not the reputation of the certificate.

faqs.question: My child wants to write JEE. Does an IGCSE background put them behind?
faqs.answer: Not behind on concepts, but behind on two habits that matter a great deal. The first is the calculator: Cambridge IGCSE permits one on most papers and Indian entrance examinations do not, so arithmetic, surds and logarithms need to come back to hand speed. The second is question volume and style, since JEE rewards pattern recognition across hundreds of problems rather than structured multi-part questions. A student moving from an IGCSE school in Mumbai to CBSE or ISC Class 11 should start that transition in the Year 11 summer, not in Class 11 itself.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 student realistically need?
faqs.answer: One session per subject per week is the working baseline, rising to two in the November to January window when mocks, coursework deadlines and sixth-form applications overlap. Two subjects at one session each is manageable alongside school. Four subjects at two sessions each is not, and families who try it usually find the student stops doing independent work altogether, which is the opposite of the point. If the list of weak subjects runs to four or more, the problem is probably the subject set or the workload rather than the teaching, and that is a different conversation.

sections.heading: How IB Gram builds a tutor shortlist for an Aditya Birla World Academy family in Mumbai
paragraphs: A request that opens with 'my daughter is in Year 11 and we cannot work out whether she should carry on into the Diploma' is a different request from 'she is stuck on quadratics'. The first is a pathway question. The second is a subject question. Most families who write to us about IB and IGCSE home tutoring for Aditya Birla World Academy students in Mumbai send the second, and discover two conversations later that they were really asking the first. So the shortlist gets built backwards from the decision rather than forwards from a chapter list. The tutor who can speak honestly about what Higher Level (HL) Chemistry asks of a sixteen-year-old is rarely the same tutor whose strength is drilling IGCSE past papers.

The process runs in four steps. 1. You tell us the year group, the board the child is sitting this academic year, the subjects that are wobbling, and whether a pathway decision is live. 2. We map that against the assessment calendar the child is actually on, because a Year 11 IGCSE term and a Diploma Programme first-year term load their pressure into different months. 3. What we deliberately avoid is sending a long list and leaving you to sort it. A directory is cheap to produce and useless to a parent with thirty minutes between a work call and dinner. We also refuse to match on the subject label alone. 'Physics' is a different job at IGCSE 0625, with its alternative-to-practical paper, than it is at Higher Level in the Diploma, where an Internal Assessment (IA) has to be individually investigated, written up and moderated. Geography is treated as a hard constraint rather than a detail. We would rather tell you on day one that your window is hard to staff from your side of the city than place someone who quietly stops turning up in November. sections.heading: Should a Year 11 student continue into the IB Diploma or move to A Levels?
paragraphs: Continue into the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme if the student is steady across six subjects and manages long, self-directed projects without constant chasing. Move to A Levels if the student is clearly stronger in three subjects than in six, and would rather go deep than wide. Aditya Birla World Academy publicly offers IB DP and Cambridge IGCSE, so an A Level route means changing schools, which turns a subject decision into a family decision with a deadline attached to it.

The two routes are not simply harder and easier versions of each other. The Diploma asks for six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level (SL), plus three core requirements: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every one of those six subjects carries its own Internal Assessment, which is marked by the school and moderated externally. The whole thing is linear across two years and lands in a single May examination session. A student who is good at tests but poor at starting work without a prompt finds the Diploma brutal, because roughly a fifth of the final points are earned months before the exams in pieces of coursework nobody will chase you about twice.

A Level programmes, run through Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel depending on the school, ask for three or four subjects and in most cases nothing else. There is no Theory of Knowledge essay, no four-thousand-word Extended Essay, no service requirement. Some schools add an Extended Project Qualification, but it is optional. The trade is breadth for depth: an A Level Mathematics syllabus goes further into pure mathematics than Standard Level analysis does, and the examination weighting is close to total, so a bad February does not permanently cost you marks the way a weak IA does.

Cambridge IGCSE sits underneath both and is the shared base. The grades a student takes out of Year 11 are what universities never see and what the next school very much does. A tutor's job at this stage is to make those grades accurate rather than flattering, because an inflated predicted grade in Extended Mathematics is how a student ends up in Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in September and in trouble by December.

sections.heading: Which subjects should a dual-board student lock in, and when?
paragraphs: Lock the IGCSE Core or Extended decision by the start of Year 10 and the Higher Level or Standard Level decision by the spring of Year 11. Those are the two gates that close. Everything else can be revisited. Our roster covers all IB and IGCSE subjects but no single tutor in Mumbai does, and a parent who is told otherwise should push back hard on which components that person has actually taught and marked.

At IGCSE, the Core and Extended split is the one families underestimate. Extended Mathematics 0580 Paper 4 is the realistic prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level; a Core candidate capped at grade C has not failed at anything, but the Diploma door for Higher Level mathematics is effectively shut. The sciences work the same way: Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610 all run Extended papers plus a practical component, usually the alternative-to-practical written paper rather than a lab exam, and the question style there rewards method description far more than recall. Language and literature choices matter for a different reason: a second language taken at IGCSE determines whether Group 2 at Standard Level will be a quiet pass or a two-year problem.

In the Diploma, the Internal Assessment is where the work actually lives. Mathematics asks for an exploration, a piece of individual mathematical writing against five criteria. The Group 4 sciences ask for a personally designed investigation assessed on exploration, analysis and evaluation. History asks for a source-based investigation with a formal evaluation of two sources. Economics asks for commentaries built on recent news articles. Business Management asks for a research project grounded in a real organisation. Visual Arts asks for a comparative study. These are not homework. They are the pieces a tutor can genuinely help with, because the criteria are published and most students have simply never been taught to read a criterion band and write to it.

We list all IB and IGCSE subjects, and at IGCSE Years 9-11 the tutor in Mumbai most families need is a strong generalist in two adjacent subjects rather than six specialists. By the first Diploma year that flips: the HL subjects want someone who has marked at that level, and a generalist starts to run out of road around the second term.

The last two kilometres are. A tutor off the 5.40 at Mumbai Central can reach Altamount Road on foot faster than by cab on a Friday, and the good ones already know that.

South Mumbai takes in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Worli, Breach Candy and Walkeshwar, and that is where almost every match for this school is made. paragraphs: Start with the boundary, because it matters more than anything else on this page. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for an Aditya Birla World Academy student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and it is what most families here ask for. A tutor at your dining table sees the things a screen hides: the phone face-down next to the notebook, the handwriting that collapses halfway down a long algebra question, the fact that your son has been copying worked examples rather than attempting them. For IB and IGCSE home tuition for Aditya Birla World Academy students in Mumbai, the strongest argument for the in-person option is diagnostic rather than pedagogical. The teaching could happen anywhere. The noticing cannot.

The honest cost of home tuition is scheduling. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai travelling to Tardeo for a six o'clock weekday slot is committing to leave wherever they are by about five, which rules out anyone teaching a late-afternoon session elsewhere in the city. That shrinks the pool, and a shrunken pool means you are choosing from fewer people with exactly the right component experience. It is a real trade and we would rather you make it knowingly.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai solves the pool problem completely. Screen-shared past papers, a graphics tablet and a document camera for handwritten working now make online sessions genuinely comparable for mathematics and the sciences, and markedly better for anything where the tutor needs to annotate a student's own typed draft: an Extended Essay chapter, an Economics commentary, a History IA source evaluation. Online is also the only mode that survives a week when the child is ill, a building lift is out, or the Peddar Road signals have turned a thirty-minute run into an hour.

Hybrid is what most of our South Mumbai families settle on after a term, and it is the arrangement we would suggest first for a dual-board household weighing a pathway decision. One in-person session a week at home for the subject that needs supervision, one online session for review and marked-work feedback, and a switch to fully online for the February crunch, when nobody wants a tutor stuck on the Eastern Express Highway while a draft is due. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai who refuses to work this way is usually optimising for their own convenience.

sections.heading: How a tutor is checked before you meet them, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Every tutor goes through the same four checks before a profile reaches you: government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification they claim, a subject interview with someone who has taught that syllabus, and references from families or institutions they have worked with. The subject interview is the one that filters hardest. We ask an applicant for an IB or IGCSE tutor for Aditya Birla World Academy students in Mumbai to talk through a real past-paper question at the level they are applying for, explain what a marker is looking for, and say what they would do with a student who got it wrong in a specific way. A surprising number of people with strong paper credentials cannot do that.

There are things verification cannot settle, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. We cannot tell you whether your daughter will find a particular person easy to talk to, which at fifteen is close to the whole game. We cannot verify a claim of insider knowledge about any school, and we do not accept such claims on profiles at all. Nobody on this platform taught at Aditya Birla World Academy on our behalf, has access to its materials, or can tell you what is coming up in a school assessment.

Here is what to check yourself, in the first session, while you are still in the room. Ask the tutor to name the papers and components your child is sitting. Ask what the mark scheme actually rewards on a six-mark extended-response question. Ask for the plan for the first six weeks and whether it starts with a diagnostic. Ask what they will do differently if the diagnostic comes back worse than the school report suggests. Vague answers to those four questions are a clearer signal than any certificate.

Parents regularly ask us who the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is, and the only truthful reply is that the question has no answer. There is a best match for one student in one subject at one stage of one board, and that person may be a poor match for the sibling or for the same child eighteen months later. Treat anyone who answers that question confidently as someone selling rather than advising.

sections.heading: What the IB Diploma and the A Level route each demand of a Year 11 student
paragraphs: The clearest way to see the difference is to put two Novembers side by side. Take a Year 11 student at a Tardeo campus in the last fortnight of November. Her IGCSE English Literature coursework portfolio has a final submission date, her Mathematics 0580 Extended Paper 4 mock falls in the same week, and the Chemistry 0620 alternative-to-practical mock is the Monday after. Three deadlines, all short, all marked against familiar criteria, all recoverable: a bad Paper 4 mock in November costs her nothing in May. Now move the same child fourteen months forward into the first Diploma year, same fortnight of November. There are no mocks. Instead the TOK exhibition commentary is due, the Physics Internal Assessment proposal needs teacher sign-off before the winter break, and the Extended Essay supervisor wants a research question in writing. Nothing is marked yet. Everything that happens here is permanent.

That contrast is the pathway decision in miniature. The IGCSE calendar front-loads short, frequent, low-stakes deadlines and the student learns to sprint. The Diploma calendar back-loads long-form, individually supervised work whose quality is determined months before anyone puts a mark on it, and the student has to learn to plan. A child who sprints well and plans badly will often post excellent IGCSE grades in May and then stall in the following December, which is the single most common story we hear from families at this school.

A Levels place the weight somewhere else again. Three subjects in depth, examination-dominated assessment, and a syllabus that assumes the student will go further into fewer things. The demand there is tolerance for depth: a student who found Extended Mathematics satisfying rather than survivable, who reads around a subject unprompted, who is bored by breadth. It also narrows university options in some systems and widens them in others, which is a conversation worth having with the school's counsellor rather than with a tutor. What we can do is give an honest read on whether the current IGCSE work would support three subjects at that depth.

This is where IB and IGCSE coaching for Aditya Birla World Academy students in Mumbai stops being about content. A tutor supporting a decision rather than a subject does three concrete things: runs a genuine Higher Level problem set with the student and reports what happened, maps the current Extended grades against the realistic prerequisites for each shortlisted Higher Level subject, and gives a blunt opinion on project stamina based on how the last piece of IGCSE coursework actually got written. On IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai, this kind of work usually runs at the same rate as subject teaching; what changes the rate is board, level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long the session runs.

sections.heading: What should progress look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see changed working habits, not changed marks. The specific things to look for: your child attempts a question before looking at the worked example, writes method lines instead of a bare answer, and can tell you what the question was testing rather than only whether she got it right. If a tutor claims a grade movement after four weeks, they are either describing noise in a single test or telling you what you want to hear. We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor will.

At one term, roughly three months and a mock series, you should see a measurable shift on one specific thing. Not an overall grade; one paper, one component, one skill. A student who was losing marks on extended-response questions in Biology 0610 because she listed points instead of linking them should, by the end of a term, be linking them. That is the unit of progress that is real. Broad statements about confidence are pleasant and almost impossible to check.

At one exam cycle, the honest picture is more complicated. Students who start in August with a clear diagnostic and keep a weekly slot tend to move. Students who start in January are usually working on damage limitation and both the tutor and the family should name that out loud rather than discovering it in May. Some students do not move much, and the reasons are usually not tutoring reasons: sleep, a subject chosen for the wrong motive, or a workload that was never survivable. A good tutor will tell you which of those they think they are looking at.

The limits are worth stating plainly because they set the terms of the relationship. A tutor cannot make a student do an Extended Essay that the student has decided not to care about. A tutor cannot change a school's Internal Assessment deadline. A tutor has no access to grade boundaries, moderation outcomes, or anything the school has not published. What a tutor can do is make sure that the hours a student does put in are spent on the right thing, which over two Diploma years is a considerable amount of leverage.

sections.heading: Booking the first home tuition session in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Five things make the first session useful instead of introductory. The most recent school report, with the comments and not only the grades. The current subject list, marked up with Core or Extended at IGCSE and Higher Level or Standard Level in the Diploma. The school's published assessment calendar for this term. A photograph of one recent marked piece of work, ideally one the child did badly on, because the marker's comments say more in two minutes than a parent can say in twenty. And the child's own list of what feels hard, written by the child, unedited.

The first session itself is a diagnostic and should be sold to you as one. The tutor works through questions at and slightly above the current level, watches where the method breaks rather than where the answer is wrong, and finishes with a short written read on what they think is actually going on. You should get that read within a day or two. If it says nothing more specific than 'needs to practise more', ask for a better one or ask us for a different tutor.

On practicalities: sessions run at your address, at a table rather than on a bed, with the phone in another room and a parent somewhere in the flat but not in the room. Most families in Tardeo and Cumballa Hill book a weekday evening slot and one weekend morning. A tutor coming by train will arrive from Mumbai Central or Grant Road; one driving in will give you a realistic arrival window rather than an optimistic one, and should tell you in advance which evenings they cannot do.

If something is not working, say so early. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai does not exist, so a mismatch on one subject is not a verdict on the platform; it is information we can act on in a few days. We keep the brief, the diagnostic and the history, so a replacement starts from where the last tutor stopped rather than from the beginning, and you are not asked to explain your child's situation a second time.

Mark the subject list with Core or Extended and Higher Level or Standard Level

faqs.question: When does a Year 11 student have to decide between the IB Diploma and A Levels?
faqs.answer: Practically, by the winter of Year 11, because schools offering A Levels in Mumbai run admissions well before the IGCSE results arrive. That means the decision gets made on predicted grades and on the student's own sense of whether six subjects or three suits them. Useful inputs are the Extended Mathematics trajectory, how the last piece of coursework actually got written, and whether the child reads around any subject without being asked. A tutor can give you an honest read on the first two. The school counsellor is the right person for university-pathway implications.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take a student through IGCSE and then into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not assume it. An IB and IGCSE home teacher for Aditya Birla World Academy students in Mumbai who has genuinely taught both boards in the same subject is valuable at exactly this transition, because they can see what the IGCSE habits will cost at Higher Level. What matters is component experience, not a claim of familiarity. Ask whether they have supervised or marked an Internal Assessment in that subject. If the answer is no, continuity is still useful for the first Diploma term and a specialist should take over after that.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor travel to our building off Peddar Road for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most of the tutors matched to this school already work in that radius. What you should settle before the first session is the arrival window and the building's entry process. Many South Mumbai buildings need a resident to authorise a regular visitor at the gate rather than clearing one each week, and sorting that once saves ten minutes every session. Tell us your preferred start time when you enquire, because a six o'clock start and a seven o'clock start draw on quite different pools of tutors once travel is accounted for.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote a figure here because any number would be misleading without them. Board and level come first: Higher Level Diploma teaching costs more than IGCSE teaching. Subject scarcity is next, and it moves rates more than anything else; Higher Level Physics and Economics are harder to staff than IGCSE English. Then travel distance, because a tutor crossing the city is pricing an hour of road. Then session length and frequency, where a longer standing weekly slot is usually better value than ad hoc hours. Finally the mode, since online sessions carry no travel.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: For Internal Assessment work, online is often better than in person. The work is a document, the feedback is annotation, and a shared screen with the criteria open next to the draft is the right tool for that job. Where online is weaker is the diagnostic phase and the student who is quietly disengaged, because a screen hides body language and a face-down phone. Our usual recommendation is in person while the tutor is still working out what is going on, then online for the drafting months, which happen to be the same months when traffic is worst.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the diagnostic read in writing and compare it with what you are seeing at the table. One month is four or five sessions, which is too early for grade movement but not too early for changed working habits. If your child is still writing bare answers with no method, still skipping the attempt before the worked example, and still cannot say what a question was testing, that is a genuine flag. Raise it with the tutor first, because the fix is often a wrong starting point rather than a wrong person. If nothing shifts in two more weeks, ask us for a replacement.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, usually within a few days. We do not ask you to justify the decision or to have a difficult conversation with the tutor yourself; that part is ours. The brief, the first-session diagnostic and any notes stay with us, so the replacement starts with the history rather than with a blank page, and you are not asked to explain your child's situation again. We would rather make a second match early than defend a first one. A mismatch on personality is common and is nobody's failure.

faqs.question: Do we need a parent at home during the session, and what study space works best?
faqs.answer: A parent should be in the flat but not in the room. Fifteen-year-olds perform for an audience and stop asking the questions that reveal what they do not understand. For space, a table with two chairs side by side rather than across from each other, good light, the phone in another room, and the textbook plus a past paper within reach. A bedroom desk works if the bed is not in the sightline. The one arrangement that consistently fails is a sofa with a laptop, because nobody writes method on a sofa.

faqs.question: How can a tutor help with a pathway decision rather than just a subject?
faqs.answer: By generating evidence instead of opinions. A tutor can run a genuine Higher Level problem set with your child and tell you how it went, map current Extended grades against what each shortlisted Higher Level subject realistically needs, and give you a straight read on project stamina based on how the last coursework piece was actually produced rather than how it was submitted. That is three pieces of concrete information to take into the conversation with the school. The choice of school and programme stays with you and the school; a tutor's job is to make it an informed one.

faqs.question: Evening traffic between Mahalaxmi and Peddar Road makes a six o'clock start risky. How is that handled?
faqs.answer: By matching from inside the radius and by agreeing a realistic window rather than a fixed minute. Tutors living or already teaching in Tardeo, Cumballa Hill, Altamount Road or Mahalaxmi are offered these slots first, precisely because the last two kilometres are the unpredictable part. We also ask tutors what else they teach that evening, since a session ending at half past five somewhere in the Western Suburbs is not compatible with a six o'clock start here. When a week looks impossible, the session moves online rather than being cancelled.

sections.heading: IB Diploma, Middle Years Programme and IGCSE: what transfers when a student moves mid-pathway
paragraphs: The American School of Bombay publicly offers the IB Diploma Programme at its BKC campus, so a student arriving in the eleventh year is joining a two-year course that is already running. What transfers from a previous school is content. What rarely transfers is assessment literacy. A student who finished an honours Chemistry course in a United States high school may know stoichiometry well and have never once been marked against a criterion descriptor. Those are separate gaps, they fail in separate ways, and they need separate work.

Arrivals come from three broad pre-Diploma routes. Students from the Middle Years Programme (MYP) arrive used to criterion-referenced marking, inquiry questions and the personal project, so the vocabulary of Diploma assessment is familiar even where content is thin. Students from Cambridge International Education's IGCSE arrive with strong examination technique, a habit of past-paper practice and clean notation, but often no experience of extended independent writing. Students from an American middle and high school arrive with the widest content spread and the strongest classroom discussion habits, and the least exposure to externally moderated coursework of any of the three.

The Diploma core is where the gap is widest and least visible. Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the creativity, activity and service strand have no close equivalent in most American curricula, and a student who joins late can be an entire term behind on the Extended Essay supervision cycle while looking perfectly settled in lessons. Families moving the other way, out of the Diploma and into an IGCSE school in Mumbai at Years 9 to 11, meet the mirror problem: choosing between the Core and Extended tiers in Mathematics and the sciences, where the Core tier caps the top grade available and the decision is awkward to reverse later.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Higher Level and Standard Level, and the internal assessment behind each one
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes six subjects across the subject groups, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), alongside TOK, the Extended Essay and the service strand. Every one of those six carries an Internal Assessment (IA): a piece of work marked by the teacher and moderated externally. For a student who joined in October, the IA calendar is the real pressure, because those deadlines were set before they arrived and do not move for them. Some families want one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai; in practice one person covers a cluster, not all six.

The internal assessments do not resemble each other. In the sciences the IA is a scientific investigation assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, which means the question has to be narrow enough to produce usable data in a school laboratory. In Mathematics it is an exploration, marked partly on personal engagement and reflection, which is where capable mathematicians with nothing to say lose marks. In History it is an investigation with a source-evaluation section and a reflection on method. In Language A it is an individual oral built on a global issue and two extracts. A tutor who has supervised the specific one your child is sitting is worth considerably more than a strong generalist.

Subject choice is often still open for a late arrival, and it deserves one honest conversation before the term hardens. Moving a subject from Higher Level to Standard Level in week six is a legitimate decision when the content gap is structural rather than a matter of effort, and it beats discovering the same problem in February with an IA half-written. A family asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects needs tutor cover in Mumbai that stretches across both boards at once: one request that spans all IB and IGCSE subjects from IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor cover in Mumbai up to Diploma Higher Level, usually because an older and a younger child sit at different stages in the same flat.

paragraphs: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to the American School of Bombay in any way. Tutors are placed for families whose children attend it, the school's published calendar is read here exactly as any parent reads it, and there is no access to its staff, its internal materials or its assessment schedule. Anything specific about a deadline should come from your child's homeroom teacher or the parent portal rather than from a tutoring platform, and a tutor who claims inside knowledge of a school is telling you something about themselves.

What can be described is the rhythm of the Diploma year as the International Baccalaureate sets it for the May examination session, which is the session most Mumbai international schools sit. The first Diploma year runs fairly quietly until around March, when internal assessment drafts begin landing. The second year is front-loaded: between November and February most schools collect science and mathematics IA drafts, run mock examinations and push the Extended Essay towards final submission, while the TOK essay moves through its prescribed-title cycle in the same window. March and April are consolidation and study leave, examinations run through May, and results arrive in July.

BKC holds other IB schools, including Dhirubhai Ambani International School and Ascend International School, and families comparing options often end up with children at more than one of them. That matters practically rather than competitively: two schools inside the same complex can run the same programme on different internal deadlines, so a tutor working with siblings plans two calendars instead of one. The useful move for any newly arrived family is to ask the school for its own assessment calendar inside the first fortnight, mark the weeks where an IA draft, a mock and a TOK deadline overlap, and concentrate tutoring intensity around those weeks instead of spreading it evenly across the year.

sections.heading: Is home tuition or online better for a Mumbai family that may relocate again?
paragraphs: Home tuition first, with the online option built in from the start if another move is possible. A tutor in the room reads a teenager better than a screen does, and that matters most in the weeks straight after a relocation, when a student will often not say what they do not understand. A family posted here on a two or three year assignment should still set the arrangement up so it survives a departure, which means the same tutor is already comfortable on a shared whiteboard long before anyone needs them to be.

Online genuinely works for some things and genuinely does not for others. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai can run Economics, Business Management, History, English and most of Mathematics well, because the material is text, graphs and worked solutions that a tablet handles properly. Scientific investigation planning, Visual Arts and any subject where a student needs to be watched while they work are weaker online. Higher Level Mathematics with a struggling student is the hardest case of all, because the tutor cannot see the page at the moment the error happens. Hybrid resolves most of it: one home session a week for the difficult teaching and one online session for review and homework checking.

For a family that may move again, the practical arrangement is to keep an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai in the home slot while the student is here, then convert that same person to online for the final stretch of the Diploma rather than changing tutors mid-course. A student who moves country in the second Diploma year keeps continuity through the IA and Extended Essay deadlines, which is the part of the course where a handover costs the most. Time zones are the only real constraint, and a tutor here can usually hold an early morning or a late evening slot for a family that has moved west.

sections.heading: How is a home tutor in Mumbai checked before the first session?
paragraphs: Every tutor is identity-checked, their qualifications are seen rather than taken on trust, and they are asked for specific evidence of teaching the exact course and not merely the subject. For an IB and IGCSE tutor for American School of Bombay students in Mumbai, that means naming the syllabus version they last taught and when, describing how a particular IA criterion is applied in practice, and talking through a real student they took from a weak draft to a submitted one. References from previous families are requested wherever a tutor has them.

Do your own checking as well, because you can test things a platform cannot. Ask the tutor to mark one paragraph of your child's existing work against the published criterion and explain the mark out loud. Ask which command terms the subject uses and what separates describe from explain, and explain from evaluate. Ask what they would do in the first four weeks, and listen for whether you are hearing a plan or a script. Parents searching IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai mostly end up comparing profiles, and profiles all read the same; a fifteen-minute conversation separates them properly.

Access is part of verification in Mumbai. BKC towers and Bandra East societies run visitor registers, several want a photograph and an identity document at the gate, and a standing weekly entry is far smoother than a fresh approval every Tuesday evening. Arrange that standing pass in the first week rather than the fourth. Sessions should happen in a shared space with the door open, with an adult or trusted house staff at home, and a parent in earshot for the first few. That is ordinary practice rather than suspicion, and any tutor worth booking will expect it and say so first.

sections.heading: Closing a mid-pathway gap: a worked example of a Diploma arrival from an American curriculum
paragraphs: Take a student who joins the first Diploma year in BKC in the last week of October, arriving from a United States high school where she finished an honours Chemistry course and a second year of algebra. She is taking Chemistry at Higher Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, English, Economics, Spanish and Environmental Systems. Her previous reports look fine, which is exactly why nobody at school is worried yet. The first diagnostic session runs two hours and splits into three parts: a content audit against what the class has already covered, an assessment-literacy audit, and a command-term audit. None of it is teaching. All of it is finding out what is actually missing.

The content audit finds that stoichiometry and the mole concept are solid, bonding is patchy, and atomic structure with ionisation energy trends was never covered to the depth Higher Level expects, which matters because energetics later leans on it. The assessment-literacy audit finds she has written laboratory reports with a results and discussion structure, but has never justified a methodology, quantified uncertainty, or been marked on evaluation as a criterion in its own right. The command-term audit finds she treats describe and explain as synonyms, which quietly costs marks in every paper she sits. In Mathematics, functions are strong, radian measure and the ambiguous case of the sine rule are absent, and differentiation has not begun.

The plan that follows is ordered by dependency rather than by chronology. Two home tuition sessions a week: a weekday evening that keeps pace with the class so the gap stops widening, and a Saturday morning that backfills in dependency order, atomic structure before bonding before energetics. The assessment-literacy work is folded into the class-pace session rather than taught as a separate topic, by marking her real homework against the real criteria each week. Week four is a review point with a written note on what closed and what did not. By the February IA draft she is not ahead of her classmates, but she is writing to the same criteria they are, which is the honest target. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and any tutor who does should be questioned closely.
bullets: Diagnose first: content, assessment literacy and command terms, in that order
Backfill in dependency order, not in the order the syllabus prints topics

sections.heading: What should progress look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see changes in process, not changes in grades. The student starts homework without a twenty-minute stall, can say which topic a question belongs to, and brings specific questions to the session instead of handing over a blank page. The written gap list from the diagnostic should have items crossed off it. If none of that has happened inside four weeks, either the match is wrong or the diagnosis was wrong. Both are fixable, but only if somebody says so out loud instead of waiting politely for the next report.

At one term, the measure is a piece of real work: an IA draft submitted on time and marked usefully by the teacher, a mock paper the student finished rather than ran out of time on, a command-term error rate that has visibly dropped. At one examination cycle, you are looking at predicted grades and at whether the student's own estimate of their work has become accurate, which is a better long-term signal than any single result. Grades are not guaranteed by anyone in this business, and a tutor who offers a specific number at the outset should be treated with caution.

When a tutor is not working out, say it in week two rather than week eight. The usual failures are easy to name: the tutor is teaching rather than diagnosing, the student is polite but silent, or the personality fit is wrong in a way no amount of subject expertise repairs. Tell IB Gram what is happening and a replacement is proposed with the handover written down, including the original gap list and what was genuinely covered, so the next person does not start from zero. Changing tutors once is normal, particularly after a relocation. Changing three times in a term usually means the brief itself needs rewriting.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four things make a first home tuition session useful. The subject list with levels, Higher or Standard, written out properly. The last report or progress sheet from the previous school, plus anything the current school has issued since. The class timetable, so the tutor knows when each subject is actually taught and can place the session where it helps. And any IA task sheet or assignment brief the student has already been given, because that single document tells a tutor more than an hour of conversation about the course ever will.

The first session is a diagnostic and should be booked as one. Expect the tutor to ask the student to attempt work rather than to sit and listen, to interrupt and ask how they got there, and to leave notes a parent can read afterwards. Expect them to ask in detail what the student did at the previous school, because that is where the transferable strength is hiding and nobody has asked about it since the move. A good diagnostic ends with three things: what to fix first, what can safely wait, and what the student should do before the next session.

Transition work is front-loaded, so expect a heavier first term, and state your budget at the start so the shortlist matches it rather than disappointing you later.

faqs.question: My child joins the first Diploma year in November. Is it too late to catch up?

faqs.question: We may be posted to another country next year. Does the tutoring have to stop?
faqs.answer: No, provided you set it up for that possibility from the beginning. Ask for a tutor who already teaches online comfortably, run at least one session a month on a shared whiteboard while you are still here, and a move becomes a change of format rather than a change of person. faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: For most of them, yes, with clear exceptions. Economics, Business Management, History, English and the written side of Mathematics work well online, because the material is text, diagrams and worked solutions that a tablet and a shared screen handle properly. Scientific investigation planning, Visual Arts and any situation where a student needs watching while they work are weaker. The hardest case is Higher Level Mathematics with a struggling student, where the tutor needs to see the page as the error appears. Hybrid is usually the honest answer: one home session each week and one online.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week two rather than week eight, and a replacement is proposed. A replacement comes with a written handover, the original gap list and a record of what was actually covered, so the new tutor does not spend two sessions rediscovering it. One change in a term is normal, particularly after a relocation. Three changes usually means the brief we were given needs rewriting, and we will say so plainly.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Go back to the written gap list from the diagnostic and check it item by item, because progress at four weeks shows up there well before it shows up in grades. If nothing on that list has closed, the problem is one of three: the diagnosis missed the real gap, the session is being spent on homework rather than teaching, or nothing is happening between sessions. Each has a different fix and none of them is simply more hours. Ask the tutor for a written answer to what changed this month, and judge the quality of that answer.

faqs.question: Who should be at home during a session, and where in the flat should it happen?
faqs.answer: An adult or trusted house staff should be at home, and the session should happen in a shared space, a dining table or a study with the door open, rather than a bedroom. For the first few sessions a parent within earshot is sensible, not because anything is expected to go wrong but because you learn a great deal about the teaching from twenty minutes of overhearing. Keep the space clear of a television and a younger sibling. A teenager who has just changed countries concentrates less than you would expect, and the room matters more than usual during that first term.

faqs.question: How do I judge the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai when every profile reads the same?
faqs.answer: Ignore the profile and run a fifteen-minute conversation with three questions. Ask which syllabus version they last taught and in which year. Ask them to mark one paragraph of your child's real work against the published criterion and explain the mark out loud. Ask what they would do in the first four weeks, and listen for whether you are hearing a diagnostic plan or a rehearsed script. Profiles are written to look alike on every platform; those three answers never do. Credentials matter, but the ability to explain a mark to a parent predicts a useful term better.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover a younger sibling doing IGCSE as well?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is worth asking, because one tutor travelling to your building for two consecutive sessions is easier to schedule and cheaper per hour than two separate visits. The practical limit is subject range: one person can usually handle IGCSE Mathematics and Diploma Mathematics, or IGCSE and Diploma sciences in the same discipline, but not Higher Level Chemistry and IGCSE English. paragraphs: B.D. Somani International School sits in Cuffe Parade, South Mumbai, and publicly offers an IGCSE pathway and an International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) pathway. That is the whole of what this page says about the school, and it is all a tutoring platform has any business saying. A school that runs Cambridge IGCSE into the Diploma Programme rather than the Middle Years Programme (MYP) into DP asks something specific of its students at one specific moment. IGCSE rewards a clean, correct answer produced alone against a clock. The Diploma Programme rewards a documented process: an Internal Assessment (IA) in almost every subject, an Extended Essay (EE), and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). A student who was comfortable at IGCSE because she was quick and accurate can stall badly in DP1, not because the content got harder but because nobody is grading speed any more. The skill being assessed changed and nobody announced it.

In the Diploma Programme a student takes six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus TOK, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. HL is not SL with extra homework. It adds additional higher level content, longer papers and in several subjects an extra option, and the jump in workload is concentrated in DP2 rather than spread evenly. The choice gets made at the end of Year 11, usually in the same weeks the IGCSE revision is at its worst, which is the least clear-headed fortnight of the two-year run.

At IGCSE the equivalent fork is Core versus Extended. In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 with grades C to G available, while Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 with grades A* to E available. Moving a child down to Core to protect against a weak result can also quietly remove the grade a Diploma Programme Mathematics course expects two years later. Schools across Mumbai run Cambridge International Education syllabuses and, less often, Pearson Edexcel ones, and the tier names differ between them, so the first thing a tutor should ask for is the syllabus code printed on the front of the paper. IB Gram covers all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 level with tutors in Mumbai who teach that exact code.
