sections.heading: Reading a criterion-marked report before you book a subject tutor
paragraphs: Take a Year 9 Science report that shows solid marks for knowledge and understanding and weak marks for the criterion covering inquiry and design. A parent reads that as a Science problem. It is usually a method problem that will reappear in Individuals and Societies, in Design, and later in every Diploma Programme Internal Assessment the child ever writes. Hiring a Science tutor fixes the symptom in one subject. Hiring someone who can teach investigation design, using Science as the vehicle, fixes four subjects and the IA years as well.

The reverse case matters just as much. A report with strong criteria across the board and a sinking examination percentage is not a content problem at all. That student knows the material and is losing it in the hall, which means timing, question selection and the discipline of answering what was asked. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai is asked to teach, these two patterns account for most bookings, and they need opposite people: one patient and conceptual, one fast and ruthless about papers.

Mathematics is the one subject where the diagnosis is almost always the same, whatever the report says. Something from two or three years ago did not set, the curriculum moved on, and every new topic now sits on sand. Indices, negative numbers, manipulating fractions in algebra, or the leap from arithmetic to symbols. A good tutor spends the first fortnight finding the layer that failed rather than drilling this week's chapter, which looks like going backwards and is the only thing that works. Expect a tutor to tell you which layer it was, by name, after two sessions.

sections.heading: The reporting rhythm Mumbai families plan tutoring around
paragraphs: International schools in Mumbai work on a year that starts around June and finishes in April or May, and the rhythm inside it is a sequence of reporting points rather than one examination at the end. For a family, that is useful, because each reporting point is a free measurement. The mistake is to treat each one as a verdict and react to it. A dip in one cycle, in one criterion, in one subject, is information. Three cycles pointing the same way is a pattern, and only the pattern is worth hiring against.

Build the tutoring year around the two weeks before each reporting cycle and the three weeks after it. Before, the work is consolidation and practice under time pressure. After, with the feedback actually in hand, the work is the specific thing the teacher wrote down, which is the cheapest and most accurate brief any tutor will ever get. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai international schools offer should be asking you for the reporting dates in the first week and should be visibly changing the plan when a report arrives.

IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with Green Acres Academy or any other school mentioned here, and we cannot guarantee grades. We also do not contact schools, ask them for records or present a tutor as acting for you in any capacity. The practical consequence is that everything our tutors know about your school's calendar, assessment schedule and reporting format comes from you. So bring the dates. A tutor who has the school calendar pinned above the desk will be useful in February; a tutor who finds out about a mock the week it happens will not.

sections.heading: Why home tuition leads, and when online is the better call in Mumbai
paragraphs: An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Green Acres Academy students in Mumbai works at your table for a simple reason: everything the tutor needs is in the room. The returned assessment with the teacher's marks on it. The exercise book that goes neat for eight pages and then collapses. The folder with last term's topic test in it that nobody has opened. A tutor who can reach over and pull the evidence off the shelf diagnoses in one session what takes three sessions to establish by asking questions over a video call. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai is also the only format where you can hear, from the next room, who is doing the thinking.

There are two situations where insisting on home visits costs your child the better teacher. The first is a narrow subject at Higher Level, where an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai teaching that exact combination might be in Navi Mumbai or Thane and the alternative within driving distance is somebody teaching it for the first time. The second is a crowded fortnight, when a short screen session at nine in the evening is possible and an hour of road is not. Both are real reasons. Neither is an argument for making the whole arrangement remote.

The honest trade-offs run in both directions. Online sessions tend to shorten before concentration fails, written work is harder to supervise as it happens, and the format quietly encourages a tutor to check homework rather than teach. Home sessions cost travel, which costs money, and they depend on a household that can keep an hour quiet. A mixed arrangement handles both, provided the split is agreed in writing at the start: which day is at home, what triggers a switch to online, how a cancelled session is made up and who keeps the shared file of worked papers.

sections.heading: What is checked before you meet anyone, and what is not
paragraphs: Identity, qualification and subject claim, in that order, and all three before a profile reaches you. Identity is matched to a government document. Qualifications are verified rather than accepted from a summary the tutor wrote. The subject claim is tested at the level stated, because teaching Chemistry and teaching Chemistry at Higher Level against the current syllabus are not the same job, and the gap between them is where most applicants are turned away. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families find through a building group or a school chat may be outstanding and has had none of this done.

What is not checked is the thing you most want to know, and it is worth being clear about that rather than pretending otherwise. Nobody can verify in advance whether a particular adult will get on with your particular fourteen-year-old. We can confirm somebody knows the syllabus. We cannot confirm they will be patient at 8pm with a child who has decided the subject is pointless. That is why the first session happens before any commitment and why asking for a different shortlist carries no cost or explanation.

Two checks are yours. In the first session, listen for the ratio of talking: a tutor who holds the floor for fifty minutes has given a lecture your child will forget by Friday. Then ask what gets set this fortnight and how you will know in four weeks whether it worked. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, or who claims special knowledge of how a particular Mumbai school marks. No tutor on this platform has any standing with any school, and one who implies otherwise should be reported to us and replaced.

sections.heading: When should you not hire a tutor at all?
paragraphs: More often than a tutoring platform is supposed to admit. If the report shows one dip in one subject in one cycle, wait for the next cycle. If your child is in the first eight weeks of a new programme, the drop is usually the transition and not the child. If the difficulty appeared the same month as a house move, a new sibling, a bereavement or a phone, the subject is the symptom. And if a child is already doing three co-curricular activities and arriving home at 7pm, adding a weekly hour subtracts from sleep, which costs more marks than any tutor adds.

There is also the over-tutored case, which is common in Mumbai and rarely named. A student with four tutors, each setting work, has no unsupervised practice time left, and unsupervised practice is where learning consolidates. Those students often present as hardworking and stuck: they can follow any explanation and cannot start a question alone. The fix is subtraction. Drop two tutors, keep the two subjects that genuinely need teaching, and give the hours back. There is no best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai for a child whose real problem is that nobody has left them alone with a past paper.

When tutoring is the right call, the sensible version is smaller than parents expect. One subject, one hour a week, for one term, reviewed honestly at the end of it. That is cheaper, easier to judge and easier to stop. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai move with the board, the level, how scarce that specialist is, how far they travel to you and how long the session runs, so a single well-chosen subject with a local tutor is a fraction of the cost of a full timetable with somebody crossing the city. Ask for a rate against a defined format and compare two tutors on the same brief rather than asking for a general price.

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one exam series: is this actually working?
paragraphs: At four weeks the only fair test is behavioural. Does your child start homework in that subject without a fight, do they attempt the questions they used to skip, and can they explain one thing to you that they could not explain last month. If the answer to all three is no, the arrangement is wrong and waiting politely until the end of term wastes both the money and the term. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who is working will usually produce a visible change in willingness before any change in marks.

At one term, look at the shape of the improvement rather than its size. Recent topics should be clearly stronger than older ones, which tells you the teaching lands and the backlog is simply still a backlog. Mechanical questions improve before explanation questions, and explanation questions improve before the long extended response, which can take a term and a half on its own. A Year 10 student in Mulund who now scores well on every calculation and still writes a thin six-mark answer is exactly where a term should put them.

Across one examination series, ask one question: did the gap between the mock and the real paper go the right way, and did your child know what to do with an unfamiliar question. That is the whole measurable benefit of tutoring and it is worth having. All IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes Mumbai families run share the same ceiling. The tutor does not sit the paper, does not write the mark scheme and cannot rebuild three years in six weeks, and anybody suggesting otherwise in February is selling the month rather than the result.

sections.heading: Setting up home classes that survive a Mumbai term
paragraphs: Send three things and skip a fortnight of setup. The latest report with the subject comments intact, the school's calendar for the term, and one line about what you want to be different by the end of it, stated as something you would be able to see rather than a number on a page. Families who send all three usually get a shortlist the same working day, because the hard part of matching is not finding tutors, it is knowing which constraint matters most.

The first session runs on your child's own work. The marked assessment, the exercise book, the topic that has been avoided since October. No invented diagnostic test, no study-skills presentation, no hour spent establishing rapport that could have been established while doing something useful. You should get a short written note afterwards naming what was covered, where the understanding stops and what the next four sessions will target. Ask for that note before session two if it does not arrive by itself.

Then protect the hour and leave it alone for a term. A fixed weekly slot lets a tutor plan around the Eastern Express Highway at 6pm and lets your child plan homework around the session, and the families who move the time every week are the ones who end up with a tutor who arrives unprepared. If it is not working in week three, say so in week three. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai parents book can be restarted with a different tutor in a few days, and nobody needs an explanation beyond the fact that it was not a fit.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach a building in Chembur on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Chembur is one of the easier parts of the city for it. Tutors living in Chembur, Govandi, Wadala or Mulund can hold a 6.30pm or 7.30pm slot through a full term, because the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway, the Eastern Freeway and the Monorail all serve the same stretch. A tutor coming from Andheri or Borivali across the Santacruz–Chembur Link Road at the same hour is a different proposition. Tell us the hour you want before you pick a tutor, not afterwards.

faqs.question: My child's criterion marks look fine. Does that still need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and this is one of the most common unnecessary bookings. Solid criterion marks with a comfortable report usually mean the teaching is landing and the student is keeping up. The exception is a student whose criterion marks are fine and whose examination performance is visibly worse, which is a timing and format issue rather than a knowledge one and can often be fixed in a handful of sessions on past papers. Wait for a second reporting cycle, read whether the same comment appears twice, and book against a pattern instead of a mood.

faqs.question: How does parking and the society gate pass work for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once with your society office and the problem disappears for the term. Most Mumbai complexes will issue a standing entry for a named visitor on a fixed day and time, which removes the ten-minute wait at the gate that otherwise eats a session every week. Give the office the tutor's name, phone number and the slot. Parking is worth checking separately, because some societies allow visitor parking and others do not, and a tutor who has to park outside and walk in needs that factored into the start time.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five factors, and no honest figure exists without them. The board and the level, because an IGCSE Core subject, the same subject at Extended and a Higher Level Diploma Programme subject are three different jobs. The scarcity of the specialist, which is the factor families underestimate most. The travel distance, since a tutor crossing the city at 6pm is spending two hours to teach one. And the session length. Ask for a rate against a defined format, then compare two tutors on the same brief rather than on a general price.

faqs.question: We move from the MYP into IGCSE next year. When should tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Start in the term before the switch, not after the first bad result. The hard part of that transition is learning to write for a mark scheme instead of a criterion, and it is far easier to teach calmly in advance than in January with mocks running. Two things are worth doing early: a few sessions comparing the same answer marked both ways, and an honest look at whether Core or Extended entries suit each subject. Confirm the subject options and entry decisions with your school's coordinator, because only the school can tell you what it offers.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Personal Project or an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits, and the limits matter more than the help. A tutor can teach research method, help a student narrow a question that is far too broad, explain what the assessment criteria are actually asking for and read a draft for structure. A tutor cannot write any part of it, supply content to be copied or edit the text into their own prose, and any tutor willing to do that is putting your child's academic honesty record at risk. Ask the tutor to state where their line is before the first session on it.

faqs.question: Our child refuses the whole idea of a tutor. What then?
faqs.answer: Treat the refusal as information rather than an obstacle. A child who refuses usually fears either being exposed as behind or losing their last free evening, and each has a different answer. For the first, a tutor who opens by asking the child what they find hardest, rather than testing them, changes the mood in one session. For the second, negotiate the hour with the child instead of announcing it. It also helps to agree a fixed review date four weeks out, so the arrangement feels finite rather than permanent.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week are too many?
faqs.answer: Two hours a week in one subject is usually the ceiling before returns fall, and three subjects tutored at once is usually too many for anybody under sixteen. The reason is practice time. Learning consolidates when a student works alone and gets stuck and recovers, and a timetable packed with tutors removes exactly those hours. If you feel you need three or four tutors, the honest reading is often that the school fit or the subject choices need looking at rather than that more teaching is required. Start with one and add only against evidence.

faqs.question: What happens at the end of a term if we want to stop?
faqs.answer: You stop, and nothing is required beyond telling the tutor and telling us. There is no notice requirement built into the matching, no term commitment and no penalty for ending an arrangement that has done its job. Many families use a tutor for one term, fix the specific gap and never come back, which is the outcome we would rather have than a standing arrangement nobody reviews. If you want a written summary of what was covered to hand to a future tutor, ask for it before the last session.

faqs.question: Does online work from Navi Mumbai or Thane for a scarce subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a scarce subject it is often the only sensible option. A specialist in a narrow Higher Level subject may live in Nerul, Kharghar or on Ghodbunder Road while you are in Chembur, and asking that person to drive in twice a week will either be refused or will not last the term. A video session with a shared document, where both people can write on the same page, loses very little for review and paper work. Keep foundation rebuilding at the table and use the screen for the specialist.

sections.heading: IGCSE Years 9 to 11 and the IB Diploma Programme are two different machines
paragraphs: Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai publicly offers both a Cambridge IGCSE pathway and an International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) pathway, which means a family here makes two separate structural decisions a few years apart. The first is Core or Extended in each IGCSE subject, settled late in Year 9 or during Year 10. The second is the Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) split at the start of the Diploma Programme. Neither decision is free to reverse once teaching groups are set.

The Core and Extended choice is the one parents underestimate. Core papers in a Cambridge International Education subject carry a lower grade ceiling than Extended papers, so a student placed in Core for comfort in Year 10 can find a subject closed to them at Higher Level two years later. The honest tutoring question is not which tier feels safer this term, but whether the student can be carried to Extended in the time left. That is answerable in about three weeks of real work.

The Diploma Programme is a different shape altogether: six subjects, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every one of those six subjects carries an Internal Assessment (IA), and the Higher Level ones carry more teaching hours and deeper content. A student taking three sciences at Higher Level has signed up for three long independent investigations in the same calendar year, and that is a workload problem before it is an academic one.

If your child is moving into IGCSE Year 9 from a Middle Years Programme (MYP) classroom somewhere else in Mumbai, expect the jump to be in written examination technique rather than content. MYP criteria reward process and reflection; Cambridge papers reward a precise answer to a precisely worded question. Several good students lose a full grade in their first Year 9 term purely because nobody told them the command word at the front of the question was doing most of the marking.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE and IB components are actually worth paying a tutor for?
paragraphs: The components worth tutoring are the ones with a long unsupervised tail: Extended Paper 4 in mathematics and the sciences at IGCSE, and every Internal Assessment at Diploma Programme level. A tutor adds least when delivering content the school has already taught, and most when marking a student's own work against the published criteria and making them redo it. Parents ask for all IB and IGCSE subjects with one home tutor in Mumbai and are almost always better served by two specialists who each own a component.

Here is the shape of a question that quietly costs marks every year. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics Extended Paper 4 presents two mathematically similar cones, gives the slant height of the smaller as six centimetres and the larger as nine, and asks for the surface area and then the volume of the larger solid. The student writes the linear ratio of three to two and applies it to both. The area needed the ratio squared and the volume needed it cubed, so the second half of the question is gone. The theory is one line from Year 9. The loss is several marks on a paper where that distance sits across a grade boundary, and no amount of extra content teaching fixes it. What fixes it is a tutor who hands back four similar-solids questions in a row until the cube reflex is automatic.

At Diploma Programme level the equivalent pressure point is the Internal Assessment. A Chemistry IA fails on the research question long before it fails on the chemistry: a student picks a question with no measurable independent variable, collects a term of data and cannot write an evaluation because there is nothing to evaluate. A tutor earns their fee in the first two sessions of that process, narrowing the question and forcing a pilot run, not in polishing the final draft the week before submission.

Languages and humanities need a different kind of help again. Economics Paper 1 rewards a definition, a diagram and an application in that order, and students who write beautiful general essays score badly. English Language and Literature guided analysis rewards close reading of one passage rather than everything the student knows about the writer. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is a sales line rather than a real person, and treating it as one is how families end up paying for hours that change nothing.

sections.heading: The Mumbai map that matters here is a road map, not a rail map
paragraphs: Powai sits in the Central Suburbs with Chandivali beside it, Ghatkopar and Kurla to the south and Mulund to the north, and it has no railway station of its own. That single fact decides your tutor pool. Every tutor arrives by road: from Andheri East along JVLR, from Kanjurmarg on the eastern side, or from Ghatkopar through Saki Vihar Road and Chandivali. Metro Line 1 between Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar gets a tutor close, then leaves the last stretch to an auto or a bike.

The Eastern Suburbs are the quietly reliable supply line. Kanjurmarg station is close enough that a tutor can be in Hiranandani Gardens shortly after stepping off a Central Line train, and tutors living in Vikhroli, Bhandup and Chembur run the Eastern Express Highway northwards against the worst of the flow. The Eastern Freeway puts Chembur and Wadala within reach of South Mumbai, which matters for tutors who teach in Worli or Colaba in the morning and come eastwards in the afternoon.

The Western Suburbs are a weekend proposition for a Powai family, and anyone who tells you otherwise has not done the drive. A tutor in Bandra, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon or Kandivali travels the Western Line, Metro Lines 2A and 7 or the Western Express Highway, all of which run north and south rather than east and west. They can hold a Saturday morning in Powai for a year. A Wednesday at half past four is a different request, and the honest answer in the Western Suburbs is usually no.

Everywhere else in Mumbai, Maharashtra is an online conversation for this school. South Mumbai tutors around Peddar Road, Worli and Cuffe Parade are boxed in by Metro Line 3, the Coastal Road and the Bandra Worli Sea Link, none of which point at Powai. Navi Mumbai tutors in Vashi, Nerul and Kharghar work Palm Beach Road and the Atal Setu, and Thane tutors stay on Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and the Central Line. A search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai will surface all of them; only a fraction can hold a weekday Powai slot.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for an IB and IGCSE student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition first, for a reason specific to this school. The child is already home. A student walking back into the township is at the dining table not long after the school day ends, so the early slot that barely exists anywhere else in the city is genuinely available here. IB and IGCSE home tuition for Hiranandani Foundation School students in Mumbai is therefore what we quote as the default, and the early weekday slot is the one worth fighting for.

The honest cost of home tuition is pool size. Families searching for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai are selecting from the tutors who can physically be in Powai at a fixed hour every week, which is a much smaller group than the tutors qualified to teach the subject. For a common request, Extended Mathematics or IGCSE Physics, that pool is comfortable. For a scarce one, Higher Level Economics or a less common second language, insisting on home visits can mean waiting weeks for a slot that never opens.

That is where IB and IGCSE online tutoring in Mumbai earns its place. Online removes the travel constraint entirely and puts a specialist from Thane, Navi Mumbai or South Mumbai in front of your child at an hour nobody could drive to. It works well for Internal Assessment drafting, past paper review and anything where both people need to look at the same document. It works less well for a Year 9 student who needs an adult in the room to notice that they stopped writing ten minutes ago.

Hybrid is what most families here settle into by the second term, and it is not a compromise. Keep the weekday early session at home with an IB and IGCSE private tutor anywhere in Mumbai who can reach Powai, and put the second weekly session online with the subject specialist. In the examination months, flipping both sessions online for a few weeks buys back the travel time on the tutor's side and makes short notice rescheduling possible when a mock gets moved.

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks before a tutor comes to your flat, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Verification here means four concrete things: government photo identification seen and recorded, an address that matches it, qualification documents checked against the subject they claim to teach, and a subject conversation with someone who has actually taught that board. References from previous tutoring families are called, not collected as written notes. A tutor who will not complete that set is not sent to a home, and that is the whole of what the badge means.

What verification cannot do is equally important to say plainly. IB Gram cannot verify anything about another organisation's internal workings, so a tutor's claims about any school, its teachers or its marking are outside what we check and outside what you should believe. We also do not verify a tutor's stories about grades previous students achieved, because nobody can. Ask the same hard questions of an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Hiranandani Foundation School students in Mumbai that you would ask of a stranger, however they were introduced.

Your own check runs in the first session and takes about fifteen minutes of attention. Can the tutor name the papers and components in your child's subject without being prompted. Do they mark your child's actual work in front of you rather than teaching from a printed worksheet. Do they leave written feedback behind. Can they explain, in a sentence a parent understands, why a particular mark was lost. A tutor who passes those four is almost always worth a term.

The red flags are consistent across the city and worth stating once. A tutor who promises a grade is either inexperienced or dishonest. A tutor who claims connections inside a school, access to its papers or knowledge of its predicted grades is making a claim that should end the conversation. So is a tutor who wants a long block of sessions paid for in advance before a single diagnostic session has happened.

sections.heading: Why does an early start work in Powai when Mumbai traffic says it should not?
paragraphs: Because only one of the two people has to travel. The child's commute is a walk across the township and takes minutes, so the student is home, changed and fed while most of Mumbai is still in a school bus. The tutor's commute is the entire journey, and Powai has no station, so it is a road journey every single time: Andheri East along JVLR, Kanjurmarg from the east, or Ghatkopar through Saki Vihar Road and Chandivali. Everything about which slots exist follows from that asymmetry.

In most of the city the early weekday slot is theoretical, because the student is still sitting in traffic at four o'clock. Here the student side of the equation costs nothing, and the entire constraint moves onto the tutor. A tutor leaving Andheri East before the JVLR build up can be at your door on time, finish, and still take a second student in the same cluster before the evening properly seizes. That is a workable afternoon. The same tutor starting from Bandra or Goregaon cannot build it at all.

So the scarce good on this page is the slot, not the subject. There are plenty of people in Mumbai who can teach IGCSE Chemistry. There are very few who can teach it in Powai at half past four on a Tuesday, and the ones who can are holding that slot because their whole week is arranged around this corridor. When they take a student across the city, the early slot is the first thing they lose. It does not come back when they want it to.

This is the practical argument for holding on to a tutor who already serves the area. If you pause an IB and IGCSE tutor for Hiranandani Foundation School students in Mumbai over the summer or through a long holiday, the slot gets filled, and when you return in October you are bidding for an evening instead. Keeping a reduced session through the thin months is usually cheaper than losing the afternoon and buying it back during examination season, when every family on this corridor wants the same hour.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, a term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking at marks, you are looking at behaviour. The student starts a past paper without being told to. They know what the command word at the front of the question is asking for. There is at least one paper in the file that has been marked, corrected and then attempted again. If a month has produced only completed homework and a pleasant atmosphere, the sessions are social rather than academic and you should say so out loud.

At one term you want a measurable change in one named component, not a general feeling of improvement. For an IGCSE student that usually shows in structured Paper 4 answers: the working is laid out, units appear, the last parts of long questions are attempted instead of abandoned. For a Diploma Programme student it shows in the Internal Assessment process: a research question that survives contact with a pilot run, data collected early enough to redo, and a draft that exists before the week it is due.

Across a full examination cycle, be careful what you attribute to tutoring. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor who has met your child a handful of times can tell you what they will score in May. Results move for a long list of reasons, including subject choice, attendance, illness and what the student does in the three hours nobody supervises. A tutor can reliably change the quality of the work in front of them; the final number sits outside anybody's control.

The honest limits are worth stating before you start. Tutoring does not fix a subject chosen at the wrong level, and the right advice in that case is a conversation with the school about moving tier or level rather than another weekly hour. It does not fix a student who will not write. It does not compensate for sessions skipped through October. If two of those three apply, more hours is the expensive answer to the wrong question.

faqs.answer: Usually two, occasionally three, almost never one. In practice one tutor takes mathematics and the sciences, a second takes a language or a humanity, and the rest of the subjects are left alone unless a specific paper is going wrong. Start with the two subjects where marks are actually being lost, run them for a term, and add a third only if the evidence says so.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for IB Diploma Programme Mathematics?
faqs.answer: For a DP student, yes, and often better than a home visit. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches work is largely worked solutions on a shared screen, which an annotated document handles well, and the graphic display calculator can be mirrored. It also opens up tutors from Thane, Navi Mumbai and South Mumbai who could never drive to Powai on a Tuesday. The weakness is attention: a DP1 student who drifts needs someone in the room. Most families here run one home session and one online session a week and treat the online one as the paper practice slot.

faqs.answer: Tell us in the fourth week and we arrange a replacement; it is a routine request and nobody takes offence. Say specifically what is wrong, because the fix differs: no written feedback is a different problem from a clash of temperament, and a tutor teaching content when the student needs examination technique is different again. Sometimes the right change is the brief rather than the person. If it is the person, the replacement starts from your existing notes so the new tutor is not rediscovering the same gaps in their first three sessions.

faqs.answer: Missed sessions are rescheduled, not forfeited, and June and July are the months this matters most in Mumbai. The practical answer is to agree a wet weather rule at the start: if the roads near JVLR or the Eastern Express Highway are flooded, the session converts to online at the same hour rather than being cancelled. That keeps the rhythm and protects the tutor's slot, which is the thing you cannot easily buy back. faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the move from IGCSE Year 11 into the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful work happens before the Diploma Programme starts rather than after. The two things that decide the next two years are the Higher Level and Standard Level split and whether the student has the independent writing habit the Internal Assessment demands. A few sessions in the gap between IGCSE examinations and DP1 are better spent stress testing the subject choice against what the student actually enjoys marking time in, and starting one piece of independent written work, than on getting ahead in content that will be taught anyway.

faqs.question: Is a six or seven in the evening slot workable for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: It is workable but it is the weakest hour of the week, and in Powai you have a better option. A DP2 student in November is carrying Internal Assessment deadlines in several subjects at once, and an evening session after a full school day produces slow, low quality drafting. sections.heading: IB Diploma Programme and IGCSE inside one large Juhu year group
paragraphs: Jamnabai Narsee International School sits in Juhu, in the western suburbs of Mumbai, and publicly offers both the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme and Cambridge IGCSE pathways. It is a large and long established school, and for a tutoring decision that size is the most useful public fact about it. A big year group is never a uniform one. The same IGCSE Physics set can hold a student who still cannot say what a resultant force is and a student who worked through the end-of-chapter problems by October and is bored.

One teacher standing in front of that room has to choose a pace. Whichever pace they choose is correct for the middle of the group and slightly wrong at both ends. This is not a complaint about any school; it is arithmetic, and it is true of every large cohort anywhere. It is also the reason two families whose children sit in the same class can both say the words needs a tutor and mean something close to opposite.

So every request gets sorted into one of two jobs before a name is suggested. Gap repair is backwards-facing work. Something from an earlier term or an earlier year never landed, and each new topic built on top of it is wobbling. The student is not slow; she is carrying a hole. Stretch is forwards-facing work. The content is understood and the basic questions are secure, and what is being lost is the last two or three marks on each question, the ones separating a 6 from a 7 at Diploma Programme level or a 7 from a 9 at IGCSE.

Those two jobs want different tutors. A repair tutor is patient, goes back further than the family expects, and will happily spend three sessions on indices before touching the current chapter. A stretch tutor is impatient in a useful way, works almost entirely from past papers and examiner comments, and spends the hour arguing with the student about why a technically correct answer was only worth four marks. Hiring the second person for the first job wastes a term, and hiring the first person for the second job bores a strong student into disengaging.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended across all IB and IGCSE subjects
paragraphs: The subject decisions in a two-board school land in a tight window and they are hard to reverse. At IGCSE the first real fork is Core versus Extended, most visibly in Mathematics and the sciences. Core caps the top grade available, which is fine for a student who will not take that subject further and painful for one who later decides on Higher Level (HL) Chemistry in the Diploma Programme. We plan all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 and find a tutor Mumbai parents can keep through the whole stretch, because the person who taught her Extended Maths in Grade 10 already knows exactly which algebra she avoids.

At Diploma Programme level the fork is HL versus Standard Level (SL) across the six subject groups. HL is not simply more of the same material delivered faster. It adds content, it adds a longer and harder paper, and in several subjects it adds question styles that never appear at SL, such as the extended evaluative responses in HL sciences and the additional option depth in HL Economics and HL History. Choosing three HLs that all carry heavy written coursework is a scheduling decision as much as an academic one.

Then there are the internal assessments, which are where strong students most often lose the marks they assumed were safe. Every Diploma Programme subject carries one: the sciences have the individual scientific investigation, Mathematics has the exploration, the humanities have their own investigation or commentary, and the languages have oral components recorded under conditions. On top of the six subjects sit the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and creativity, activity, service. At IGCSE the equivalent pressure is coursework and practical papers, depending on the option the school enters students for.

A tutor matched across all IB and IGCSE subjects with a tutor in Mumbai who has actually marked internal assessment drafts is worth more at this stage than one who only teaches content. Internal assessment marks are awarded against published criteria, and most lost marks are structural rather than scientific: a research question that is too broad to be answered in the word count, an evaluation section that lists limitations without weighing them, a mathematical exploration with no genuine personal engagement. Those are fixable in two sessions if someone names them early, and close to unfixable the week before submission.

paragraphs: Repeating what was said at the top, because it matters more on a page named after a school than anywhere else: IB Gram is independent and is not affiliated with Jamnabai Narsee International School, nor endorsed by it, nor connected to it. What we can talk about honestly is the shape of the year that any IB and IGCSE school in Mumbai works to, because the boards set it rather than the school. The academic year opens in June and the first eight weeks feel calm, which is exactly when repair work is cheapest and most effective. From late August the first formal assessments arrive and the picture clarifies. October and November bring Diwali break, which families treat as rest and which is in practice the single most productive block for a student carrying a gap, because there is no new content arriving on top of the old hole.

December through February is the compression. Diploma Programme internal assessment drafts come due across several subjects at once, the Extended Essay has its own checkpoints, Theory of Knowledge has an essay and an exhibition, and mock examinations land in the middle of all of it. A DP2 student sitting May examinations can easily have a science investigation draft, a TOK essay deadline and two mocks inside the same fortnight. For IGCSE students the same window holds mocks and coursework deadlines, with final papers from late April into June. March and April are revision months, and by then nobody is fixing a two-year gap; they are triaging.

Juhu and the roads immediately around it hold several schools running these boards, and parents routinely compare them before Grade 9. Ecole Mondiale World School is also in Juhu and runs IB programmes, and Utpal Shanghvi Global School offers IGCSE and IB Diploma Programme pathways. Naming them is useful for one practical reason only: tutors who work this belt tend to teach students from more than one of them, which means a tutor who has free slots near JVPD Scheme on a Thursday is often already in the area. That is logistics, not endorsement, and nothing here implies any relationship between IB Gram and any of these schools.

sections.heading: Is home tuition or online better for a Jamnabai Narsee International School student?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and the lead service, and for most families here it is the right answer. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai sitting at the dining table can see the things a screen hides: the student who writes the first line of a mechanics question and then stops, the one who reaches for the calculator before reading the stem, the one whose notes are beautiful and whose rough work is chaos. Handwritten working is central to how both boards award method marks, and watching a pen move is still the fastest diagnostic anyone has. An IB and IGCSE home tuition slot also removes the evening travel problem from the child, which in Juhu in December is not a small thing.

The honest costs of home tutoring are these. The tutor's travel narrows your choice of tutor, because the pool is whoever can reliably reach JVPD Scheme or Vile Parle West at your slot. Travel time also feeds into pricing. A cancelled session is harder to reschedule, because the tutor has usually built the evening around the trip. And a house with a younger sibling, a television and visitors is sometimes a worse study environment than the student's own room with a laptop.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai solves the scarcity problem and nothing else. For a rare combination, HL Further Mathematics, Diploma Programme Mandarin ab initio, IGCSE Computer Science taught by someone who codes, online is often the only way to reach a genuine specialist. It is also the only mode that reliably survives monsoon week, the last fortnight before mocks when nobody wants to lose an hour to the Western Express Highway, and the family trip out of Mumbai. A document camera or a cheap overhead phone mount restores most of the handwriting visibility, provided someone sets it up properly in session one rather than apologising about it for six weeks.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it, and we would rather they planned it. One home session a week for the teaching and the diagnosis, one shorter online session for marking, question practice and checking that the homework was actually done. It costs less in travel, it gives the tutor two touchpoints instead of one, and it means a student booking an IB and IGCSE home teacher for Jamnabai Narsee International School students in Mumbai does not lose the week when the tutor has a wedding in Pune. For a student in repair mode, two shorter contacts a week beat one long one almost every time.

sections.heading: Does your child need gap repair, or a push towards a 7?
paragraphs: This is the section the rest of the page exists for. Take IGCSE Mathematics Extended Paper 4, the longer structured paper, and put two students from the same class in front of it. Student A loses marks from question three onwards and her script thins out towards the end. Looking at her working, the trigonometry questions fail not at the trigonometry but at the rearrangement: she can write the sine rule correctly and then cannot isolate the unknown cleanly. That is a Grade 8 algebra gap wearing a Grade 10 costume. The repair job is three or four sessions on rearrangement and indices, done properly and away from the current chapter, after which half the lost marks come back without anyone teaching her any new trigonometry at all.

Student B, on the same paper, answers nearly everything and still lands short of the top grade. His losses are at the ends of questions: the final part of a multi-step problem, the one asking him to justify or to show that rather than to calculate. He knows the mathematics. What he does not do is write the intermediate line that earns the method mark, and he does not budget time, so the last two questions get rushed. The stretch job is entirely past papers under timed conditions, with the tutor marking as an examiner would, pointing at the exact place a mark was available and not claimed. That is a different tutor, a different hour, and a different conversation with the student.

The same split appears at Diploma Programme level. Take HL Biology Paper 2, the one with data-based questions and extended responses. Student C cannot reliably read the data question: she describes a graph when the command term says explain, and she loses marks she could have had without knowing any extra biology. The repair is command terms and data handling, drilled across topics, plus whatever core content is genuinely missing underneath. Student D sits at a 6 and keeps scoring moderately on the longer extended-response questions. His answers are accurate and unstructured, and in an eight-mark question structure is most of the mark. The stretch is planning those answers in ninety seconds before writing, and learning which named examples the syllabus expects him to deploy.

Diagnosing which student you have takes one session and a pile of marked work, and getting it wrong costs a term. The signal is simple: if marks are lost early in questions and across topics, it is repair. If marks are lost at the ends of questions and only on the harder parts, it is stretch. Mixed cases exist, and in those we start with repair, because stretch work built on a hole does not hold. This is also the honest answer to what IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on, since repair work typically needs more sessions per week for a shorter period while stretch work needs fewer sessions over a longer run, and the total cost follows the board, the level, how scarce the subject specialist is, the travel distance to your home and the session length.

sections.heading: What progress realistically looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: Start with the sentence that most tutoring pages avoid. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. Nobody honestly can, because the grade depends on the student's work between sessions, on the examiner's paper that year, on illness, on the subjects chosen and on a dozen things outside any tutor's control. What we can be accountable for is a match to the right job, a tutor who shows up, and a clear read of whether anything is changing.

At four weeks, do not look at marks. Four weeks is roughly four to eight contact hours, and school assessments in that window were set on material taught before the tutor arrived. What should have changed is diagnostic clarity and behaviour. The tutor should be able to tell you precisely what is wrong, in a sentence you can repeat. The child should be starting homework without a standoff, and should be able to attempt a question she would have skipped in week one. If after four weeks the tutor still describes the problem as the student lacking confidence, that is not a diagnosis and you should ask for a better one.

At one term, marks should move on the type of question that was targeted, even if the overall grade has not shifted. This is where repair and stretch diverge sharply in what they look like. Repair work often produces a jump that arrives all at once, late, after weeks of apparently flat effort, because the gap has to be filled before anything built on it can stand. Stretch work produces small, steady gains that look unimpressive week to week and add up to a grade boundary crossed. Judging repair work by stretch timelines is the most common reason families change tutor one month before it was about to pay off.

At one exam cycle, which means mocks to finals for most students here, you should be able to see the full arc: a measurable change in the targeted components, internal assessment work submitted on time rather than in a panic, and a student who can say what she will do differently in the next paper. Some students gain a great deal and some gain less, and a tutor arriving in February for a two-year gap will not produce what one arriving in June would have. That is not a disclaimer, it is the reason we push families to start repair work in the calm part of the year.

Three, your real availability: which evenings, what time the child actually gets home, and whether weekends are genuinely free or already full. Send those and we will come back with two or three options rather than a directory. We will tell you which job we think this is, and we will say so when we think it is stretch work being described as a crisis, or a crisis being described as needing a bit of polish. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families imagine hiring rarely exists as one person; what usually works is one strong subject specialist for the failing subject and a second only if a second subject is genuinely breaking.

The first session runs ninety minutes in most cases and is structured, not a getting-to-know-you chat. The tutor reads the marked work, watches the student attempt two questions from a past paper with no help, asks her to explain her reasoning out loud, and then teaches one thing properly so the hour is not wasted. Afterwards you get the written read: the diagnosis, the recommended frequency, the first four weeks of plan, and an honest note if the tutor thinks the subject is not the real problem.

Further out across Mumbai the slot matters more than the postcode, and we will say honestly if a travel pattern is going to collapse by October rather than booking it and hoping. A tutor who agrees to a 7pm Khar West slot from further north will usually hold it for a month and then start arriving late. We would rather match you with someone slightly less ideal on paper who lives within a genuinely short run of your building, or move you to a 5pm slot, or put one of the two weekly sessions online. Reliability over a full term beats a perfect profile.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for Diploma Programme subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one condition: the tutor must be able to see handwritten working in real time. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai teaching HL Mathematics or HL Chemistry without a document camera or an overhead phone mount is working blind, because the marks in those subjects live in the method lines, not the final answer. Set that up in the first session. Beyond that, online is often the only route to a genuine specialist in a scarce subject, and it is the mode that survives monsoon week, exam-season traffic and family travel. For discussion-heavy subjects like TOK and History it works particularly well.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the diagnosis in writing before you change anything. At four weeks you should expect clarity and changed behaviour rather than changed marks, since any assessment in that window tested material taught before the tutor arrived. The question to put to the tutor is specific: what exactly is wrong, what have you done about it, and what will be different in three weeks. A good tutor answers in concrete terms. If the answer is still about confidence or motivation, that is a reason to rematch. Repair work in particular often looks flat for weeks and then moves in one step, so check which job you booked.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is simply not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we rematch, at no additional matching cost. It is worth doing this early rather than politely waiting out a term. The most useful thing you can give us is the reason, in plain terms: too slow, too fast, unreliable on timing, cannot explain things a second way, or the child does not speak in sessions. That detail changes who we suggest next far more than a general dissatisfaction does. In many cases the mismatch turns out to be a job mismatch rather than a person mismatch, a stretch tutor placed on a repair problem, and the replacement is a different kind of teacher entirely.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, though not in the room. That is standard practice for home tuition anywhere and it protects everyone, including the tutor. Beyond that, the practical requirements are small: a table rather than a bed, a chair for the tutor, decent light, and the younger sibling and the television somewhere else for ninety minutes. Agree a policy on missed sessions at the start, such as twenty-four hours notice for a free reschedule, since a cancelled home session costs the tutor a travelled evening. Settle the gate pass question before the first visit, not at the gate.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all IB and IGCSE subjects, or do we need several?
faqs.answer: One tutor can rarely cover everything well above Grade 9, and you should be cautious of anyone who says they can. A good Mathematics and Physics pairing is common and credible. Mathematics, Chemistry, Economics and English from one person is usually a generalist stretched thin. Our normal recommendation is one strong specialist for the subject that is actually failing, run properly for a term, and a second tutor added only if a second subject genuinely breaks. Two tutors at two hours each beats one tutor at four hours spread across four subjects, which tends to become homework supervision rather than teaching.

faqs.question: My son is predicted a 6 in a Higher Level subject and wants a 7. Is a tutor worth it?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but only with a stretch tutor and only if you start early enough. The gap between a 6 and a 7 is rarely about content; it is about the last marks on extended responses, command-term precision, answer structure under time pressure and the quality of the internal assessment. That is coachable, and it responds to examiner-style marking of real past papers rather than more teaching. Starting in September gives it room; starting in March means triage. We will tell you honestly if we think the timeline is too short, and we do not guarantee grades to anyone.

sections.heading: The IB and IGCSE pathway a Borivali campus family is choosing between
paragraphs: A campus offering both an International Baccalaureate route and a Cambridge IGCSE route puts a decision in front of parents that most schools never do. Through the Middle Years Programme (MYP) the two look similar from a kitchen-table distance: projects, criteria, a report that talks about skills rather than marks. From Year 9 they separate. IGCSE moves towards terminal written papers set by Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, while an MYP stream carries on with criterion-based assessment and a personal project, and the two now reward quite different habits.

Within IGCSE the first real fork is Core versus Extended. Core trims the syllabus and caps the attainable grade; Extended keeps the full content and the full grade range. Schools usually set this during Year 10 on the strength of Year 9 internal marks, which is exactly the point at which a few months of targeted work changes what the child is permitted to attempt. A tutor who arrives in Year 11 can lift a grade inside Core. They cannot move a child back onto Extended.

The Diploma Programme fork comes later and bites harder. Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. HL is not SL with extra homework; it adds content, a longer paper and a different standard of discussion in class. A student who chose HL Physics because a friend did and is drowning by the October of DP1 needs a conversation about the subject change deadline long before they need more past papers.

We match across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 with a tutor in Mumbai who has taught that exact level, which sounds obvious and is not what most families get. The level matters as much as the subject. Year 9 work is about building the habits the board rewards; Year 11 work is about mark schemes and timing. A brilliant DP teacher can be a poor fit for a Year 9 who still writes answers in paragraphs when the paper wants bullet points and a unit.

sections.heading: Which papers and internal assessments does each subject actually carry?
paragraphs: Every subject on both boards has a shape, and a tutor who does not already know the shape burns the first month finding it. Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 runs a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical paper that most schools sit as the Alternative to Practical. IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits calculator and non-calculator work across two papers at Extended. English as a Second Language and First Language English are different qualifications with different reading mark schemes, and parents regularly discover that distinction in Year 11 rather than Year 9.

On the IB side the Internal Assessment (IA) is where the quiet marks sit. DP Biology and DP Chemistry each carry a scientific investigation. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics Applications and Interpretation both carry an exploration. Business Management, Economics, Psychology and History each carry their own written task with its own criteria and word limit. These are marked by the school and moderated externally, which means the child's own teacher sets the standard, and a tutor's job is to teach the criteria rather than to produce the work.

That distinction matters more on an IA than anywhere else on either board. A tutor who hands a student a research question has given them something they cannot defend in a conversation with their teacher and cannot rescue when the data misbehaves in week two. What a good tutor does is slower: read the published criteria with the student, look at the student's own first idea, ask what can genuinely be measured in a flat in Borivali or in a school lab in forty minutes, and make the student rewrite it themselves.

Across the two boards we are asked most often for Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Economics, then English Language and Literature, then Business Management, Psychology and Computer Science. Second-language subjects are the hardest to staff anywhere in the northern suburbs: French B, Spanish ab initio and Hindi B all run short. We cover all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes across Mumbai, but for the scarce ones the honest answer is often a strong online teacher with a weekend in-person block rather than a weekly weekday visit from someone who is merely nearby.

sections.heading: Where the northern catchment lives, and the rest of Mumbai we cover
paragraphs: This campus anchors international-board education at the northern end of Mumbai, and its catchment reflects that. Families come from Borivali West and Borivali East, from Dahisar, from Kandivali, and in real numbers from Mira Road and Bhayandar, with a few travelling in from Vasai. Most of those parents made a deliberate trade: a long school commute every single day, in both directions, because the alternative within a short drive is no IB or IGCSE school at all. That trade shapes everything else on this page.

Borivali station anchors the geography. The Western Line carries parents south to work while the children travel by bus along Link Road and the Western Express Highway, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 have changed the evening arithmetic for tutors more than for students: a teacher finishing in Kandivali East can now reach Borivali East without surrendering an hour to the highway. We use that when building a tutor's evening chain, because an IB and IGCSE home tutor for JBCN International School Borivali students in Mumbai who is not sitting in traffic is a tutor who arrives when they said they would.

We match outside this corridor too, and the same travel logic applies everywhere. In South Mumbai we work in Colaba, Breach Candy and Worli, where the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 matter more than raw distance. Across the Western Suburbs we cover Bandra West, Juhu, Andheri West and Goregaon East, matching along the line rather than across it. In the Central Suburbs that means Powai and Ghatkopar, reached by JVLR, Metro Line 1 and the Eastern Express Highway rather than by train.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur up through Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway doing more for those families than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is matched node by node, Vashi and Kharghar most often, along Palm Beach Road and now the Atal Setu. Thane we cover from the station across Pokhran Road and out along Ghodbunder Road. The Bandra-Worli Sea Link helps a Worli tutor reach Bandra; it does nothing for a Borivali family, which is why we almost never propose a southern tutor for a weekday slot this far north.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a child who commutes across north Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here for a plain reason: a child who has already spent two hours on a bus will not get back into a vehicle for a tuition centre. IB and IGCSE home tuition for JBCN International School Borivali students in Mumbai removes the one journey the family can actually control. The tutor absorbs the travel, and the student is at the table five minutes after changing out of uniform, which on a Tuesday in October is the difference between a session and an argument.

The trade-off is real and worth stating. A home tutor is drawn only from people who can physically reach your building at that hour, which narrows the pool, and the pool is narrowest exactly where the subject is rarest. Home sessions also depend on a room that works: a cleared dining table with the television off beats a bedroom desk with a younger sibling in it. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai lives or dies on whether the slot is honest, because if the Western Express Highway goes bad the session starts late and the hour is yours to lose, not ours.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai solves the scarcity problem and solves nothing else. For HL Chemistry, Economics or French B the right teacher may live in Chembur or Navi Mumbai and will never be a weekday visitor to Borivali. Online works well for past-paper walkthroughs, mark-scheme work and IA feedback, where the document is on the screen for both people anyway. It works badly at 8pm with a tired fourteen-year-old who needs someone physically present to stop the drift into a phone.

Hybrid is where most families in this catchment land within a month, so we usually propose it from the start rather than let them discover it. One in-person weekend block of ninety minutes or two hours, when the child is rested and the tutor can travel without fighting the evening, plus one shorter online session midweek for correction and question-setting. For a Mira Road or Bhayandar family that pattern survives a full term. A twice-weekly 7pm home visit, in our experience, usually does not.
bullets: Home tuition first: the tutor absorbs the travel so the student does not.

sections.heading: How are IB and IGCSE tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet one?
paragraphs: Before any profile reaches you we check four things: identity against a government photo ID, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, genuine experience of the board and level in question, and a subject conversation with someone who knows the syllabus. A candidate who says they teach IGCSE Physics is asked how they would handle a Paper 6 question on anomalous results, and what they would say to a student who plotted the line through every point. Vague answers end the conversation there.

Board experience is where most applicants come apart, and it is the check that matters most for a family at this campus. Teaching Class 10 Mathematics well is a real skill and it is not the same skill as teaching IGCSE 0580 at Extended, where the command words, the working marks and the expected layout all differ. The same gap sits between a capable undergraduate physicist and someone who has marked against DP criteria and knows what a Grade 5 script looks like. We ask for specifics and we verify them against documents.

Then there is the part only you can check, and we would much rather you did. Watch the trial session. Does the tutor ask your child to explain something back, or do they talk for fifty minutes? Do they open the child's own marked script, or do they open their own notes? Ask them directly what the IA criteria are called for your child's subject. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai who cannot answer that in plain language is not ready for Diploma Programme work, whatever the CV says.

Two warning signs are worth naming out loud. The first is anyone claiming a connection to your child's school: access to its papers, a former staff member on the team, knowledge of what is on an upcoming assessment. The second is anyone promising an outcome. Choosing an IB and IGCSE home teacher for JBCN International School Borivali students in Mumbai should feel like hiring a professional, not buying a result, and a tutor who sells certainty is selling the wrong product to the wrong family.
bullets: Government photo ID and the claimed qualification are both checked against documents.
Board experience is tested with a syllabus question, not accepted from a CV.
Watch the trial: does the tutor open your child's own marked script?
Ask what the IA criteria are called for that exact subject.
