faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Oberoi International School, JVLR in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Oberoi International School, JVLR, or to any other school named on this page. We have no access to its staff, its internal documents or its reporting system, and we do not present any tutor as having taught there. Everything written here about the school is public: it is an IB school on the JVLR corridor in Mumbai offering Primary Years Programme, Middle Years Programme and Diploma Programme pathways. If any tutor claims inside knowledge of a school's marking or admissions, treat that claim as a warning sign rather than a selling point.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach our building in Chandivali for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor already works the eastern half of the JVLR corridor. Chandivali is reached off Saki Vihar Road, which queues in the evening peak alongside JVLR itself, so the tutors who hold these slots reliably are the ones with other families in Powai, Kanjurmarg or Vikhroli on the same evening. A tutor crossing from Andheri West or Bandra will manage it in September and start asking to move the slot by October. That is why an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Oberoi International School JVLR students in Mumbai is matched on travel direction first and on the timetable second.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor need from us at the society gate?
faqs.answer: One registered recurring visitor entry, rather than a fresh argument every week. Most societies along JVLR, in Powai and in Andheri East will log a repeat visitor if a resident registers the tutor's name, phone number and weekly slot with the society office once. Share those details the day before the first session, keep the slot consistent so the gate staff recognise the pattern, and tell the tutor which gate to use and where to park, because those two are rarely the same entrance. Sessions themselves stay in a shared room with an adult at home, which is a rule we do not bend.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 4 and the criteria make no sense to me. Where does a tutor start?
faqs.answer: With the criterion wording, not with content. A Middle Years Programme tutor should spend the first two or three sessions teaching your child to read the strand being assessed and to feel the difference between describing, explaining and evaluating, because that distinction is where marks are lost by children who know the material perfectly well. After that the work becomes content delivered through task types: a Criterion D question in Sciences, a Criterion B investigation design, a Criterion C table with repeats and uncertainty. If the first month instead looks like a textbook worked through in order, the match is wrong.

faqs.question: Should we choose Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Choose on how your child writes and what the university route requires, not on which course sounds harder. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy and proof-leaning, and it is the safer route into engineering, physics and most quantitative economics degrees. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and data-led with a technology-assisted feel, and it suits children who think in context rather than in abstraction. Higher Level against Standard Level is a separate and bigger decision, because Higher Level adds both content and the pace at which it arrives. A tutor who has taught both courses can usually tell you within two sessions which one fits.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, session length and travel, in roughly that order of weight. A Diploma Programme Higher Level science, or a less commonly taught language, costs more than a Middle Years Programme subject simply because fewer tutors can teach it properly. Travel is a genuine component on the JVLR corridor: a tutor crossing from one half to the other in the evening peak spends an hour nobody is paying for, which is why we match within a side wherever the subject allows. Online sessions remove that component entirely. We will not print a figure here, because any number would be wrong for half the families reading it.

faqs.question: We live in Jogeshwari West but both parents work in Bandra Kurla Complex. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes the slot rather than the tutor pool. If nobody is home before eight, your real options are a later weekday session with an adult present, a weekend morning slot, or an online session on the evenings you cannot get back in time. Jogeshwari West sits on the western side of the corridor, so your pool is the Andheri East, Jogeshwari and Goregaon one. The variable is your commute on the Western Express Highway, not the tutor's. Tell us the earliest time an adult is reliably in the flat and we will match against that rather than against an ideal evening.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: It works well for review and drafting and underperforms badly for teaching a younger child who is drifting. An online tutor cannot see that a thirteen-year-old stopped writing four minutes ago, has a chat window open behind the call, or is copying the worked example rather than following the logic of it. For Diploma Programme students working on an exploration or an essay draft, a shared screen genuinely beats a shared table. Our standard recommendation for Middle Years Programme families is home sessions for the teaching and online only for a short review or a pre-test clinic.

faqs.question: Our older child does IGCSE at another school. Can one tutor cover both boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only where the tutor has actually taught both rather than read about one of them. Cambridge IGCSE and the IB share a great deal of content in the sciences and in mathematics but assess it very differently: tiered papers and mark schemes on one side, published criteria and internal assessment on the other. A tutor who teaches both well will describe that difference without being prompted. Where it genuinely helps is logistics, because one visit to your home covers two children and one travel slot on the corridor instead of two. Ask the question directly in the introductory call.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three weeks. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us with one specific example and we go back to the shortlist, usually within a week. The example is what makes it fast: a complaint that the child does not like him is hard to act on, while two sessions spent on content she already had, or homework that ignored the unit the school is running, tells us exactly what to change in the brief. The replacement inherits the notes from the first tutor, so nothing restarts from zero. There is no penalty for changing once. Changing twice in a term usually means the brief was wrong, and we will say so.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, though not sitting in the room. That is a safety rule rather than a supervision one: sessions happen in a shared space with the door open and a responsible adult present in the home, which can be a grandparent or a long-standing member of household staff. It helps practically too, because the tutor can hand over a two-minute summary at the door instead of sending a message that gets read at midnight. If nobody can be home on the evening that suits your child, that is an argument for a weekend slot or for online.

faqs.question: How early should a DP1 student start, and what about the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Start in the first term of Diploma Programme Year 1, before the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines stack up in the second year. The Extended Essay is the piece families consistently underestimate: it needs a researchable question, a supervisor relationship the student has to manage themselves, and a reading phase that cannot be compressed into a fortnight in January. A tutor cannot and must not write any part of it, but can help a student narrow the question, build a reading list and hold the drafting schedule. The same logic applies to the Mathematics exploration and the science Internal Assessment.

sections.heading: The IGCSE and IB pathways behind one school name in Mumbai
paragraphs: Podar International School is publicly described as offering IGCSE and International Baccalaureate (IB) pathways at its Santacruz and Powai campuses. Which pathway runs in which year group at which campus is a question for the school's own office, and we do not claim to know it. A tutor needs something narrower anyway: the board your child is sitting this year, the year group, and whether the paper in front of them is school-set or board-set.

On the Cambridge International Education side, IGCSE Years 9-11 usually means a two-year teaching run into a May or June series, graded 9 to 1 per subject, with each subject split into numbered components rather than one exam. Maths 0580 has Papers 2 and 4 on the Extended tier and Papers 1 and 3 on Core. The sciences carry a practical-style component. English First Language 0500 carries directed writing and composition. The component matters more than the subject name, because a student can be strong in Chemistry and still be losing most of their marks on one paper type.

On the IB side the structure changes shape rather than difficulty. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) and Middle Years Programme (MYP) are assessed against published criteria scored in bands, so an MYP Science task is marked on Criterion B inquiry design and Criterion C processing rather than on a percentage. The Diploma Programme (DP) splits subjects into Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), adds an Internal Assessment (IA) in almost every subject, and sits them under the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) core out of forty-five points.

The pathway change that catches families is MYP into DP. A student used to criteria bands meets externally marked papers, a word-limited IA and a TOK essay inside eighteen months. A request that begins as all IB and IGCSE subjects and narrows at IGCSE Years 9-11 to one home tutor in Mumbai per subject is the normal outcome, not a failure of the brief. An IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai who is excellent on DP Economics is not automatically the right person for 0580 Paper 4, and pretending otherwise wastes a term.
bullets: IGCSE Years 9-11: a two-year run, numbered components, grades 9 to 1.
Core and Extended are different papers, not the same paper marked differently.
MYP tasks are scored against published criteria in bands, not percentages.
DP adds Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge to the exams.
HL and SL differ in syllabus content and paper structure, not only in hours.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: what travels between campuses
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision that quietly sets the next two years. At IGCSE the question is how many subjects and which tier; at DP it is the six-subject grid plus three Higher Levels. Families at both campuses face the same syllabus documents, so the choice itself is portable. What is not portable is the local teaching set, the timetable clash pattern and the availability of a tutor who has taught that exact combination recently.

Core and Extended at IGCSE are separate papers with separate grade ceilings, and the entry is made by the school with Cambridge, not by a tutor. We work with the decision the school has entered, prepare the student for the papers that entry implies, and say plainly when the evidence in front of us points the other way so that you can raise it with the subject teacher. HL and SL at DP differ in content and in paper structure: HL Biology carries extra syllabus material and a longer Paper 2, and HL Mathematics Analysis and Approaches adds a third paper that SL students never sit.

Every route carries internal work that is marked against a published rubric and then moderated. IGCSE subjects carry coursework or a practical-style alternative. MYP carries criterion-assessed tasks across the year. DP carries a subject IA in almost every subject, the Extended Essay, and the TOK exhibition and essay. Internal work is where tutoring earns its keep, because it is planned, drafted and improvable, unlike a three-hour paper. It is also where the boundary sits: a tutor may teach method, question a research design and mark a practice piece, but the words must be the student's own and the school's academic honesty policy decides what counts.

A worked example makes the point. Take Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical. A question hands the student a circuit with an ammeter and a voltmeter and asks them to record readings, tabulate them, plot a graph and find a gradient. The marks are not for knowing that resistance is voltage divided by current. They are for a column heading that carries the quantity and the unit, readings written to a consistent number of decimal places, axes scaled so the points fill more than half the grid, a best-fit line drawn through the scatter instead of joined dot to dot, and a gradient taken from a large triangle with its coordinates shown. A student who understands the physics can still lose most of that question in twenty minutes. A tutor who has marked the paper fixes it by making the student draw the empty table before taking a single reading.
bullets: Tier and subject entries are made by the school with the board, not by tutors.
HL adds syllabus content and extra papers, not simply more lessons.
Internal Assessment is planned work, so it responds best to tutoring.
A tutor may mark practice pieces; the submitted words stay the student's own.
Ask which component your child loses marks on, not which subject feels weak.

sections.heading: Santacruz, Powai and the rest of Mumbai: where tutors actually come from
paragraphs: Santacruz West and Santacruz East sit either side of Santacruz station on the Western Line, which makes the western campus one of the easier addresses in Mumbai, Maharashtra to staff. A tutor living in Khar, Bandra, Vile Parle, Juhu or Andheri West reaches a Santacruz West building by one short train hop or a ten-minute auto, and the Western Express Highway carries the Santacruz East side. Metro Line 1 at Andheri and the airport-belt stretch of Metro Line 3 widen that pool further.

Powai and Chandivali work differently. Both hang off JVLR, and tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar or Vikhroli rather than stepping off a platform. Kanjurmarg is the Central Line station most families use for the Powai side, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road joins the two halves of this page in about half an hour off-peak. Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai means the area already holds a resident pool of IGCSE and IB DP tutors, which helps, but a Powai slot is still booked around traffic rather than around a timetable.

Beyond those two addresses, IB Gram matches across the city. In South Mumbai that means Colaba, Worli, Tardeo and Fort, where the Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link now matter more than raw distance. The Western Suburbs run from Bandra and Khar up through Malad, Kandivali and Borivali on the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7. The Central Suburbs cover Kurla, Ghatkopar, Mulund and the Powai pocket off JVLR. The Eastern Suburbs take in Chembur, Vikhroli and Bhandup on the Harbour and Central lines, with the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway behind them.

Navi Mumbai is matched node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Kharghar along Palm Beach Road, with the Atal Setu now making a Chembur or Wadala tutor plausible for a weekend slot. Thane is its own market, running from the station across Pokhran Road and Majiwada out to Ghodbunder Road. The practical range of an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Podar International School students in Mumbai is set by one rule: match along a corridor, not across the city. A tutor crossing from Borivali to Powai twice a week will quietly stop coming by the third month, and nobody wins that argument with a map.

Powai and Chandivali: JVLR access from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg and Ghatkopar.

sections.heading: What a multi-campus school calendar does to a tutoring schedule
paragraphs: A Cambridge and IB school in Mumbai runs June to April, which puts the heaviest assessment load in the months when the city is least cooperative. June and July are settling weeks and tier conversations. August and September bring the first formal school assessments that actually predict anything. October carries the Diwali break, which families treat as rest and schools treat as revision time.

November and December are mock season for IGCSE Years 9-11 and the stretch where DP2 students hand in IA drafts. January and February are the compression point: DP IAs and the Extended Essay close, DP mocks run, and IGCSE coursework deadlines land in the same fortnight. March to June is the board series itself, and a smaller November Cambridge series pulls a second group of students into October revision. A tutor booked in September for two sessions a week is cheaper and calmer than a tutor hunted in January.

Here is the part specific to a network school. Two campuses under one name do not have to share an assessment week, a parent-teacher meeting date or a holiday pattern, and we have no way to check which dates apply to you. IB Gram is independent and has no affiliation with Podar International School, so we work from the circular your campus sends you rather than from a central calendar, and we ask you to forward the dates exactly as published. A tutor planning a pre-exam intensive from the wrong campus's dates wastes a fortnight of a family's money.

The practical consequence is scheduling. A tutor who covers Powai and Chandivali may hold students at more than one school, including Hiranandani Foundation School, whose IGCSE and IB DP calendar is its own. When those exam weeks do not align, that tutor's evening slots in the critical fortnight are already gone. Book the intensive block the week the circular arrives, not the week before the paper. The same holds on the Santacruz side, where a tutor's Western Line round often covers several schools between Bandra and Andheri.
bullets: June to July: settling in, tier conversations, homework patterns worth watching.
November to December: IGCSE mocks and DP Internal Assessment drafts collide.
January to February: IAs, Extended Essay and coursework deadlines in one fortnight.
Campuses in one network may hold different assessment weeks; use your own circular.
Book pre-exam blocks when the circular arrives, not the week before the paper.

sections.heading: Is home tuition, online or hybrid better for a Podar student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition first for IGCSE Years 9-11 and for any subject with a written or practical component, online for scarce subjects and for the week before a deadline, hybrid for most families by the second term. Home tuition leads because a tutor at your dining table sees the actual working rather than a cropped photograph of it.

The honest cost of home tuition is travel, and it is paid in the tutor's evening rather than in yours. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who sits in traffic for fifty minutes each way will take fewer students, hold the slot more rigidly and price the distance in. On the Santacruz side that cost is low, because the Western Line does the work for them. On the Powai and Chandivali side it is real, which is why a Powai slot at seven in the evening is harder to hold than the same slot at five.

Online is not a downgrade, it is a different set of trade-offs. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is the right answer for a scarce combination, for a tutor who is simply better than anyone within reach, and for the seven in the morning slot that no travelling tutor will take. It works well for essay subjects, for DP Economics and TOK, and for marking a draft on a shared document. It works less well for graph work and practical write-ups unless you add a document camera and insist on photographs of full working rather than of answers.

Most families who ask for IB and IGCSE home tuition for Podar International School students in Mumbai end up on a hybrid pattern by the second term: one home session a week for the long teaching block, one shorter online session for homework review and draft marking. IB Gram can run all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes in Mumbai or online, and an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai will usually propose the hybrid split themselves once they have watched a month of the student's week. The phrase best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai gets typed constantly, but there is no single best tutor, only the right one for one subject at one level.
bullets: Home tuition: full working visible, a fixed slot, travel priced into the rate.
Online: a wider tutor pool, early-morning slots, weaker on graphs and practicals.
Hybrid: one long home session plus one short online review each week.
Santacruz slots are easier to fill than Powai slots at the same hour.
A document camera fixes most of what online loses in Maths and the sciences.

sections.heading: How are tutors verified, and what should you check yourself?
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram has had identity and qualifications checked, has stated the boards, subjects and levels they teach, and has named the syllabus codes they have taught most recently. Beyond that, you check the teaching yourself in the first session, because no document proves that a person can explain moles to a fourteen-year-old at eight in the evening.

What we check before a profile reaches a parent: government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, the specific boards and components rather than a vague tutor label, two contactable references where they exist, and a subject conversation with someone who knows the syllabus. Tutors who cannot name the components of the paper they say they teach do not get sent out. Every IB and IGCSE tutor for Podar International School students in Mumbai is matched on syllabus evidence rather than on a general claim of experience.

What you should check in the first two sessions, in this order. Ask which component the plan targets and what the next four sessions will cover. Ask for one marked practice question back, with the mark scheme logic shown rather than a tick. Ask what the session note will say and where you will receive it. Then watch your child's own behaviour: a student who starts attempting the hard question before the tutor arrives is the only early signal worth trusting.

Two red flags are worth naming. Anyone who claims access to a school's internal materials, mark schemes, predicted grades or report data is either wrong or doing something you do not want attached to your child's file, and IB Gram will not pass such a request to a tutor. Anyone who promises a grade is selling what nobody can deliver. We do not guarantee grades, and a tutor who does has told you the most important thing about themselves in the first ten minutes.
bullets: Checked: photo identity, qualification claimed, boards, levels and recent syllabus codes.
Checked: a subject conversation with someone who knows the components.
You check: one marked practice question with the mark scheme logic shown.
You check: a written session note and a four-session plan you can read.
Red flag: anyone claiming school-internal materials, mark schemes or report data.

sections.heading: Moving between the Santacruz and Powai campuses mid-year: what actually changes
paragraphs: A family relocating from Santacruz to Powai inside the same school network is not changing curriculum. The board is the same, the syllabus codes are the same, the textbooks are the same, and an IA already half drafted is still the same IA. What changes is geography, and geography is what tutoring actually runs on. This is the question a single-campus school never has to answer, and it is why the campus line sits at the top of this page.

Transferable without argument: the syllabus and component list, the student's notes and past papers, the tier or Higher Level decision the school has already entered, the diagnosis a tutor has written down, and the four-session plan. Not transferable: the slot time, the travel assumption, the visitor protocol at the new building, and often the tutor. Someone who held a Tuesday at six in Santacruz West by walking from the station cannot hold the same Tuesday in Hiranandani Gardens, and asking them to try is how a good match quietly dies.

So we run the move as a handover rather than as a restart. The outgoing tutor writes a note covering the component the student is on, what has been tried, what worked, the two errors that keep returning, and the next four sessions as planned. The incoming tutor reads it before the first session and is told not to re-diagnose from scratch. Where the subject is scarce, the outgoing tutor stays on online for three or four weeks while a new home tutor starts in person on the Powai side, so the teaching continues while the logistics settle.

Families choosing between the two campuses rather than moving ask a fair version of the same question: does the campus matter for tutoring? Mildly, and only on supply. Take DP Mathematics Applications and Interpretation SL Paper 2, which is calculator-allowed and rewards a student who knows which graphing display calculator menu answers the question in thirty seconds instead of three minutes of algebra. Finding a tutor fluent in that exact calculator workflow is quick near the Western Line and takes about a week longer off JVLR. That is a sourcing lead time, not an academic difference, and it is the only honest answer to the question.
bullets: Transfers: syllabus, components, notes, tier entry, diagnosis, four-session plan.
Does not transfer: slot time, travel assumption, gate protocol, often the tutor.
The handover note names the component, what was tried and the recurring errors.
Scarce subjects: keep the outgoing tutor online for three weeks during the move.
Choosing a campus changes sourcing lead time, not the syllabus your child sits.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see a diagnosis and one changed habit, not a changed grade. At one term, marks on the school's own assessments should move, or you should know exactly why they have not. At one exam cycle you get a grade, and that grade belongs to the student. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will.

Four weeks is eight sessions at twice a week. By then a tutor should be able to tell you in a sentence what is actually wrong: not knowing the content, knowing it and misreading the command word, knowing it and running out of time, or not writing enough down to earn the method marks. One habit should have changed visibly, and the ones that show up first are mechanical: drawing the table before taking readings, writing the formula before substituting, underlining the command word before answering.

A term is where honesty matters. Marks on school assessments should move, and if they have not there are only a few real explanations: the plan was aimed at the wrong component, the student is not doing the between-session work, sessions are being cancelled, or the tutor and the student simply do not work together. All four are visible in session notes, which is why the notes exist. A term in which nothing moved and nobody can say why is a term you should not pay for twice.

Across a full cycle a tutor can close a content gap, rebuild exam technique and make internal work land on time. A tutor cannot sit the paper, cannot fix attendance, cannot replace school teaching and cannot turn an unprepared student into a prepared one in April. Progress also stops being linear near the end: the last two grade boundaries cost more work than the first three. If the honest answer by March is that the realistic target is a grade below the one on the wall, you deserve to hear that in February.
bullets: Four weeks: a written diagnosis and one visible change in working habits.
One term: movement on school assessments, or a clear reason there is none.
Session notes exist so a stalled term can be explained rather than argued about.
A tutor cannot fix attendance or replace school teaching, and grades are not guaranteed.
Late gains cost more work than early ones; plan the final term accordingly.

sections.heading: Starting home classes in Mumbai: what to have ready for the first session
paragraphs: Three things make a first session useful instead of introductory: the most recent marked school assessment, the textbook or syllabus booklet with its code visible, and ten minutes of your own time at the start to say what you are actually worried about. The tutor spends that first session diagnosing rather than teaching, and that is the correct use of it.

Set up the physical side before the tutor arrives. A table with a chair on each side, not a bed. A plug within reach. The phone in another room, agreed in advance rather than confiscated in the moment. For a Santacruz West or Santacruz East flat, send the building name and the lane, because map pins in that grid are unreliable. For Powai or Chandivali, pre-register the tutor with the gate as a weekly visitor on day one, or you will spend fifteen minutes of a paid hour on the intercom every week.

Expect the first session to end with a short written note: the component the student is on, the two errors the tutor saw, what the next three sessions will cover, and what the student is meant to do before the next one. If that note does not arrive, ask for it once. Searches for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai end in the same place for every family: one tutor, one subject, one fixed slot, and a note you can read on a Sunday.

One more practical point. Decide at the start who holds the schedule. The parent who books the slot should be the person who cancels and reschedules it, because a tutor handling two conflicting instructions loses that slot to somebody else. Term-time consistency beats intensity: two steady hours a week from July does more than six hours a week from January, and it costs less in total. If the first tutor is wrong, say so in week two rather than in week eight.
bullets: Bring the most recent marked school assessment to the first session.
Have the textbook or syllabus booklet with its code visible.
Pre-register the tutor at the Powai or Chandivali gate as a weekly visitor.
Agree on one parent as the single point for booking and cancelling.
Ask for a written note after session one naming the component and next steps.

faqs.question: What does an IB and IGCSE tutor for Podar International School students cost in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things, and any page quoting you a single number is guessing. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai move with the board and level, because a DP Higher Level subject or a Year 11 Extended paper needs a scarcer tutor than Year 9 Maths. They move with subject scarcity: Chemistry and Economics tutors are easier to find than DP Music or Further Maths. They move with travel distance, which is why a Powai evening slot prices differently from a Santacruz West one. They move with session length and frequency, and with whether you are booking a term-time weekly block or a pre-exam intensive. Ask for the rate per session and the travel assumption in the same sentence.

faqs.question: Do your tutors work at Podar International School or have any connection to it?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Podar International School in any way, and no tutor is presented as a member of its staff. We name the school because parents search by school name, and because its published IGCSE and IB pathways tell a tutor which syllabus to prepare. That is the whole extent of it. We hold no school materials, no internal mark schemes, no predicted grades and no report data, and we will not ask a tutor to obtain any of them. If a tutor ever claims that sort of access, tell us and the profile comes down.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Santacruz West for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and Santacruz West is one of the easier asks in the city. Santacruz station on the Western Line puts a large pool within fifteen minutes, and tutors living in Khar, Bandra, Vile Parle or Juhu treat that run as local. The constraint is not distance but sequence: someone finishing a session in Andheri at six cannot be at your door at seven, so the slot that holds is the first or the last of their evening. Send your building name and lane with the request, because the mid-block addresses between S V Road and the Western Express Highway are badly mapped and a wrong pin costs the first twenty minutes.

faqs.question: How does gate and visitor access work for a home tutor in Powai or Chandivali?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a recurring visitor and the problem disappears. Most Powai and Chandivali societies log visitors by phone number and purpose, some issue a weekly pass, and a few insist on a resident confirmation call every visit. Settle which one applies in the first week, with the tutor's name and number given to the gate in advance. The reason this matters is arithmetic: fifteen minutes lost at an intercom each week is close to a full session gone by the end of a term, and the tutor is already arriving by road off JVLR with no train timetable to fall back on.

faqs.question: We are moving from the Santacruz campus to the Powai campus in November. What happens to our tutor?
faqs.answer: The teaching continues; the logistics restart. The board, the syllabus codes and any part-drafted Internal Assessment travel with your child unchanged, so there is no academic reset to manage. What usually cannot travel is the tutor's weekly journey, because a Santacruz West slot reached on foot from the station is a completely different proposition off JVLR. We handle it as a handover: the outgoing tutor writes up the component, the diagnosis, the two recurring errors and the next four sessions, and the incoming tutor reads that before session one. For a scarce subject we keep the first tutor online for three or four weeks while a new home tutor starts in person.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for IGCSE Physics and Chemistry practical papers, or are home sessions better?
faqs.answer: Partly, and only with a camera pointed at the page. The practical-style components reward table layout, units in column headings, consistent decimal places and graph plotting, all of which a tutor has to watch the student produce rather than read afterwards. A phone photo of a finished answer hides the order the student worked in, which is usually the actual problem. With a document camera or a second phone on a stand, online works well enough for technique drilling. For the first month of rebuilding how a student lays out a practical answer we still recommend home sessions, then move online once the habit holds.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the diagnosis in writing before you change anything else. After eight sessions a tutor should be able to name what is wrong in one sentence and show you the evidence from marked practice questions. If that sentence does not exist, the tutoring is the problem. If it does exist and marks still have not moved, check the between-session work and the cancellation record first, because a month of sessions with no work between them is not a month of tutoring. If the plan was aimed at the wrong component, the fix is a new plan rather than a new tutor.

faqs.question: The tutor is not a good fit. How does a replacement happen?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week two rather than week eight and the replacement is straightforward. We ask one question: what specifically is not working, the explaining, the pace, the slot or the relationship. That answer changes who we send next, which is the point of asking it. The outgoing tutor writes a handover note covering the component, what was tried and what worked, so the new tutor does not spend two sessions re-diagnosing a student you have already paid to have diagnosed once. There is no penalty for a change in the first month, and most changes happen there.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all the subjects my child is taking?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is usually a mistake to try. One home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai makes sense for Years 6 to 8, where a strong generalist is genuinely useful. From IGCSE Year 9 upward the papers reward component-specific knowledge: the person who knows 0580 Paper 4 question styles is not usually the person who knows DP History Paper 3 or the Biology IA rubric. Two subject tutors, each once a week, beat one generalist three times a week at this level. Where budget forces a choice, pick the subject carrying the heaviest internal assessment load first.

faqs.question: Do you have past papers, mark schemes or assessment data from the school?
faqs.answer: No, and we would not use them if they were offered. Our tutors work from published syllabus documents, from official past papers and mark schemes released by Cambridge International Education and the International Baccalaureate, and from the marked work your child brings home. School-internal assessments, predicted grades and report comments belong to the school and to the family. You are free to show a tutor your own child's marked paper, which is the single most useful thing you can put in front of them. What we will not do is seek material from a campus, approach its staff, or imply that we know how any campus sets its tests.

faqs.question: Which Mumbai areas do you cover besides Santacruz and Powai?
faqs.answer: All six zones, matched by corridor rather than by distance. South Mumbai covers Colaba, Worli, Tardeo and Fort; the Western Suburbs run Bandra to Borivali along the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7; the Central Suburbs take Kurla, Ghatkopar, Mulund and the Powai pocket off JVLR; the Eastern Suburbs cover Chembur, Vikhroli and Bhandup; Navi Mumbai works node to node from Vashi to Panvel along Palm Beach Road; and Thane runs from the station out along Pokhran Road and Ghodbunder Road. An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Podar International School students in Mumbai is matched from the nearest workable corridor, never from a central pool.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches a home tutor to an RBK International Academy family in Mumbai
paragraphs: A request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor for RBK International Academy students in Mumbai usually arrives with three facts and one unstated one. The three facts are the year group, the subject and the evening the family is free. The unstated fact matters more: whether the child is behind on content, behind on technique, or behind on neither and simply rattled by the last report. Those are three different problems and they need three different tutors. A student who cannot yet balance a redox equation needs content taught again from the start. A student who can do every question in the textbook and still loses marks in a timed paper needs somebody who marks like an examiner and explains why a correct answer scored two out of four. A student who has gone quiet needs the subject broken into pieces small enough to finish one in an hour.

So the first conversation is a diagnostic one, not a scheduling one. We ask for the most recent report, the last two pieces of marked work and, if the school has issued them, the predicted or working grades. We ask what the school has already said, because a coordinator who has flagged an internal assessment deadline has usually told you the real problem in one line. We ask which subjects the child chose willingly and which were chosen for them, since motivation in a Year 11 Economics class a student resents is not a tutoring problem at all.

Only then do we look at availability. Shortlisting works backwards from the household: the slot you can actually protect week after week, the travel time from where tutors who teach that course live, and whether a second subject should be added now or in the next term. Families who ask for four subjects in week one almost always drop to two by week five, so we would rather start at two and build. Tutors are offered as a shortlist of two or three with their teaching background in your child's specific course, and you speak to them before anyone commits to a term.

sections.heading: Which course is your child actually entered for?
paragraphs: Establish this before you hire anybody. A school that runs both a Cambridge pathway and an International Baccalaureate (IB) pathway produces parents who describe their child as doing IGCSE when the registration says Middle Years Programme (MYP), or who say IB when they mean Year 10 Cambridge. The paperwork that settles it is the school's own: the subject registration slip, the examinations officer's entry confirmation, or the coordinator's email naming the course code. Ask for that in writing. A tutor briefed on the wrong programme will teach the wrong assessment style for a month before anyone notices, and that month is expensive in a two-year course.

The distinction is not cosmetic. In the Cambridge IGCSE years the shape of the work is a set of papers sat at the end, with coursework or alternative-to-practical components depending on the syllabus the school has chosen. In the IB Diploma Programme (DP) the shape is continuous: internal assessments running alongside teaching, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) decisions that change the depth of every unit. A child moving from Year 11 into DP1 is not continuing; they are starting a different kind of course with a different kind of deadline. Families who treat the transition as continuous are the ones who call us in October of DP1 sounding surprised.

There is a related trap in the middle years. Where a school runs MYP before the Diploma, the reporting language and the criteria are not the ones the Cambridge-trained tutor down the road knows. Where a school runs Cambridge Lower Secondary and then IGCSE, Year 9 is a genuine ramp and Year 10 is the year the habits set. Either way, an IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents hire in Year 9 is cheaper and calmer than one hired in the second term of Year 11, because the work in Year 9 is habit formation and the work in Year 11 is damage control. Home tuition started early is also easier to taper, which is the outcome you actually want.

Cambridge IGCSE: Core or Extended changes the grade range available
IB DP: HL and SL change depth, not just the number of hours
MYP criteria are not IGCSE grade descriptors; tutors must know which applies
A Year 11 to DP1 move is a change of course, not a continuation

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards and what an IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai has to hold in their head
paragraphs: Subject choice is where families at a dual-pathway school make the decisions they later pay for. The three recurring ones are Core against Extended in Cambridge Mathematics, Higher Level against Standard Level in the Diploma, and whether to carry a science the child dislikes because a university page somewhere mentioned it. A good home tutor is useful in all three conversations precisely because they have no stake in the timetable. They can tell you what the Extended paper demands in algebraic fluency that the Core paper does not, and whether your child is three months or three weeks away from that fluency.

Every subject on both boards carries work that is marked inside the school and counts towards the final result. In the sciences it is practical and investigative work. In Mathematics at Diploma level it is an exploration the student chooses. In the languages it is oral and written task work. In the humanities it is a research-based piece. The names and the structures differ by subject and the boards revise their subject guides on their own cycles, so do not take a weighting, a word count or a paper duration from a tutoring page, including this one. Get the current Cambridge or IB subject guide for the exact syllabus your child is entered for, or ask the school's examinations officer, and plan the term off that.

What a tutor can do without any ambiguity is teach the skill the component rewards. For an investigative science piece that is variable control, uncertainty and honest evaluation of a method that partly failed. For a Mathematics exploration it is choosing a question narrow enough to finish and mathematics the student can genuinely explain. For a language task it is structure and register under time pressure. For a humanities piece it is using a source rather than quoting it. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families engage for a single subject often ends up advising on the whole subject block, which is fine, as long as the advice stays with the school's coordinator as the decision maker. Among all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers, the scarce ones are predictable: Economics at HL, Business Management, Mandarin, Hindi at the higher levels, Computer Science and Physics at HL.
bullets: Core or Extended Mathematics decided on current fluency, not on ambition
HL and SL choices checked against the student's total deadline load

sections.heading: Where RBK International Academy families live across Mumbai
paragraphs: RBK International Academy sits at the northern end of the Western corridor, on the Mira Road side of the Mumbai metropolitan region, and that single geographic fact shapes every tutoring arrangement its families make. The daily catchment runs along the Western Line: Mira Road, Bhayandar, Dahisar, Borivali and Kandivali, with a thinner stream coming up the Western Express Highway from Malad and Goregaon. IB and IGCSE home tuition for RBK International Academy students in Mumbai works best when the tutor lives inside that same stretch, because a tutor who has to come north from Andheri at six in the evening is making a journey that is fine in September and unsustainable by January. The phrase IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai parents type into Google is the right instinct: proximity is what decides whether a weekly slot survives a whole year.

Across the rest of the city the pattern repeats with different roads. In South Mumbai, families in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar and Tardeo are served by tutors who stay on the island; eight kilometres from Worli to Colaba can still cost forty minutes once the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals back up, and the Coastal Road has changed the north-south run far more than it has changed the cross-island one. In the Western Suburbs, matching along the line beats matching across it: Khar West to Santacruz West is routine, Malad to Kandivali is routine, Bandra to Andheri at 6pm on the Western Express Highway is not. Metro Line 1 between Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 from Dahisar down to Gundavali have made some of these runs predictable in a way the road never was.

In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali hang off JVLR with no station of their own, so tutors reach Hiranandani Gardens by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road matters more there than the Central Line. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway puts South Mumbai within reach of Chembur faster than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is a set of nodes, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, linked by Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and the Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing without making a weekday evening tutor from Worli to Kharghar a sensible plan. Thane spreads from the station out along Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: twenty minutes to Kasarvadavali off-peak, close to an hour in the evening. The Bandra-Worli Sea Link and Metro Line 3 help the BKC-bound more than the suburb-to-suburb traveller. Home classes anywhere in Mumbai are a scheduling problem before they are a teaching problem, and we solve the scheduling first.

sections.heading: The RBK International Academy calendar and the months it squeezes
paragraphs: The school year at an international school in Mumbai, Maharashtra starts in June and ends in the spring, and the pressure does not arrive evenly. June and July are quiet enough that families postpone hiring, which is exactly when a tutor is most useful and most available. August and September bring the first unit assessments and the first real report, and that report is where most families discover a problem they could have seen in July. October and November carry the heaviest internal deadline load in the Diploma years and the first serious mock run in the Cambridge years. December is short and broken by the break. January and February are the months when nothing can be fixed slowly any more. March onwards belongs to the examination boards.

That rhythm has a practical consequence for anyone arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai. A tutor hired in June can work on foundations, which is cheap in hours and durable in effect. A tutor hired in January is being asked to do exam technique only, because there is no time for anything else, and the honest version of that conversation is that technique raises a mark somewhat and foundations raise it more. Families who hire twice, once for foundations and once for the run-up, usually get a better result from fewer total hours than families who hire late and buy intensity.

Use the school's own reporting rhythm as your trigger, not your own anxiety. Parent-teacher meetings, interim reports and the coordinator's deadline calendar tell you what the subject teacher already knows. Take that into the first tutoring session as evidence. A tutor who reads a teacher's comment about weak evaluation in a lab report knows what to do in week one; a tutor who is told the child is weak at Chemistry does not. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with RBK International Academy or with any other school named on this page, including Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Thakur International School in Kandivali East or Singapore International School in Dahisar East. We name them because Mumbai families recognise the calendars, not because we represent them, and we never name or approach individual teachers.

August and September: first reports expose the gap families suspected

sections.heading: Home tuition, online, or a mix for an RBK International Academy student?
paragraphs: Start with home tuition and change only if there is a reason. For a student in the Cambridge years, an IB and IGCSE home tutor for RBK International Academy students in Mumbai sitting at the same table is worth more than any software, because most of what goes wrong at that age is attention rather than understanding. A tutor in the room sees the page the student is avoiding, notices the phone face-down, and can take the pen and work a step by hand. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai also inherits a small amount of household authority that an online window never gets, which is why home classes survive a bad week better than video sessions do.

Online tuition earns its place in three situations and you should know which one you are in. The first is a scarce subject: if the right Economics HL or Mandarin teacher is in Pune rather than on the Western Line, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is a better tutor than a convenient local one. The second is a short, sharp intervention before a deadline, where two thirty-minute screen sessions beat one travelled hour. The third is monsoon weeks and examination weeks, when travel collapses and a session you can hold at short notice is worth more than the ideal one you cancel. The trade-offs are real: screen sessions suit a student who already works independently and punish one who does not, and they are poor for anything requiring a tutor to watch a student's hand move across a diagram.

Hybrid is what most families settle into by the second term without planning it. One travelled session a week carries the teaching and the relationship; one short online session carries homework review, a marked draft or a question set before a test. It also solves the January problem, when a tutor who normally reaches Mira Road in twenty minutes cannot, and the family would otherwise lose the week. Set the hybrid pattern deliberately at the start rather than drifting into it, and write down which session is the one that never moves. The home tutoring slot is almost always that one.

Online justified by subject scarcity, not by tutor convenience

sections.heading: How are tutors checked before they reach your building in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Every IB and IGCSE tutor for RBK International Academy students in Mumbai goes through the same four checks before a profile is shown to a family: identity against a government photo document, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, a reference from a previous tutoring or teaching engagement, and a subject conversation with somebody who knows the course. The subject conversation is the one that removes the most applicants. A graduate who knows Physics is not automatically someone who can teach a Diploma student to write an investigative report that scores, and the only way to find out is to ask them how they would mark a weak one.

Then there is what you should check yourself, in the first session and in the first month, because no platform check substitutes for a parent in the house. Ask the tutor which board and which level they have taught, and how recently. Ask them to name the components your child's subject carries; a tutor who has taught the course answers that in one breath. Ask what they will do in the first four sessions and what you should expect to see by session five. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or a fixed number of marks, because nobody can promise that and the offer tells you what kind of operation you are dealing with.

Practical checks matter as much as academic ones in Mumbai. A tutor who will be entering your building weekly should be comfortable with your society's visitor register and happy for you to record their phone number and identity details at the gate. Sessions should happen in a room a family member can walk through, not behind a closed door, and the tutor should expect that rather than resent it. Ask for a short written note after every few sessions; one honest paragraph about what was covered and what was weak is worth more than a monthly report nobody reads. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families eventually need is a person in their house every week, and that relationship deserves the same scrutiny as any other.

Ask which board, which level and how recently they taught it

sections.heading: Working alongside RBK International Academy teachers, never against them
paragraphs: The single most common way private tutoring fails a student at a school running both Cambridge and IB pathways is that the tutor sets up as a rival authority. It happens without malice. A tutor trained on one board teaches a method the school does not use, tells the student the school's approach is inefficient, and within three weeks the child is running two conflicting systems and trusting neither. The student then writes a hybrid answer that satisfies nobody, and the subject teacher, who marks the work that counts, sees a student who has stopped following instruction. IB and IGCSE home classes for RBK International Academy students in Mumbai are only useful when the tutor treats the school's method as the specification and their own preference as a private opinion.

In practice that means a few firm rules. The tutor works from the school's unit plan and the school's assessment criteria, not from a general syllabus found online. Where the school has shown a worked format for a lab report or a commentary, that format is the one practised, even if the tutor prefers another. Where the school has set a deadline, the tutor's plan works backwards from the school's date and not from a comfortable one. And where the student says the teacher wants something different, the tutor's answer is to follow the teacher and check the brief, never to override it.

There is a boundary on the other side too. A tutor does not contact the school, does not ask for marking schemes the school has not published, does not request meetings with staff and does not write to a coordinator on your behalf. If something needs to be raised with the school, you raise it as the parent, and the tutor's contribution is to help you ask a precise question: not that your child is struggling in Biology, but that your child is losing marks on evaluation in practical write-ups and you want to know what the department expects there. Schools answer precise questions well. They answer vague anxiety with reassurance, which helps nobody.

The same logic governs academic honesty, which at Diploma level is not a soft issue. A tutor coaches process: they ask questions, challenge a research question that is too broad, point at a paragraph that asserts rather than argues, and give feedback on the student's own draft. They do not write sentences, supply content, or hand over a structure the student has not reasoned out. If a tutor ever offers to draft a section, that is the moment to end the engagement, because the consequence of an authenticity problem lands on your child's result and not on the tutor.
bullets: School's unit plan and criteria are the specification, not the tutor's preference
Practise the format the subject teacher has actually shown the class
Plan backwards from the school's deadline, never from a comfortable one
The tutor never contacts the school; the parent asks a precise question
Feedback on the student's own draft only, never supplied content

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look at behaviour. Has the homework pile stopped growing? Does your child start the subject without an argument? Can they tell you what they are weak at in specific words rather than saying they are bad at the subject? Those three changes are the real four-week signal, and in our experience they arrive before any mark moves. If none of them has happened in four weeks of weekly home tuition, something is wrong with the match and you should say so rather than wait politely for the term to end.

At one term, marks should have moved on the kind of work the tutoring targeted, and you should be able to name the change. A student who was losing marks on method and evaluation in practical write-ups should now be losing them somewhere else, which is progress even if the overall grade is unchanged. A student doing Extended Mathematics should be finishing the paper rather than running out of time on the last two questions. If the grade has moved and nobody can explain why, treat that with the same suspicion as no movement at all, because an unexplained rise is usually a kind test rather than a learned skill.

At one exam cycle, the honest picture is that tutoring changes outcomes for most students by a meaningful amount and changes them for some students by very little. We do not guarantee grades and no reputable tutor will. The variables outside anyone's control are large: whether the student does the independent work between sessions, whether the subject was a poor fit from the start, whether the family's year contained something harder than school. What a good tutor reliably delivers is that the student knows what they know, has a method for the parts they find hard, and walks into the hall without panic. Where that produces two grades it is because the student did the work; where it produces half a grade, it was usually started in January.

The limits are worth stating plainly. Tutoring does not fix a wrong subject choice, and five hours a week of Chemistry a child should never have taken is five wasted hours. It does not fix attendance. It does not substitute for the school, and a student who has disengaged from the classroom entirely needs the school involved and probably needs more than a tutor. We would rather tell you that in week one than bill you for a term of it.
bullets: Four weeks: homework current, less resistance, specific self-diagnosis
One term: marks move on the targeted skill and the reason is nameable
An unexplained grade rise deserves the same scrutiny as no rise
Exam cycle: method and composure are deliverable, specific grades are not

sections.heading: Starting home classes for an RBK International Academy student in Mumbai
paragraphs: Prepare four things before the first session and it will be worth twice as much. The most recent school report, with the subject teacher comments and not just the grades. Two pieces of marked work, ideally one the student did well and one they did badly, because the gap between them is the diagnosis. The school's written confirmation of the course and level your child is entered for. And the deadline calendar for the term, including internal assessment dates if the coordinator has issued them.

The first session is a diagnosis, not a lesson, and a tutor who spends it teaching has skipped a step. Expect the tutor to work through a past question or a recent piece of marked work with your child, stopping at each point where the method breaks down, and to say out loud which of those breakdowns is content and which is technique. Expect them to ask your child what they want, because a fifteen-year-old who has an answer to that works differently from one who has been enrolled. Expect a plan within the week: what the first four sessions cover, what the student does between them, and what you should be able to see by session five.

We arrange all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai families ask about, though we would rather you began with two subjects than four. Set the practical frame at the same time. One fixed weekly slot that does not move, ideally not immediately after a long school day on a day with activities. A table in a room with a door that stays open. The student's own materials out before the tutor arrives, because ten minutes of hunting for a textbook is ten minutes you paid for. A standing arrangement at the society gate so the tutor is not re-registering as a new visitor every week. And one agreed point of contact in the family, so the tutor is not reporting to two people with different expectations.
bullets: Have the latest report with teacher comments ready, not only the grades
Bring one strong and one weak piece of marked work
Confirm the course and level in writing from the school office
First session diagnoses; expect a written plan within the week
Fix the slot, the room and the gate arrangement before week two

faqs.question: Do you place tutors who have taught the exact Cambridge and IB courses this school runs?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the filter we apply first. Before a profile reaches you, the tutor has had a subject conversation with somebody who knows the course, and they are asked which board, which level and how recently they taught it. A tutor who has only taught one board is shortlisted for that board's students and not the other. You can test this yourself in the first call by asking them to name the components your child's subject carries and describe how they would give feedback on a weak draft of one. A tutor who has actually taught the course answers without hedging.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Mira Road for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the way to make it last is to match within the corridor rather than across the city. Tutors living along the Western Line between Dahisar and Bhayandar reach Mira Road reliably on a weekday evening; a tutor coming north from Andheri or Bandra on the Western Express Highway at 6pm is making a journey that works in September and collapses by January. We would rather offer you the second-best tutor who lives twenty minutes away than the ideal one who will start cancelling. If the subject is scarce enough that nobody local teaches it, we will say so and propose a hybrid pattern instead.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor need from our flat before the first session?
faqs.answer: A table in a room where someone can walk through, good light, a plug point and no television in earshot. That is genuinely the whole list. Sessions should not happen behind a closed door, and a tutor who expects that rather than resents it is the kind you want. Have the student's own textbooks, notebook and calculator out before the tutor arrives, because ten minutes of hunting for materials is ten minutes you have paid for. If your building requires visitors to register, sort out a standing arrangement in the first week so the tutor is not treated as a new guest every time.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 10 and wants to move from Extended to Core Mathematics. Can a tutor advise?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give you the evidence, but the school makes the decision and should. What a tutor adds is an honest read on fluency: whether your daughter is three weeks or three months from the algebraic confidence the harder paper assumes, and whether the gap is content she never learned or practice she never did. Take that read to her Mathematics teacher and the coordinator, who know the class, the entry deadlines and what the move does to her options later. Ask the school for the current syllabus for the exact course she is entered for before anyone argues about grade ranges.

faqs.question: Will a tutor contradict what her teachers at school are telling her?
faqs.answer: They should not, and if they do, tell us. A tutor works from the school's unit plan, the school's assessment criteria and the format the subject teacher has shown the class, even where they personally prefer a different method. Two competing systems are worse than one imperfect one, because the student ends up writing a hybrid answer that satisfies neither and the teacher who marks the work sees someone ignoring instruction. Where your child reports that the teacher wants something different, the tutor's job is to follow the teacher and help you ask the school a precise question about it.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai actually depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and no honest page can quote you a number without them. The board and level, because a Higher Level Diploma subject with internal assessment supervision is not priced like a Year 9 subject. Subject scarcity, which is why Economics at HL, Mandarin and Physics at HL cost more than Mathematics everywhere. Travel distance and direction, since a tutor crossing the city in the evening peak is selling you two hours to teach one. Session length and frequency, where two shorter sessions often cost more than one long one and work better. And whether you need marked written feedback between sessions, which is real work and is charged as such.

faqs.question: Is online tuition good enough for IGCSE Chemistry when there is practical work?
faqs.answer: For the theory and the write-ups, yes. For the practical skills, partly. An online tutor can teach method design, variable control, uncertainty, data presentation and the evaluation paragraph that most students lose marks on, because all of that is thinking and writing. What a screen handles poorly is watching a student's hand move: setting up apparatus, reading a scale, noticing that they are recording to the wrong precision. If the school's course includes a practical component, use home classes for the laboratory thinking and the school's own sessions for the apparatus, and ask the school what it expects students to be able to do unsupervised.

faqs.question: We live in Borivali but she studies here. Which tutor would you send?
faqs.answer: One who lives or already teaches in the Borivali to Dahisar stretch, not one near the school. This surprises families, but the tutor comes to your home, so your address is the one that matters, not the campus. Borivali is well served because Metro Lines 2A and 7 and the Western Line both run through it, so a tutor from Kandivali East or Dahisar East reaches you predictably on a weekday evening. We also check the direction of travel, since a tutor who finishes a session in Malad at 6pm is coming towards you rather than against the flow.

faqs.question: Nothing has changed after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Tell us in that fourth week rather than at the end of term. First we check what was meant to change: at four weeks you should see homework current, less resistance to starting the subject, and your child describing their weakness in specific words. If none of that has happened, the usual causes are a mismatch of teaching style, a tutor working on content when the problem was technique, or a plan that was never written down. Sometimes the fix is a conversation and a revised plan. Often it is a different tutor, and we arrange that without asking you to restart the term.

faqs.question: How does replacing a tutor work without losing the rest of the term?
faqs.answer: You tell us, we take the handover off your hands. The outgoing tutor writes a short note on what was covered, what is still weak and where the student was heading, and the incoming tutor reads that before the first session so you are not paying for the same diagnosis twice. We shortlist again against what you have learned from the first attempt, which is usually more specific than your original request. The new tutor keeps your existing slot wherever possible, because the slot is the hardest part of the arrangement to rebuild once a family has lost the habit.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get a standing gate pass for our society in Bhayandar?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is worth doing in week one. Most societies in Bhayandar and Mira Road will register a weekly tuition visitor against a resident's authorisation once the secretary or the facility manager has the tutor's name, phone number and photo identity on file. Ask your committee what it needs rather than sending the tutor to argue at the gate. Fifteen minutes of paperwork removes a recurring ten-minute delay and the friction of a different guard each week. Record the tutor's details yourself at the same time; you want them on file regardless of what the society keeps.

We name schools because Mumbai families recognise their calendars and assessment rhythms, not because we represent them, and we do not approach or name individual teachers. sections.heading: IB and IGCSE programme structure across both Ryan Global School campuses in Mumbai
paragraphs: Ryan Global School is publicly listed with campuses including Kandivali and Worli in Mumbai, offering International Baccalaureate (IB) and IGCSE pathways. Exactly which programme runs in which year group at which campus is the school's own information and it does change, so confirm it at the school office rather than taking it from any tutoring website, including this one. A tutor only needs two facts from you: which programme your child is in this year, and which one they are heading into next.

On the IB side the structure is three stacked programmes. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is inquiry-led with no external examinations. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) assesses every subject against four published criteria, each marked out of eight, which is why an MYP report can show a child who is strong on Criterion A knowledge and weak on Criterion D reflection in the same subject. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year sixth-form qualification: six subjects drawn from the subject groups, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the core of Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity and service requirement.

On the IGCSE side the two awarding bodies families here meet are Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel. Cambridge splits many subjects into a Core tier and an Extended tier, and the tier decision made in Year 9 or Year 10 caps the grade available later, which makes it the single most consequential conversation of the IGCSE Years 9-11 block. Pearson Edexcel grades on the 9-1 scale and structures its papers differently, so a tutor who says IGCSE without naming the board and the syllabus code is guessing.

The two transition points are where most enquiries come from. The first is MYP Year 5 into DP1, where a child moves from criteria-based marking to raw marks and examiner mark schemes. The second is IGCSE Year 11 into DP1, where subject choice suddenly has to carry HL decisions. Finding someone who can genuinely teach all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 with one tutor in Mumbai is rare, and a parent is usually better served by one strong tutor in the subject that is actually failing plus a short block of help on the choice itself.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: where the marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Marks are rarely lost because a child does not know the content. They are lost on the structure of the assessment: the command word, the mark scheme's expected form of words, the internal assessment criterion that was never read properly, and the tier or level decision taken a year earlier. A tutor who starts by teaching the topic again from the beginning is solving the wrong problem and will burn a term doing it.

Every subject carries its own internal component and they are not interchangeable. DP Sciences carry a single Internal Assessment (IA) investigation assessed on criteria that reward a focused research question over an ambitious one. DP Mathematics carries an exploration that fails most often on personal engagement and mathematical communication rather than on the mathematics. DP English carries an individual oral tied to a global issue and two set texts. MYP subjects carry the Personal Project in the final year, which is assessed on process rather than product and which eats the same fortnight as everything else. On the IGCSE side, Cambridge Sciences carry either a laboratory paper or Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, and the two demand completely different preparation.

A worked example, since Paper 6 is where confident students quietly lose grades. A Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry Alternative to Practical question gives a table of three burette readings from a titration, one of which is nearly a full cubic centimetre away from the other two. The question asks which results should be used to calculate the mean, and why. There are separate marks for selecting the two concordant titres, for stating that the third is anomalous and excluding it for that reason, for the arithmetic, and for carrying the unit. A student who averages all three loses three of four marks while knowing the chemistry perfectly well. The follow-up part asks for one improvement to the method, where be more careful scores nothing and add the acid dropwise near the end point scores the mark. That is a two-session fix and it is worth more than a month of revisiting bonding.

Be sceptical of anyone offering to cover every subject. No single person teaches all IB and IGCSE subjects well, and any tutor in Mumbai who claims to is overselling. The honest pattern is one tutor for Mathematics, one for the Science that is wobbling, and occasional short-block help for a language or for TOK. IB Gram matches that way instead of selling a bundle, and will tell you when a subject is scarce enough that online is the realistic option.

paragraphs: Start with the island city. Distances in South Mumbai are short and the clock is still against you: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can lose forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. In practice tutors for Worli and Prabhadevi are drawn from inside the island, which means Lower Parel, Mahalaxmi, Dadar, Tardeo, Cuffe Parade and Colaba, with Bandra at the outer edge of workable.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school year, and the months when IB and IGCSE deadlines actually bite
paragraphs: International schools across Mumbai run a June to April year, and that single fact explains most of the panic calls IB Gram takes. The year opens inside the monsoon, which is also when evening travel is least reliable, so new home tuition slots agreed in June and July should be booked with an online fallback built in from the start. The first MYP criteria tasks and IGCSE unit tests land in late July and August, which is the first honest signal of where a child stands.

October brings the Diwali break, and the week after it is the most common starting point for tuition because the first real reports have landed. November and December are the first hard pressure point: IGCSE and DP mock examinations, DP1 students producing first IA drafts, and MYP students being pushed on the Personal Project at the same time. Late January and February are the second and sharper one, because DP2 final IA deadlines, the Extended Essay submission and the TOK essay all sit within a few weeks of each other, and a tutor booked in January is often booking into a queue.

March and April are IGCSE coursework, practical examinations and then the written examinations of the May session, which is the session the overwhelming majority of Mumbai candidates sit. A smaller number sit the November session, usually retakes or students who moved schools mid-cycle. Working backwards from May, the useful calendar is simple: diagnose by October, build technique from November to January, and spend February to April on past papers under timed conditions. A parent who starts in March is buying triage, and an honest tutor will say so rather than promise a transformation.

One more boundary worth stating since this page is built around a school name. IB Gram is independent and has no affiliation with Ryan Global School; nothing on this page reflects the school's own calendar, its internal assessment schedule or any information held by its staff. Families looking for an IB and IGCSE home tutor for Ryan Global School students in Mumbai are matched on the board, the year group and the campus, never on anything the school holds. What is described here is the ordinary shape of the IB and IGCSE year as it runs across Mumbai schools. Your child's actual deadline list comes from the school, and the right first step is to put that list in front of the tutor in session one.
