sections.heading: Why does DP Year 1 shock students who spent IGCSE at the same Mumbai school?
paragraphs: Because the building stays the same while the demand changes completely. A student who sat IGCSE at Thakur International School walks into DP1 through the same gate, past the same noticeboards, with the same friends, and meets criterion-referenced internal assessment, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Higher Level depth inside a single academic year. Continuity of campus hides a real discontinuity of demand, and it is the commonest reason parents in Kandivali East ask for help in October of DP1 rather than in June.

The four changes arrive together, which is the problem. Marking stops being a checklist: an IGCSE A often came from learning what a mark scheme accepts, while a DP criterion asks whether the method was justified and whether the evaluation is honest, so a student with no practice at that reads a middling band as unfair rather than as information. The Extended Essay is the first piece of independent research anybody has asked them for, with a supervisor, a research question of their own invention and a four-thousand-word limit, where IGCSE coursework arrived with a task sheet. Theory of Knowledge has no content to revise, which hurts the diligent students most, because revision has been their entire method since Year 9. Higher Level is not the same subject with more questions on the end; it brings extension topics and a different paper, and the step from Extended IGCSE Maths to Analysis and Approaches HL is the one families underestimate most reliably.

The fix is timing rather than intensity, and it belongs in Year 11. In January of Year 11, read the published assessment criteria for one likely DP subject with your child and let them notice that the descriptors describe judgements, not answers. In the gap between the last IGCSE paper and the first DP1 lesson, which is the cheapest preparation window in the whole two years because nothing is due, have them write one piece of four or five hundred words from a research question they invented, reference it properly, and carry uncertainties through one calculation end to end. That is perhaps six sessions of work, and it converts the DP1 shock into a nuisance. Parents often ask who the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is for this transition; the more useful question is whether the tutor has taught both boards and can show you, inside one session, the practical difference between a mark scheme and a criterion.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks, expect behaviour to change rather than grades. The markers that actually predict a good term are small ones: your child attempts homework before being asked twice, can say in their own words what a question or a criterion is looking for, starts a hard problem instead of waiting for the session, and brings a specific doubt rather than a general complaint. A good tutor will also have told you by week four what the real gap was, and it is frequently not the one you booked for. The Physics problem turns out to be algebra, the Economics problem turns out to be command terms, and the English problem turns out to be reading speed.

At one term, progress should be visible on school work and not only inside the sessions. A Year 11 student should be finishing an Extended structured paper inside the time allowed instead of running out before the last question. A DP1 student should have an IA draft with a method section that survives being questioned, and should be able to say which criterion their draft is weakest against and why. At one exam cycle grades do move, but they move in company: subject choice, attendance, the amount of independent work and whatever else happened that term all sit inside the same result. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and any tutor who does is guessing with your child's name on it.

The honest limits matter as much as the plan. A home tutor cannot repair a subject choice that was wrong at the start, and an HL that should have been SL will keep costing points through DP2 whatever happens in a weekly session. A tutor cannot attend school for your child, cannot write an internal assessment, and cannot compress two years of reading into the fortnight before the Theory of Knowledge essay is due. What a tutor can do is make the next task tractable and the standard visible, week after week, until the student can see it without help. If nothing has moved by week four, we change the plan or we change the tutor, and the written plan from the first match travels to the new one so your child does not start again.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have five things ready and the first session stops being an interview. The last school report with the teacher comments, not only the grades, because the comments usually say whether the problem is understanding or output. The subject list with each level written out: Core or Extended at IGCSE, Higher or Standard in the DP, and which Mathematics route. The school's assessment deadline sheet, which tells the tutor what to work on first instead of guessing. Two or three evening windows you can genuinely hold for a term rather than the ones you hope for. And the gate rule for your building, so the first visit does not stall at reception while your child waits upstairs.

The first session is a working session, not a test. A good tutor opens the task your child has due next, watches them attempt it, and stops at the first place the method breaks rather than at the first wrong answer. By the end there should be one page: what the gap is, what the next four weeks cover, what your child does between sessions, and what you should be able to see by week four. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai does not exist at DP level, so if you need several subjects, say so at the start and we schedule them back to back instead of scattering them through your week.

After that the pattern is deliberately dull. One standing weekly slot per subject, a review at four weeks against the written plan, and a louder conversation in the months the calendar makes hard: December, January and February. Families who want a single provider for all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai get a small coordinated team rather than one heroic person, arranged so the DP child and the IGCSE child are not both losing their Saturday. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Thakur International School, so what you are buying is tutoring and a plan, not access to anybody inside the school.

faqs.question: My child did IGCSE at the school and starts DP1 next term. What changes first?
faqs.answer: The marking changes first, before the content gets harder. In IGCSE your child learned to produce what a mark scheme accepts; in the DP, a lab report, an essay or an exploration is judged against criteria descriptors that reward justified design and honest evaluation. The second change is the volume of self-directed work, because the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the first internal assessment drafts all arrive inside twelve months. Most DP1 students who struggle are not weaker than they were in Year 11; they are being asked a different kind of question.

faqs.question: When should we start preparing for the IB Diploma Programme if my child is in Year 11 now?
faqs.answer: January of Year 11 lightly, then seriously in the June gap once the IGCSE papers are finished. Light work in January means reading the assessment criteria for one likely DP subject and writing one short piece from a research question your child chose. The June gap is the cheapest window in the two years because nothing is due: a handful of sessions on command terms, referencing and uncertainty handling puts a student ahead of a cohort that starts DP1 cold. Waiting until October of DP1 means learning the format during the first graded tasks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building inside Thakur Complex on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the internal layout is why. Buildings in the Thakur Complex area sit on short internal lanes, so a tutor already teaching in Kandivali East reaches you on foot or with a short auto ride instead of crossing the Western Express Highway. The practical limits are the slot band and the gate. Everyone wants 6pm to 9pm, so earlier slots go to the families who ask for them, and visitor protocol varies by society: tell us at matching whether your gate needs a name on a list, an app approval or a call to the flat.

faqs.question: We live in Borivali East. Will a tutor come that far for home tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes, Borivali East sits inside the normal travel radius for this corridor. Magathane and the lanes off the Western Express Highway are a short run from Kandivali East, and Metro Line 7 makes that trip predictable in a way the highway stops being after 6pm. The honest caveat is direction rather than distance: a tutor living in Borivali East or Kandivali East will hold a Borivali East slot for a full term, while a tutor travelling up from Andheri or Bandra tends to cancel by the second monsoon week. Ask where the tutor lives before you ask what they charge.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then scarcity, travel and session length. Higher Level DP subjects cost more than IGCSE Core work because the teaching pool is smaller and the preparation per session is longer. A subject with few qualified tutors in this city, such as Computer Science HL or a Group 2 language, prices differently from IGCSE Mathematics. Travel distance matters because a tutor crossing Mumbai loses an hour each way, and so does whether you want ninety-minute or two-hour sessions, one subject or four, and internal assessment support close to a deadline. IB Gram quotes per match rather than publishing a rate card.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work as well as home classes for a DP Chemistry internal assessment?
faqs.answer: For the internal assessment itself, online is often better than home classes. The work is a document: a research question, a method, a data table, an uncertainty treatment and an evaluation, and a shared screen with live annotation beats two people leaning over one laptop. Online is weaker at the earlier stage, when your child is still learning to handle apparatus and read a scale, and at the exam-technique stage, where a tutor wants to watch handwritten working appear. Most DP Chemistry families run home sessions through term and move online for the fortnight around the deadline.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after two sessions. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the tutor, with no debate about who was right. We ask one question first, because the answer changes the replacement: is the problem reliability, explanation or fit? A tutor who arrives late needs replacing with someone who lives closer. A tutor whose explanations do not land needs a different teaching style, not a better degree. A clash between a brisk tutor and a quiet fifteen-year-old is nobody's fault and is the easiest of the three to fix. The new tutor receives the written plan from the first match, so your child does not repeat the diagnostic.

faqs.question: There is no visible progress after a month. Should we change the tutor?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but you should ask for evidence this week. At four weeks the honest markers are behavioural: does your child attempt homework unprompted, can they say what a criterion is asking for, do they start a question instead of staring at it? If those are moving, grades usually follow within a term. If none of them have moved, something is wrong with the plan or the match, and we run a three-way conversation with you and the tutor before replacing anybody. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and one month is too early to judge a grade anyway.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, or only subjects?
faqs.answer: Both, inside the academic honesty rules the school and the International Baccalaureate enforce. A tutor can help your child narrow a vague Extended Essay topic into an answerable research question, build a reading plan, understand what the criteria actually reward and rehearse the supervisor meetings. For Theory of Knowledge, a tutor can work on choosing exhibition objects and on structuring an essay against a prescribed title. What a tutor must never do is write or rewrite any part of it. The EE and the TOK essay are submitted as your child's own work, and a tutor offering to draft them is a risk, not a shortcut.

faqs.question: Our society gate will not admit an unregistered visitor. How is that handled?
faqs.answer: It gets handled at matching, not at the gate on the first evening. Many societies in Kandivali East and Borivali East require the resident to register a visitor in an app, add a name to a list at the main gate, or take a call before entry. Tell us which applies and the tutor arrives with the right expectation and photo identity, and you register them once for a standing weekly slot instead of every week. Where a society refuses recurring visitors outright, the usual answers are the clubhouse study room or a hybrid pattern with some sessions online.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all IB and IGCSE subjects for two children in the same house?
faqs.answer: Usually no, and a tutor who says yes is telling you something useful. A request for all IB and IGCSE subjects needs more than one tutor in Mumbai as soon as DP Higher Level work is involved, because nobody teaches HL Physics and Language A English to the same standard. What does work is pairing: one tutor across Mathematics and the sciences for the IGCSE child, another for the DP child's two weakest subjects, scheduled back to back so your evening carries one disruption instead of two. For a Year 9 or Year 10 child, a single strong generalist is often the better answer.

We would rather send three names who can hold the slot for a full term than eight who read well in a list and collapse in October.

You then speak to the shortlist yourself, and we expect you to interrogate it. Ask each tutor the catchment question directly: which schools in the Juhu area do you currently teach, and what does your existing week actually look like? sections.heading: IGCSE Years 9-11 and the IB Diploma Programme side by side in Mumbai
paragraphs: Utpal Shanghvi Global School sits in Juhu, in the western suburbs of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and offers an IGCSE pathway followed by the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP). That is public information about the school and it is the only school-specific fact this page leans on. For a parent, the practical consequence is that your child will meet two assessment systems that reward completely different habits, and will switch between them at the end of Year 11 with roughly six weeks of summer in between.

IGCSE, run by Cambridge International Education, is modular in feel. Each subject is its own contract: a syllabus, two or three papers, a tier where one exists, and sometimes a coursework or practical component. A student can be genuinely strong in IGCSE Physics and genuinely weak in IGCSE English Literature without either affecting the other, and the fix for each is local to that subject. Searches for all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor level in Mumbai come mostly from Year 10 parents who have just seen that pattern in a report and want it addressed subject by subject.

The Diploma Programme is a package, and that is the part families underestimate. Six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the core: the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Points come from everywhere at once, the core can add or subtract from the total, and an unfinished TOK exhibition cannot be rescued by a strong Paper 2 in something else. A DP1 student is carrying six syllabi and two long-form pieces of writing on the same calendar, which is why DP tutoring is usually about sequencing before it is about content.

So when we match, we treat the two stages as different jobs. An IGCSE Year 10 request is normally one or two subjects, weekly, with a clear target component. A DP request is often one subject plus an hour of planning discipline, and the tutor who is right for the second is not automatically right for the first. An IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai who is excellent at Year 9 Maths foundations may not be the person you want reading an HL Economics internal assessment proposal.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Core or Extended, HL or SL, and the assessment attached to each
paragraphs: Most families arrive asking for help with a subject and leave having fixed a decision instead. The decisions that matter at this stage are three: which subjects to carry, whether to sit Core or Extended at IGCSE where a tier exists, and whether a subject goes HL or SL in the Diploma Programme. Each of those choices drags an internal assessment or a practical component along behind it, and a good tutor will tell you about the attachment before you commit.

The Core and Extended question is where parents most often take advice from the wrong source. Extended opens the higher grades and is the normal route for a child continuing to the Diploma Programme in a quantitative subject. Core is the right call for a student who will otherwise spend Year 11 drowning and still miss the boundary, and it is not a failure. The test is not ambition, it is whether the student can currently do the Extended-only topics without a tutor sitting next to them. A tutor who has taught both tiers can usually answer that inside two sessions by giving your child a tier-boundary topic and watching what happens.

Take the Alternative to Practical paper in IGCSE Chemistry, usually sat as Paper 6. A student who knows the content cold can still bleed marks across it, because the paper tests experimental literacy more than chemistry: reading a burette scale to the right precision, naming the control variable rather than describing it, explaining why a result is anomalous instead of circling it, drawing a line of best fit through a plot with one obvious outlier. A home tutor who has actually taught that paper does not begin by re-teaching rates of reaction. They put four past-paper tables in front of your child and work through where the mark is earned: the unit in the column heading, consistent decimal places, the word because in the explanation line. Three focused sessions on that tends to shift a grade more reliably than a term of general revision, and it is the fix Juhu parents ask us for most often in Year 11.

The Diploma Programme equivalent is the internal assessment, and the failure mode is earlier. A DP Chemistry investigation is lost at the research-question stage, not at the write-up, because a question with no measurable independent variable cannot score on analysis however neatly it is presented. The same is true of an HL History investigation with no usable sources in English, or a Maths exploration built on a dataset that has three points. The useful tutor is the one who reads the proposal in week two and says no, pick something you can actually vary, rather than the one who proofreads a finished draft in week nine.

sections.heading: Juhu, JVPD Scheme, Vile Parle West and Santacruz West: where Mumbai families book from
paragraphs: An IB and IGCSE home tutor for Utpal Shanghvi Global School students in Mumbai is almost always travelling within a tight square. The families who write to us live in Juhu itself, in JVPD Scheme, in Vile Parle West and in Santacruz West, and the lanes between those four are short. That is the whole advantage of this catchment and also its constraint: a tutor can hold four sessions a week inside it without ever touching a highway, which means the good ones fill up locally and never need to advertise further out.

The two stations that matter here are Vile Parle and Santacruz, both on the Western Line, and they define where a tutor who does not drive can realistically come from. A tutor living near Andheri or Khar Road reaches Vile Parle in minutes and walks or takes an auto into JVPD Scheme. The Western Express Highway is the road version of the same thing, with the caveat that the stretch past the airport approach in the evening peak is the reason a seven o clock slot is safer to promise than a six o clock one. Link Road is the alternative for anyone coming down from Malad or Goregaon, and the Bandra–Worli Sea Link only becomes relevant when the tutor is based in South Mumbai, which for a weekly Juhu slot is rarely sustainable.

Outside this square, IB Gram matches across Mumbai on the same logic, zone by zone. In South Mumbai we match within the island, Worli to Colaba or Cuffe Parade to Peddar Road, because the Coastal Road has helped the north-south run but the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals still eat an evening. In the Western Suburbs we match along the line rather than across it, Khar West to Santacruz West or Malad to Kandivali, using the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali are reached by road off JVLR because Powai has no station of its own, with Metro Line 1 and the SCLR carrying tutors in from Ghatkopar, Kanjurmarg and Andheri East. In the Eastern Suburbs we work Chembur, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund off the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, with the Eastern Freeway making Wadala and Chembur closer to town than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is matched node to node, Vashi to Nerul or Belapur to Kharghar and Panvel, along Palm Beach Road and the Sion–Panvel Highway; the Atal Setu has shortened the crossing but pulling a tutor over the creek for a weekday evening lesson still rarely survives a full term. Thane is its own market, where Ghodbunder Road sets the timetable and a tutor near the station reaches Kasarvadavali quickly off-peak and slowly at seven, with Pokhran Road and Majiwada in between. Metro Line 3 has changed how tutors reach BKC and Cuffe Parade, but none of that helps a Juhu parent: your match will come from within a few kilometres, which is exactly why the slot question comes before the subject question.

sections.heading: The Juhu catchment: strong schools drawing on one shared tutor pool
paragraphs: Within a short drive of Juhu you have Utpal Shanghvi Global School, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School. Named here purely as public local context: IB Gram has no relationship with any of them, is not affiliated with or endorsed by Utpal Shanghvi Global School, and we have no access to staff, materials, mark schemes or report data from any school. What we have is a tutor pool, and the thing nobody tells new parents is that it is one pool for the whole catchment rather than one pool per school.

That shared pool is the defining fact of tutoring here, and it works in your favour and against you at the same time. In your favour, because a tutor who teaches IGCSE Maths to families from three different Juhu schools has seen the same syllabus taught three ways and knows which topics the local cohorts tend to arrive shaky on. Against you, because the three schools run on broadly similar international calendars, so their internal deadlines and mock windows land in overlapping weeks. When demand spikes, it spikes for everyone at once, and a tutor with four committed families cannot absorb a fifth in the same fortnight.

Read the year through that lens. June and July are quiet and cheap in attention terms: tutors are rebuilding their week and will shape it around you. From late August the Diploma Programme internal assessment proposals and the first unit tests start arriving, and by late September the week is set. October and November bring mocks and the first serious round of IGCSE past-paper work. December and January are the hardest fortnight to find anyone, because DP2 internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay final drafts and IGCSE mock results all converge. February to April is exam-season triage, where you can usually only get what is left. May is the exam series itself.

The practical reading of all this is simple and slightly unromantic. The tutor you want in November is a tutor you contacted in June, and the reason is not scarcity of tutors in Mumbai generally but scarcity of tutors who can be in Juhu at seven on a Wednesday. Enquire in June and you are choosing from a tutor's blank week. Enquire in late August and you are choosing from what three other families in the same few lanes did not take.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a Juhu student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead option and for a Juhu family it is usually the right one. A tutor in the room can see the page, catch a wrong method in the second line rather than at the end of the answer, and stop a student quietly looking something up. The IB and IGCSE home tuition for Utpal Shanghvi Global School students in Mumbai that works best is a fixed weekly slot in the same room at the same hour, because the habit does more than the hour does. Short distances inside the catchment mean the tutor arrives unhurried and leaves on time, which matters more over twenty weeks than anyone expects.

The honest cost of home tuition is reach and rigidity. A home tutor can only hold so many slots in an evening, so the pool of people who can be at your building at your hour is smaller than the pool who can teach the subject well. If your child needs IB Higher Level Economics or a less common Diploma Programme subject, the local home-tuition pool may simply not contain that person, and insisting on home-only means accepting a weaker subject match. Travel also means a cancelled session is harder to reschedule, because the tutor has lost a journey as well as an hour.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai solves exactly that scarcity problem. Online opens the whole city and beyond, which for a scarce HL subject or a specific internal assessment review is the difference between a real specialist and a generalist. It also makes late and early slots workable, and makes a thirty-minute check-in before a deadline practical in a way that a home visit never is. Against it: screen attention is harder to hold for a Year 9 student, written working is slower to share unless you set up a document camera or a tablet, and a tired child at nine in the evening in front of a laptop learns less than the same child at seven at the table.

Hybrid is what most of our Juhu families settle into by the second term, and it is worth planning for rather than drifting into. One home session a week for the main subject, where the tutor sits with the working, plus an online session or a short online review for a second subject or for internal assessment feedback. Families searching for an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai often assume they must pick one mode and stay there. You do not. Asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai from one person is usually a mistake, while asking for one strong home subject plus online cover for the rest is usually the sensible shape.

sections.heading: What we check before a home tutor in Mumbai reaches your gate
paragraphs: Every IB and IGCSE tutor for Utpal Shanghvi Global School students in Mumbai goes through the same checks before a name reaches you, and none of those checks involve the school. IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with Utpal Shanghvi Global School, so nobody on our panel is presented as a current or former member of its staff, and we do not claim access to its materials or results. What we verify is ordinary and checkable: government photo identity, the degree or qualification they claim, teaching or tutoring history with contactable references, and the specific boards and levels they have actually taught rather than the ones they are willing to attempt.

The subject check is the part that filters hardest. A tutor saying they teach IGCSE Maths is asked to work through an Extended-tier question cold and explain the method as they would to a Year 10 student. A tutor offering Diploma Programme sciences is asked how they would respond to a weak internal assessment research question. Plenty of competent graduates do not clear that, and the gap is usually not knowledge but the ability to make a method visible to a fifteen-year-old. We also ask about their current week, because a tutor who already holds slots near your area is a far safer bet than one who will be learning your commute at your expense.

There is a second half to this and it is yours. Platform checks tell you a tutor is legitimate; only you can tell whether they are right for your child. In the first session, sit nearby for ten minutes, not the whole hour. Listen for whether the tutor is asking questions or delivering a lecture, whether your child is holding the pen, and whether the tutor started from what your child actually got wrong rather than from the top of the chapter. Ask at the end what the next three sessions will cover. A tutor who can answer that specifically has a plan; a tutor who says we will see how it goes does not yet have one.

Then do the things that are easy to skip. Confirm the name on the identity document matches the person at your door and keep the tutor on your society visitor record under their real name. Agree the slot, the cancellation rule and the payment interval in writing before the second session rather than after a dispute. And ask the catchment question once more: which other families in this area do you teach, and on which evenings? You are not being nosy, you are establishing whether your slot is embedded in a stable week or hanging off the edge of one.

sections.heading: Why does your neighbour's Juhu slot decide yours?
paragraphs: Because the tutor you want has a finite number of weekday evenings and your neighbour already took one. That is the whole mechanism, and it is more useful to a Juhu parent than any list of tutor credentials. Within a few kilometres of Utpal Shanghvi Global School there are several strong international schools, so the same tutors serve all of them, and the ones who are genuinely good are booked across the catchment rather than attached to a single school. You are not competing with the city for a tutor. You are competing with four or five families in neighbouring lanes for one of a tutor's four or five slots.

Follow the arithmetic of a working tutor's week and the behaviour makes sense. A home tutor doing a weekday evening in Juhu can realistically teach two families back to back, perhaps three if the buildings are close and the sessions are an hour. Over five weekdays, that is a ceiling, and most tutors deliberately keep it below the ceiling because a packed week collapses the moment one family reschedules. So the question that determines whether you can have a particular tutor is not how good is this tutor, it is which of their evenings is still unshaped. An IB or IGCSE tutor for Utpal Shanghvi Global School students in Mumbai with a free Wednesday is available to you in a way that an identically qualified tutor with a full Wednesday simply is not, and no amount of willingness on either side changes that.

This is also why the existing Juhu slot determines yours rather than the other way round. A tutor who already teaches a family in JVPD Scheme at five o clock can take you at half past six in Juhu because the journey is five minutes. The same tutor cannot take you at five, and cannot take a six o clock slot in Santacruz West either, because the sequence has to be geographically coherent. When you ask whether a tutor already works this area, you are really asking what shape their evening has, and a tutor who can describe that shape clearly is a tutor whose commitment to your slot will survive the term. One practical consequence: being flexible by thirty minutes often gets you a better tutor than being flexible about the subject.

And it is why a late-August enquiry loses to a June one. In June a tutor's September week is a blank sheet and your preference sets the pattern. By late August the pattern exists, built around whoever asked first, and you are being fitted into gaps. By the time internal assessment proposals and first unit tests land, the tutors who know this syllabus well in this catchment have no evenings left at the hours a school-age child can actually work, and what remains is either a nine o clock slot or an online compromise you did not want. If your child is going into Year 10 or DP1 and you already suspect you will want support by November, make the enquiry in June and book a fortnightly session you can scale up. Holding a slot costs far less than finding one in a hurry.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after a month of home tuition in Mumbai?
paragraphs: After four weeks you should see changed working, not a changed grade. Specifically: your child attempting the hard question instead of leaving it blank, showing a method where they previously wrote only an answer, and being able to say in one sentence what a question is asking for. If a tutor has been in your home four times and your child still cannot explain what they worked on last week, that is a fit problem and you should raise it now rather than at the end of term. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will promise one, which is exactly why the four-week signal has to be about behaviour.

At one term, roughly twelve to fourteen sessions, you should expect measurable movement on a defined component rather than across a whole subject. A student who was losing marks on IGCSE practical-style papers should be handling tables and graphs cleanly. A Diploma Programme student should have an internal assessment research question approved and data actually collected, not a plan to collect it. If the target was broad, nothing will look like it moved, which is a reason to agree one specific target with the tutor in the first session and write it down.

Across a full exam cycle the picture is honest and mixed. Some students move more than a grade, usually the ones whose problem was technique and timing rather than understanding. Some move half a grade and feel the difference mainly in how they walk into the hall. A few do not move, and the reasons are rarely mysterious: sessions missed through travel or illness, a subject chosen at the wrong tier or level in the first place, or a student who never did work between sessions. A tutor cannot fix a tier choice in March and should say so plainly in September instead.

Two limits worth stating before you commit. First, tutoring works on what happens between sessions; an hour a week with no independent practice produces very little, and the most useful thing a parent can enforce is not more tutoring but the forty minutes afterwards. Second, we have no insight into what any school does internally, so a tutor works from the published syllabus, past papers and your child's own returned work. That is enough to be genuinely useful, and claiming more would be dishonest. There are no guarantees in any of this, and anyone offering you one is selling something else.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful instead of exploratory, and all three are already in your house. Your child's last two pieces of returned marked work, the subject syllabus or course outline, and an honest sentence about where it goes wrong. Not the grade, the moment: she can do the calculation but cannot set up the equation, or he understands the chapter and then writes four lines in an eight-mark question. A tutor given that sentence starts working in the first twenty minutes. A tutor given only a grade spends the first session finding out what you already knew.

The first session itself should be diagnostic and should look slightly underwhelming. Expect the tutor to give your child work to do in front of them rather than to explain things at them, to stop at the first error and ask what happened there, and to spend the last ten minutes setting out what the next three sessions will cover and what your child will do in between. A single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is rarely the right answer, so expect to be told honestly if the second subject needs a different person rather than a stretched one.

On logistics, settle them before session one. Pick the room: a table with two chairs, the door open, no television in line of sight, and a plug within reach. Put the tutor on your society visitor list by name for a standing weekly slot so the gate does not become a ten-minute negotiation every week. Fix the hour and keep it, including through the week of a school event, because the slot you repeatedly move is the slot the tutor eventually gives to someone else in the catchment.

Then write to us with the board, the year, the subjects, your two workable evenings and your area. We come back with a small shortlist of tutors who already work the Juhu area and can hold your hour, with what they teach and when they are free. You speak to them, you run one trial session at home, and you tell us yes or next. If the fit is wrong after two sessions, say so and we re-match rather than asking you to persist with a tutor your child has stopped talking to.

Write one honest sentence about where the work goes wrong
Set the room: table, two chairs, plug, no television in view
Add the tutor to your society visitor list for a standing weekly slot

faqs.question: Do you have tutors who teach at Utpal Shanghvi Global School?
faqs.answer: No, and we would not say so if we did. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Utpal Shanghvi Global School, and we have no access to its staff, teaching materials, mark schemes, internal results or report data. Anyone claiming insider knowledge of a school is either mistaken or marketing. What our tutors do have is the published Cambridge International Education and International Baccalaureate syllabi, past papers, and your child's own returned work, which is genuinely enough to diagnose a problem and fix it. Judge a tutor on whether they can teach your child's actual weak component, not on a claimed connection to the school.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees depend on in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote you a number because the honest answer varies. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai move with the board and level, since Diploma Programme Higher Level work commands more than IGCSE Year 9; with subject scarcity, because fewer people teach HL Economics well than teach IGCSE Maths; with travel, since a tutor crossing the Western Express Highway in the evening peak is pricing an hour of road as well as an hour of teaching; with session length and frequency; and with whether you book a term or a session at a time. Inside the Juhu catchment travel is short, which usually works in your favour. We confirm the rate with you in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually come to our building in Juhu on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this catchment it is the normal arrangement rather than a favour. Juhu, JVPD Scheme, Vile Parle West and Santacruz West sit close enough together that a tutor can hold back-to-back home sessions without touching a highway, which is why home tuition holds up here better than in most of Mumbai. The practical constraint is the hour, not the address: the airport approach stretch of the Western Express Highway in the evening peak makes a seven o clock start safer to promise than six. Tell us your two workable evenings and we will only send you tutors whose existing week has room at those hours.

faqs.question: How does society gate access and the visitor pass work for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Set it up once, before the first session, and it never costs you time again. Most Juhu and JVPD Scheme buildings will register a recurring visitor if a resident gives the name, phone number and the standing day and hour at the office or on the society app. Do that rather than letting the tutor be logged as a fresh guest each week, because a ten-minute gate negotiation in a sixty-minute session is a sixth of the lesson. Ask your tutor for the name exactly as it appears on their identity document so the record matches. If your building requires police verification paperwork for recurring service visitors, tell us at the matching stage.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work, or is home tuition always better?
faqs.answer: Home is better for most IGCSE work; online is better for scarce subjects and deadline reviews. A tutor in the room catches a wrong method in the second line and can see whether your child is actually writing. But an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai gives you the whole city's pool, which matters when you need a specific Higher Level subject or someone to read an internal assessment proposal properly. Online also makes a short pre-deadline check-in practical. The honest requirement is a camera pointed at the page or a tablet your child writes on, otherwise the tutor is teaching blind. Most of our Juhu families end up hybrid: one home session, one online.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all IB and IGCSE subjects for my child?
faqs.answer: Up to Year 9, often yes; from Year 10 onwards, usually not, and you should be suspicious of anyone who says otherwise. Families ask for an all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Mumbai because one person is simpler to schedule and pay, and for Years 7 to 9 a strong generalist genuinely can hold Maths and Science together. Once IGCSE tiering and component work begin, and certainly in the Diploma Programme, the depth required per subject outgrows one person. The better structure is one home tutor for the subject that needs eyes on the working, plus a specialist online for the second subject. We will tell you which split your request needs.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and we re-match at no extra cost rather than asking you to persist. Say it after two sessions, not at the end of term, because the signals are visible early: your child cannot explain what was covered, the tutor talks for most of the hour, or sessions keep moving. Be specific about what is wrong, since a mismatch of pace is a different problem from a mismatch of subject depth and leads to a different replacement. We also ask the tutor for their read, which is sometimes useful and occasionally tells you the work between sessions is not happening. Changing tutors twice in a term is a last resort, not a plan.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: First check what you are measuring, because a grade will not have moved in four weeks and was never going to. Look instead for attempted hard questions, visible method and your child being able to say what last week covered. If none of those changed, hold a three-way conversation: you, the tutor, and one specific written target for the next month. If that target is also missed, the problem is the fit or the diagnosis and we will re-match. Occasionally the answer is uncomfortable and nothing to do with the tutor, such as a subject sitting at the wrong tier or level. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor who promises one in month two is not being straight with you.

faqs.question: When should we book for the academic year?
faqs.answer: June or early July, well before you think you need it. In June a tutor's September week is unshaped and your preferred evening sets the pattern; by late August that week is already built around whoever enquired first, and you are being fitted into leftover hours. Because several strong schools sit within a few kilometres of Juhu, the same tutors serve all of them and the good ones fill locally and fast. From late August the Diploma Programme internal assessment proposals and first unit tests arrive together, and December to January is the hardest fortnight of the year to find anyone. Booking a fortnightly slot in June and scaling it up later is cheaper than hunting in October.

faqs.question: Do we cover Santacruz West and Vile Parle West as well as Juhu?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we treat the four areas as one catchment because tutors do. Juhu, JVPD Scheme, Vile Parle West and Santacruz West are close enough that a tutor can hold sessions in two of them on the same evening, and Vile Parle and Santacruz stations on the Western Line mean a tutor who does not drive can still reach you. A search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai from any of these four addresses draws on the same pool, so when you ask us for a tutor, the relevant question is which of these lanes they are already teaching in and on which day.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole hour, and for a teenager it is usually better if you are not. Be in the house for the first session and sit nearby for ten minutes, long enough to hear whether the tutor is asking questions or lecturing and whether your child is holding the pen. After that, an adult at home is sensible for a school-age child but hovering is counterproductive. Keep the session in a shared room with the door open rather than a bedroom, make sure the table has two chairs and a plug within reach, and take the five minutes at the end when the tutor says what comes next.

faqs.question: Should my child take Core or Extended at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Extended if they are continuing to the Diploma Programme in that subject and can currently handle Extended-only topics without someone sitting beside them; Core if Year 11 would otherwise be a year of drowning for a grade they will still miss. Core is a legitimate choice, not a surrender, and switching down late in Year 11 is far more damaging than deciding early. A tutor who has taught both tiers can usually read this in two sessions by giving your child a tier-boundary topic cold and watching what happens. Parents often search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai when what they actually need first is this decision made honestly.

You speak to them, run one trial session at home, then confirm or ask us to re-match. Enquire in June and you choose your slot; enquire in October and you take what is left.

sections.heading: Which campus, which stream: the first two questions we ask in Mumbai
paragraphs: A school group with locations in different parts of the city creates a problem no other type of request has. Two families can send an identical message asking for an IB IGCSE tutor for VIBGYOR High International students in Mumbai, and the right answer for one of them is a tutor in Kandivali while the right answer for the other is a tutor in Airoli. So the first reply is never a profile. It is three questions: which campus, which stream, and where do you live. The third one decides the shortlist, because the tutor comes to your flat rather than to the school gate, and a family in Borivali and a family in Mulund attending the same school group need entirely different people.

The second layer is the stream question, and parents are sometimes vague about it in a way that costs a fortnight. A school running an Indian board alongside a Cambridge or International Baccalaureate pathway has children in the same building sitting completely different assessments. A tutor booked for Class 10 when the child is in fact registered for IGCSE will teach the wrong question style, the wrong command words and the wrong mark scheme, and everyone will be polite about it for three weeks. Check the stream on the registration paperwork, not from memory, and send us exactly what it says.

After that the process is short on purpose. We put forward three tutors and write against each one why they are there and what the catch is: travel, availability, a thinner record at Higher Level. You telephone them yourself before anyone is given a gate pass. Then one paid first session with a single instruction given in advance, which is to read the most recent marked work and come back with the error pattern rather than a lesson. The answer we want to hear is specific. She can state Newton's third law and cannot identify the pair of forces in a question she has not seen before is a diagnosis. Needs to revise more is not.

Two disclosures before anything is booked, because they shape what we can honestly promise. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with VIBGYOR High, with any of its campuses, or with any other school named on this page. And we do not guarantee grades. Our accountability is over the quality of the shortlist and the speed of a replacement, not over an examination result that depends mostly on what the student does in the hours nobody is watching.

sections.heading: Moving into the international stream: what actually changes?
paragraphs: Three things change at once, and only the first is about content. The question style changes: the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) asks for applied reasoning in unfamiliar contexts rather than reproduction of taught material, so a student used to scoring well by learning answers suddenly finds her method does not travel. The mark scheme becomes visible and specific, with command words that mean particular things, where describe, explain, evaluate and justify each earn marks differently. And coursework or practical components start carrying real weight, which means part of the result is produced at a desk over weeks rather than in a hall over hours.

Then come the levels. IGCSE offers Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, and the tier a student is entered for sets the ceiling on the grade available, which is a decision with consequences two years out. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) that follows asks for six subjects split between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and a creativity, activity and service strand. Students arriving from a Middle Years Programme (MYP) background have met criteria-based grading already; students arriving from an Indian board usually have not, and that gap is the single most common reason a strong student has a weak first term.

Nobody speaks the way a search box does, but the request arrives phrased like this anyway: all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai parents want before the next report. Underneath it is a reasonable instinct. In Years 9 and 10 one capable tutor really can hold several subjects together, because what the child needs is study method, mark-scheme literacy and the confidence to attempt an unfamiliar question. By Year 11, and certainly in the Diploma Programme, one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is a fantasy, and a tutor who claims it is telling you what you want to hear.

A caution about structure that applies to every page like this one. Do not plan from paper counts, component weights, durations or mark totals quoted on a tutoring site. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel revise syllabuses on their own schedules and the IB reissues subject guides by cohort, so what was true for a student who sat the exam two years ago may be wrong for yours. The current subject guide for your child's registered syllabus is the authority, and the school's examinations officer or Diploma Programme coordinator can confirm what applies to that cohort.
bullets: Command words carry specific mark-scheme meanings and have to be taught
The Core or Extended entry decision sets the ceiling on the grade

Students from an Indian board meet criteria-based grading for the first time

sections.heading: Subject by subject: where an hour a week pays off most
paragraphs: The return on a weekly session is not the same across subjects, and knowing where it is highest saves families real money. Mathematics gives the fastest return, because the weaknesses are usually identifiable and finite: a student who cannot handle indices, surds or rearrangement is losing marks in every topic that builds on them, and three or four focused sessions close that properly. Physics gives a slower but larger return, since the work is teaching a student to apply a small number of principles to situations she has never seen, which is a habit rather than a fact. Chemistry rewards precision, and much of the lost mark total is notation, state symbols and units rather than chemistry.

Biology behaves differently and parents often misjudge it. The content volume is large and the terminology must be exact, so the useful tutor hour is partly a testing hour: closed-book recall, then correction, then recall again. Pure explanation feels productive and changes very little. In the Diploma Programme the investigation adds a second job, since a student has to defend a research question, control what needs controlling and discuss uncertainty honestly, and a weak question chosen in month one caps the mark no matter how good the write-up is.

The written subjects are where families wait too long. English, History, Economics, Business Management and the language courses are marked on how an argument is constructed from evidence, and that improves over months. A student who writes everything she knows about a topic and scores poorly has a structure problem, not a knowledge problem, and the fix is repeated short pieces with specific feedback rather than more reading. This is also where all IB and IGCSE subjects one tutor in Mumbai claims to cover tends to fall apart, because a strong mathematics tutor marking an essay gives encouragement rather than criteria.

So the sensible shape for most families is narrower than they expect. Pick the one subject where the marks are furthest below what the child is capable of, and put the weekly home session there. Add a second subject only if the first is stable. Where the real problem is spread across everything, the diagnosis is usually organisation, and a short block of work on planning, revision schedules and how to read a mark scheme does more than four subject tutors. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families keep for two years is almost always doing this kind of narrow, boring, repeatable work.
bullets: Mathematics gives the quickest return because the gaps are identifiable
Chemistry marks are often lost to notation, units and state symbols
Biology hours should be recall testing, not explanation
Written subjects need months, so start them before the mock season
One weak subject at a time beats four tutors and no free evenings

sections.heading: A school in several parts of Mumbai means several tutor pools
paragraphs: Finding an IB IGCSE home tutor for VIBGYOR High International students in Mumbai is really six separate searches, because Mumbai, Maharashtra is not one labour market for tutors. Start with the Western Suburbs, where the demand is heaviest. Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali, Dahisar, Andheri West, Juhu and Khar West sit in a single corridor served by the Western Line, the Western Express Highway, Link Road and Metro Lines 2A and 7 running down from Dahisar to Gundavali, with Metro Line 1 cutting east from Versova through Andheri. Matching within two or three stations of each other works. Malad to Borivali is nothing. Dahisar to Khar West on a weekday evening is a slot that will be renegotiated by the fourth week.

Thane is the second pool and it is more self-contained than people assume. From the station the city runs out through Majiwada and Pokhran Road to Ghodbunder Road, and the Ghodbunder stretch is the scheduling variable: twenty minutes to Kasarvadavali when the road is clear, close to an hour in the evening peak. Thane tutors cover Thane, with the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway linking them to Mulund and Bhandup, and the Thane to Borivali tunnel corridor gradually changing what is possible westward. Navi Mumbai is the third, organised in nodes: Airoli, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, connected by the Trans-Harbour Line, the Harbour Line, Palm Beach Road, the Sion-Panvel Highway, the Belapur to Pendhar metro and now the Atal Setu. Airoli families are closer to Mulund and Thane than to the rest of Navi Mumbai, which is useful to know when the specialist you want lives in the wrong node.

The Central Suburbs and the Eastern Suburbs behave as one catchment for scheduling purposes even though they are separate zones on paper. Kurla, Ghatkopar, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund sit on the Central Line, with Powai and Chandivali off the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road and no station of their own, while Chembur, Govandi, Mankhurd and Wadala run along the Harbour Line with the Monorail joining Chembur to Wadala. The Santacruz-Chembur Link Road is the single connection that makes an east-to-west match viable at all, and the Eastern Freeway makes the island reachable from Chembur far faster than the distance implies.

South Mumbai is the last pool and the most closed. Marine Lines, Churchgate, Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Tardeo, Walkeshwar and Worli are served by the Western Line out of Churchgate, the Harbour Line, Metro Line 3 up to Bandra Kurla Complex and the Coastal Road, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link connects the island to the western corridor. Distances here are short and journeys are not: the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals turn eight kilometres into forty minutes at the wrong hour. A family in Marine Lines should expect a tutor from the island rather than one driving down from Goregaon, and the exceptions are weekend mornings.

sections.heading: How does the Mumbai school year decide when to hire a tutor?
paragraphs: It decides it almost completely, and the good moment is earlier than most families act. Mumbai's international schools share a broad rhythm: a start after the summer break, a settling period through the monsoon, a first substantial reporting point in the autumn term, mock examinations in the cooler months, coursework deadlines in the early part of the calendar year, and the May examination session. The autumn report is the signal. A family that moves on it has a choice of tutors and a choice of evenings. A family that waits until the mock results are back is hiring in the one month when every competent Higher Level tutor in their corridor is already committed.

Campus location changes the pressure in a way parents rarely connect to academics. A child who spends ninety minutes a day on the Western Express Highway or Ghodbunder Road has ninety fewer minutes of usable evening than a classmate who walks home, and the two cannot sustain the same tuition timetable. When we are told the campus and the home locality, part of what we are calculating is how much evening is actually left. A seven o'clock slot for a child who gets in at half past six is a slot she will attend exhausted, and a Saturday morning session she is awake for is worth more than two weekday hours she sleeps through.

The other calendar worth planning around is the examination series itself. A student sitting the November session rather than May has a completely inverted year, with revision running through the monsoon and results arriving in the new year, and a tutor who has only ever worked to the May cycle will pace the preparation wrongly. Families retaking a paper in a later series need the same thought: the useful plan starts from the component being retaken and works backwards from its date, not from the school's general timetable. Other Mumbai schools in the same corridors, such as JBCN International School, Borivali, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Billabong High International School and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, follow broadly similar rhythms, which is why tutors in these corridors tend to know both boards.

What we do not know is your school's actual dates, and no tutoring platform should pretend otherwise. IB Gram has no affiliation with VIBGYOR High or any campus of it, no access to internal deadlines and no sight of any teacher's marking. Reporting dates, mock windows and coursework deadlines move between cohorts and between campuses. Ask the school office for the current calendar, mark the three pressure windows on your own, and hire backwards from them instead of reacting after each report card.

sections.heading: Home tuition in Mumbai, online, or a mix of the two?
paragraphs: Start with home and move online only where there is a reason. Most parents searching for an IB IGCSE home tutor for VIBGYOR High International students in Mumbai have already decided this, and they are usually right for Years 9 to 11. A tutor at the table sees the exercise book, notices the questions quietly left blank, and cannot be reduced to a muted tab. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai also protects the hour from the rest of the household in a way a screen does not. For a child who is avoiding a subject rather than failing to understand it, physical presence is the entire intervention.

The costs of an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai arrangement are travel and fragility. One route, one slot, one person, and a single blocked road removes the session with no fallback. Travel also narrows your choice invisibly: insist on a tutor who can reach Dahisar by seven and you have excluded most of the city's Higher Level specialists before you start. All IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes Mumbai families manage to sustain for two full years are, with very few exceptions, arranged inside a short radius.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is the right answer in three cases. Scarce subjects first, since Higher Level Economics, Psychology, Computer Science, Global Politics and the less common languages do not have a specialist in every suburb and a confident generalist does measurable damage at that level. Frequency second, because short, repeated contact in the fortnight before a mock is more valuable than one long weekly session and nobody will travel four times. Written feedback third: marking a draft on a shared screen, with the criteria open alongside it, is genuinely better than two people reading one printed page. What online needs in return is a student who stays engaged without supervision, and many fifteen-year-olds do not.

The arrangement that holds longest is hybrid, and it is worth setting up deliberately in the first month rather than drifting into it. One home session a week carries accountability, agenda-setting and the reading of body language that a camera loses. One or two short online sessions carry drilling, doubt-clearing and draft review. During mock season the online half expands without adding a single journey. Through the monsoon, an agreement that a rained-off session moves online the same evening is the difference between losing one hour and losing a fortnight.
bullets: Home sessions work because presence removes the option of avoidance
Insisting on a short commute quietly excludes most Higher Level specialists
Online is how a thin-subject specialist becomes reachable at all
Short repeated online contact beats one long session near a mock
Set the hybrid split and the wet-weather rule in month one

sections.heading: Who is standing at your door, and what has been checked?
paragraphs: Identity first, because it is the check with the worst downside if it is skipped. Every IB IGCSE tutor for VIBGYOR High International students in Mumbai who reaches a shortlist has had government photo identification matched against the name and contact number on file, and has confirmed in writing that they will attend personally. Sending an unannounced substitute into a family's home is not a scheduling lapse, it is a safety issue, and it removes a tutor from the platform rather than starting a discussion. If someone you did not speak to arrives at your door, do not admit them and tell us the same day.

The second check is competence, and it is narrower than a qualification list. We ask a tutor to name the components of the subject they want to teach, describe how its internally assessed work is marked, and say what students most often lose marks for. Somebody who has recently prepared candidates answers immediately and in detail. Somebody who has read a syllabus summary moves the conversation to their degree. A tutor who says IB Mathematics without being able to separate Analysis and Approaches from Applications and Interpretation has not taught the Diploma Programme lately, whatever the certificate says.

The third check is yours, and it happens in the first session. Stay in earshot. Listen for whether the child is doing the work or watching it being done, because a tutor who solves everything on the page produces a comfortable hour and no learning. At the end, ask what the child must do alone before next week, then check whether it was done. Be wary of anyone who promises a guaranteed grade on a first call, since no honest tutor offers a guaranteed result before reading a single script. We do not guarantee grades. A reachable target with conditions attached, given after three or four sessions, is what a competent tutor provides instead.

The final boundary is coursework, and it needs stating because the pressure to cross it is real. A tutor may teach the research skills an Internal Assessment requires, explain the criteria in ordinary language, and tell a student plainly that her analysis does not support her conclusion. A tutor may not design the investigation, provide data, or rewrite her sentences. Internally assessed work is submitted under an authenticity declaration that the student signs, and the consequences of a breach fall on her and on her diploma. A tutor who is relaxed about that line is not being helpful.
bullets: Photo identification matched to the name and number, with personal attendance confirmed
Turn away anyone you did not speak to, and report it the same day
Ask for components, marking criteria and the commonest lost marks
Watch session one for whether the child works or watches
Drafts may be read and criticised; they may not be written

sections.heading: What a home tutor should never do to a child's school work
paragraphs: There are four ways a well-intentioned tutor damages a student at a school with a strong department, and all four are avoidable. The first is teaching a competing method. A child holding two procedures for the same operation trusts neither, blends them under pressure, and loses marks for steps her department expects written out. The rule is that the tutor teaches inside the school's notation and sequence, and any neater approach waits until the examinable one is secure. The second is replacing the school's resources with a personal set of notes, which leaves a student revising two incomplete versions of one topic instead of one complete version.

The third is contradicting the teacher in front of the child. If a mark looks harsh, the correct move is to open the published criteria with the student and help her write a short, polite question for her teacher. It is never to announce that the department is wrong. Students repeat what tutors say, and a child who believes her teacher is incompetent has damaged the relationship that determines her predicted grade, her coursework supervision and the reference that goes with her applications. A tutor has an hour a week. The teacher has the year.

The fourth, and the most consequential, is doing the work. It arrives disguised as kindness: a deadline tomorrow, a panicking child, a draft that could be fixed in twenty minutes. A tutor who fixes it has taught the student that panic produces rescue, and has put an authenticity declaration at risk. The honest version is harder and better: submit the weaker version, read the feedback, and build the next piece properly with more time. Families should tell a home tutor out loud, in the first session, that they want this boundary held even when it is inconvenient, because a tutor under pressure from a parent is far more likely to cross it.

What is left after those four exclusions is the work worth paying for. Closing a foundation gap the class cannot stop for, such as a student who never learnt to rearrange an equation and has been compensating since Year 8. Supervised silent practice under timed conditions, with an adult reading over her shoulder, which households almost never manage alone. Pressing on a vague Internal Assessment research question until it becomes answerable with data the student can actually collect. And teaching a child to read her own mark scheme, which is the most transferable skill either board offers and the one almost nobody is taught directly.
bullets: No competing method; teach inside the school's notation and sequence
Annotate the school's resources rather than issuing a parallel note set
Marking disputes go to the teacher through the student, criteria in hand
Never fix a draft under deadline pressure, however kind it feels
Spend the hour on gaps, timed practice and mark-scheme literacy

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one exam series: the realistic timeline
paragraphs: At four weeks, measure the approach rather than the marks. The things that should have shifted are observable without a report card. She starts the question she cannot immediately see through, instead of turning the page. She arrives with her own doubts written down. She describes her last mistake as a method error rather than as carelessness. She knows what the command word in a question is asking her to produce. On the tutor's side, there should be a one-sentence statement of the weakness that a third party could act on. If after a month nobody can produce that sentence, the diagnosis never happened and a second month will not supply it.

At one term, school assessment marks should begin to move, with coursework moving first because a draft responds directly to feedback. Calculation subjects follow, on the condition that the practice between sessions is genuinely happening. Written subjects are the slowest, since building an argument from evidence is a skill measured in months. The size of the movement also depends on where the student started. A child well below the pass line usually shows the largest visible jump. A child already sitting mid-range is doing finer work to climb a band, and a flat term for her can still be progress that shows up in the next series.

Across a full examination series you learn what was real. Some things do not improve on any schedule, and saying so is part of the job. A student who does nothing between sessions will plateau, because an hour or two a week cannot carry a two-year syllabus on its own. A Higher Level subject chosen for family reasons stays heavy whoever teaches it. A child with six subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, a competitive sport and a long daily commute has a shortage of hours rather than a shortage of teaching, and buying more lessons for that week makes it worse.

We do not guarantee grades and we will tell you when tutoring is the wrong purchase. Where the obstacle is organisation, a short block on planning and revision method beats a year of subject sessions. Where every subject is slipping at once, the conversation belongs with the school about learning support. Where a level or a subject choice was a mistake, changing it in the first term costs a fraction of what two years of compensation costs. A platform that answers every problem with more hours is selling, not advising.
bullets: Week four: attempts hard questions, brings her own doubts, reads command words
A one-sentence diagnosis the tutor can state, or there was no diagnosis
Coursework moves first, calculation second, written argument last
Mid-range students climb more slowly than students who were failing
Time shortages need commitments dropped, not lessons added

sections.heading: Your first home tuition session in Mumbai: what to prepare
paragraphs: Send five lines and the shortlist gets much better. The campus. The stream and year group as the registration paperwork writes them. The subject and, for the Diploma Programme, the level. Your locality with a nearby landmark. And two or three time windows that survive the drive home. Travel is the first filter for an IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai, so the locality line matters more than the subject line. If a report card or a marked paper exists, attach it, because the teacher's own sentence about what is going wrong replaces an hour of our questions.

Have four things physically ready for the first session: the school exercise book, the last two marked assessments, the textbook or resource the department uses, and a cleared table away from the television. Agree in advance that the hour is a diagnosis rather than a lesson. What should come out of it is a description of the error pattern, a target that is actually reachable, and a plan for the next four weeks specific enough that you could explain it to someone else. A pleasant hour of general revision has told you nothing and should be treated as a failed first session, not a good start.

Then handle the household details in the same week, because these are what wear a good match down. Get the tutor registered at your society office so entry does not cost fifteen minutes every time. Settle where the session happens and keep it free. Put the slot in the family calendar as fixed rather than negotiable. Decide what happens when the roads flood. And agree the reporting format, even if it is three lines on a message after each session saying what was covered, what was set and what is still weak.

A phrase such as best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai returns directories rather than answers, and a search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai is closer to the right instinct than it looks, because proximity is what makes a tutor reliable in February. The tutor you want lives close enough that the journey is boring, teaches your child's exact syllabus, and said clearly on the first call what they would not take on. If the person you choose turns out not to be that, tell us precisely what went wrong and we re-match within the week where the subject allows it.
