faqs.question: Which campus my child attends: does it change who can teach her at home?
faqs.answer: It changes the timing rather than the tutor pool, and both matter. The tutor travels to your home, not to the school, so where you live sets the shortlist. What the campus determines is how much evening your child has left: a student commuting along Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway arrives home far later than one who walks, and a seven o'clock slot that works for one family is useless for the other. Send us the campus and the home locality together, because the gap between the two is what we are really scheduling around.

faqs.question: How should we compare IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai between two tutors?
faqs.answer: Compare on five dimensions instead of one number, or the cheaper quote will quietly be the worse value. Board and level, since Diploma Programme Higher Level work commands more than IGCSE Core because fewer people can mark against current criteria. Subject scarcity, which is why a Higher Level Psychology specialist costs more than an equally experienced Mathematics tutor. Travel distance and hour of day, the largest single variable in this city. Session length and frequency. And format, because online removes travel from the equation. Also ask what is included: written feedback between sessions and draft marking are real work and not every quote covers them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor park at our society, and does that delay the start of a session?
faqs.answer: It delays it every single week if you do not deal with it in advance, and it is one of the commonest reasons an hour becomes forty minutes. Ask your society office whether visitor parking is available for a regular weekly visitor or whether the tutor should come by train, metro or auto instead. Many Mumbai societies will register a recurring visitor and issue a standing pass once a resident puts the request in writing, which also removes the argument at the gate. Give the tutor the name exactly as it appears on their identification so the register matches, and confirm the entry route before the first visit.

faqs.question: My son is moving from an Indian board into the international stream. What hits him first?
faqs.answer: The question style, within about three weeks. Students arriving from an Indian board are usually well drilled on content and unprepared for questions that apply a principle to an unfamiliar scenario, so marks drop even though knowledge has not. The second shock is command words, where describe, explain, evaluate and justify earn marks in specific ways that nobody has previously made explicit. The third is coursework, which is self-managed over weeks rather than delivered in a hall. A good tutor spends the first month on mark-scheme literacy rather than on content, which feels counterintuitive to parents and is the right sequence.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to teach at the same campus my child attends?
faqs.answer: No, and in most cases they should not. A tutor working at your child's own school creates an obvious conflict if they also teach or assess in that department, and no tutor should ever be in a position to see assessments your child will sit. What you want instead is someone who teaches the same syllabus, knows how it is marked and has recently prepared candidates for the components in question. Ask about board, syllabus and components rather than about which school they work at. Any tutor who offers access to internal papers or deadlines should be reported to us straight away.

faqs.question: We are in Borivali and the best Higher Level tutor is in Chembur. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Take the Chembur specialist online and keep a local tutor for accountability if you need one. A Chembur to Borivali journey crosses the city at the worst hour and will not survive a term, whatever anybody promises in week one. For a thin Higher Level subject the specialist genuinely matters more than the format, so run the subject sessions online and, if your child needs physical supervision, book a nearby tutor for supervised timed practice in a different subject. What does not work is a weaker Borivali generalist at Higher Level, which costs more in the long run than the inconvenience of a screen.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week actually enough to change anything?
faqs.answer: For one subject with a clear, identified weakness, yes, provided the work between sessions happens. Weekly home tuition is priced and planned on exactly that assumption. The hour is for diagnosis, correction and setting the next task; the improvement happens in the days in between. For two or three subjects under pressure at once, one hour each is not enough and five hours a week is too much, because the child then has no time left for the independent practice the exam measures. The honest answer in that situation is to prioritise one subject, fix it, and move on rather than spreading thin across everything and improving nothing.

faqs.question: She understands everything in the session and cannot do it alone afterwards. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the session is being taught as a demonstration rather than as practice, and this is the single most common structural fault in private tuition. Understanding someone else's solution feels identical to being able to produce one, and it is not the same skill at all. The fix is to change the shape of the hour: the tutor explains for ten minutes, then the child works while the tutor watches and says nothing, then they review the errors. Ask for that explicitly. A tutor who fills the hour with fluent explanation is producing a comfortable session and very little transfer.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to VIBGYOR High in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation, partnership or endorsement arrangement with VIBGYOR High, any of its campuses, or any other school named on this page. Schools appear here purely as local context, so parents can see that we understand the commute and the calendar their family works around. We hold no information about any school's internal deadlines, its marking or its staff, and we do not represent families in dealings with a school. Registration, deadlines and programme requirements should always be confirmed with the school office directly.

faqs.question: Can we start in January, or is that too late to be useful?
faqs.answer: It is late but not useless, and what changes is the plan rather than the answer. Starting in the second half of the year means the work becomes examination-focused: past papers under timed conditions, mark-scheme analysis, and targeted repair of the two or three topics costing the most marks. There is no time to rebuild a foundation gap from Year 8 and no point pretending otherwise, so a good tutor will triage openly and tell you which topics are being abandoned. For coursework still in draft, a January start can still matter a great deal. For a subject that needs rebuilding from the base, be realistic about what one term delivers.

faqs.question: What should the tutor send us after each session?
faqs.answer: Three lines are enough and you should insist on them from the first week: what was covered, what has been set for the child to do alone, and what is still weak. That short note is what lets you check progress without sitting in the room, and it is what makes a conversation with the tutor in week six specific rather than vague. It also exposes drift quickly, because a tutor who writes the same third line for four consecutive weeks is not getting traction. Agree the format at the start; asking for it in month three feels like a complaint and is usually too late.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Airoli or Thane for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, from within the same corridor. Airoli is well served by tutors from Mulund, Bhandup and Thane across the Trans-Harbour and Central lines rather than from the rest of Navi Mumbai, which surprises families who assume Vashi or Nerul is closer in practice. Thane is covered from Thane itself, with Ghodbunder Road setting the realistic limit on how far west an evening slot can go. What does not hold through a term is a tutor from the Western Suburbs or the island promising a weekday evening journey, and we would rather put that person online than watch the slot collapse in week three.

sections.heading: The IGCSE and IB pathways Witty families in Mumbai are choosing between
paragraphs: Witty International School publicly offers both an IGCSE pathway and an International Baccalaureate (IB) pathway across its Malad and Chembur campuses. That is the whole of what we will claim about the school, and it is enough to explain the decision in front of you. The International General Certificate of Secondary Education, run by Cambridge International Education, is a two year programme usually taught across Years 9 to 11 and assessed by terminal papers in a May or June or an October or November series. The IB side runs the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and then the Diploma Programme (DP), assessed continuously against published criteria as well as by final examinations.

The two systems reward different habits, and this matters more than any league table. IGCSE rewards a student who can answer a tightly worded question in the way the mark scheme expects, repeatedly, under time pressure. The Diploma Programme rewards a student who can plan, draft, redraft and justify, because the Internal Assessment (IA), the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) are all extended pieces with staged deadlines. A child who thrives on a weekly past paper drill can struggle badly with a Chemistry IA, and the reverse is just as common.

For families at Witty, the practical question is usually whether to take Extended or Core papers at IGCSE and, two years later, which three subjects go to Higher Level (HL). We do not advise on that in isolation. A tutor who has marked the Extended paper can tell you what the Extended grade thresholds actually demand of a borderline student, which is a far more useful input than a general opinion about ambition. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Witty International School, so nothing we say here reflects the school's own guidance to you.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Core or Extended, HL or SL: what actually transfers across a campus move
paragraphs: Across all IB and IGCSE subjects, roughly half of what a tutor builds with a student transfers cleanly to a new tutor and roughly half does not. Knowing which half is which is the difference between losing a fortnight and losing a term. Content knowledge transfers. A student who understands moles and limiting reagents understands them in Chembur exactly as she did in Malad. Technique on a specific paper transfers, because the paper does not change. A written error log transfers, if one exists. What does not transfer is anything held in a particular teacher's head about a particular rubric.

The internal assessments are where this bites. An IGCSE coursework component, a Global Perspectives team project, an MYP Criterion C investigation or a DP Internal Assessment all have an approved topic, a drafting history and a marker who has already given feedback once. A new tutor who restarts that conversation costs the student weeks of real work. A new tutor who reads the existing drafts and the feedback already received can pick up mid paragraph. So the first thing we ask for on a handover is not the report card, it is the last marked draft with the comments still on it.

Subject by subject, the clean transfers are Maths, Physics, Chemistry and Economics, where the skill ladder is explicit and a diagnostic reveals the gap in one session. The ones that need a genuinely fresh diagnostic are English Language and Literature, Business Management and any second language, because so much of the mark depends on a style of response the previous tutor was coaching towards. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai taking over a Language A course mid-year should expect to spend the first two sessions reading, not teaching.

What we do know is the shape of the IGCSE and IB year as it is published by Cambridge International Education and the International Baccalaureate, and that shape is the same for every school in Mumbai running these programmes. It is what produces the pressure points below.

The academic year opens in June, and for the first two months almost nothing is urgent, which is exactly when a tutor should be hired and almost nobody does. October and November bring the first serious internal assessments on both pathways, and for Diploma Programme students in their second year, several IA deadlines land in the same fortnight. January and February are the hardest stretch: IGCSE coursework is being finalised while final mocks run, and DP students are redrafting the Extended Essay against a hard school deadline. Families at Witty also sit inside a cluster of other Cambridge and IB schools that set the local tutoring market, and knowing them helps you read availability. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid when you move from Malad to Chembur?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and it should be. For a Witty student in Years 9 to 11, a tutor at the dining table with the student's own past paper scripts, her own calculator and her own annotated textbook in front of them is worth more than any screen share. The tutor sees the working, sees the crossings out, sees which question she skipped and came back to. We arrange IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai as the lead service on both sides of the city, with standing weekly slots cleared through the society gate once rather than negotiated every week.

Online earns its place in two specific situations. The first is a scarce subject: if your child needs Higher Level Further Mathematics, Design Technology or a less common second language, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai, or one outside the city altogether, may simply be the only person qualified. The second is traffic. A 7pm slot that requires a tutor to cross the SCLR or run north along the Western Express Highway will be cancelled or shortened more often than either side admits, and an online session that actually happens beats a home session that keeps slipping.

Hybrid is the answer to the specific problem this page is about. When a family moves from the Malad campus to the Chembur campus mid-year, the clean solution is not to replace the tutor on moving day. It is to keep the existing tutor online for three or four weeks while a local tutor starts in person on the eastern side, with both working from the same written plan. The outgoing tutor holds continuity on the IA or coursework; the incoming tutor runs the fresh diagnostic and takes the paper technique. After a month, one of them steps back. Running all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai works well, but during a handover the overlap is the point.

sections.heading: How are tutors verified, and what should a Mumbai parent check themselves?
paragraphs: Every IB and IGCSE tutor for Witty International School students in Mumbai on our panel has had identity and qualification documents checked, has been asked component level questions about the syllabus they claim to teach, and has given contactable references from previous families. That is what verification means here, and it is deliberately narrow. We check that a person is who they say they are and has taught what they say they have taught. We do not and cannot verify anything about any school, including Witty International School, with which IB Gram is not affiliated.

What we cannot check is fit, and fit is where most placements fail. So there are three things worth doing yourself, and they take ten minutes. Ask the tutor which syllabus code they are teaching to and whether it changes for the next series. Ask them to talk through one question from your child's last marked paper, with the paper in front of them. Then ask what they will be able to tell you after four weeks that they cannot tell you now. A tutor who answers all three concretely is a tutor who has done this before.

On a handover specifically, add a fourth question: what will you want from the previous tutor? The right answer is specific. The last marked draft, the error log, the past paper scores broken down by component, the IA stage and the school's own internal deadlines. A tutor who says they prefer to start fresh is telling you they intend to re-teach ground your child has already covered, and in January that is a term you do not have. Ask for the handover note in writing before the first session, not after.

sections.heading: Moving campus mid-year in Mumbai: the handover that decides whether the term holds
paragraphs: Here is the fact that shapes everything on this page. Malad and Chembur are not two neighbourhoods, they are two cities for the purpose of a weekly lesson. Malad is Western Line and Link Road. Chembur is Harbour Line, Central Line, the SCLR and the Eastern Freeway. There is no direct train between them; you change at Dadar or you cross by road. A tutor who serves one campus almost never serves the other, so a family that moves from one to the other is not changing address, it is changing tutoring markets. When that happens in October or January, the instinct is to go shopping for a better tutor. That instinct is wrong. The variable that decides whether the term holds is the quality of the handover, not the quality of the second tutor.

Take a concrete case. A Year 11 student is sitting IGCSE Physics and losing marks on Paper 4, the Extended written paper. Her Malad tutor has worked out, over six weeks, exactly what is wrong: given a velocity time graph and asked for the total distance travelled and then the acceleration over a named interval, she sets up the area under the graph correctly and reads the gradient correctly, then loses the final mark because the axis is in kilometres per hour and the answer is wanted in metres per second squared. Her physics is sound. Her multi step unit conversion is not. That single sentence, written down, is the whole value of six weeks of work.

If that sentence travels to the Chembur tutor, the second IB and IGCSE tutor for Witty International School students in Mumbai starts on Paper 4 unit conversion drills in session one and the student loses nothing. If it does not travel, the new tutor runs her own diagnostic, sees weak Paper 4 marks, and reasonably concludes that kinematics needs re-teaching. Three weeks go on ground she already holds, and the actual defect is still there in February. Meanwhile her Chemistry IA, with an approved research question and one round of feedback already received, must not be reopened at all; the new tutor's job there is to read and continue.

So the questions to ask when you relocate across Mumbai are not about credentials. They are: which of my child's subjects transfer cleanly and can be picked up at the point they were left, which need a fresh diagnostic because the mark depends on a coached style of response, what is written down that the next tutor can read, and who is paying for the overlap weeks. Settle those four and the second tutor can be merely good. Leave them unsettled and the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai cannot save the term, because he will spend it rediscovering what somebody already knew.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a mark to move, and a tutor who promises one is not being straight with you. What you should expect is evidence of diagnosis: a written list of the specific things going wrong, a changed homework pattern, and your child able to tell you what she is working on in component terms rather than saying the subject name. If none of that exists after four weeks, the placement is not working and you should say so rather than wait politely for the term to end.

At one term, marks should move at component level on past papers taken under timed conditions. Not the final grade necessarily, but the specific paper or criterion that was identified in week one. This is why the week one diagnostic matters so much: without it there is no baseline, and without a baseline any conversation about progress becomes a conversation about feelings. At one full examination cycle, a grade change is a reasonable thing to discuss. Even then, IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor who has taught these boards honestly would.

When a placement is not working, tell us in writing and we replace the tutor. There is no argument and no notice period beyond the sessions already booked. The outgoing tutor writes the handover note as a condition of the placement, and the incoming tutor reads it before the first session, which is the same discipline this page argues for in a campus move. We also say no sometimes. If a student is three grades below target with eight weeks to the series, we will tell you what is achievable in eight weeks rather than sell you a package. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with Witty International School or any other school named on this page, and we do not guarantee results.

sections.heading: Starting home tuition in Mumbai after a campus move: what to prepare
paragraphs: Prepare five things and the first session is worth paying for. The most recent school report. The last two marked papers or drafts with the marker's comments still on them, which matters more than the report. The syllabus code for each subject, because Cambridge and the International Baccalaureate both revise specifications and the wrong code means the wrong past papers. The current stage of any coursework or Internal Assessment, including whether the topic is approved. And the school's own internal deadlines for the next term, which are the deadlines that actually bind.

The first session is a diagnostic, not a lesson, and you should want it that way. The tutor gives timed questions from the relevant paper, watches how your child works rather than whether she gets the answer, and writes down what is wrong in component terms. You get that in writing within a day or two. From there the plan covers six weeks, names the component being targeted, and says how it will be measured. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai cannot fix four subjects at once, so the plan will usually pick two.

If you are mid-move between the Malad and Chembur campuses, say so in your first message. We will shortlist on the side of Mumbai you are moving to, not the side you are leaving, and we will ask whether the outgoing tutor can stay online for three or four weeks of overlap. If there was no previous tutor, that is fine too; we simply build the baseline from the marked scripts instead of from a handover note. Either way the first session covers the same ground, and neither route involves us claiming any connection to your child's school.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Witty International School in any way?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor matching platform and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Witty International School. We have no access to the school's staff, teaching materials, internal mark schemes or student reports, and no tutor on our panel is presented as a current or former member of its faculty. What we work from is public information, that the school runs campuses in Malad and Chembur offering IGCSE and IB pathways, plus the published Cambridge International Education and International Baccalaureate specifications that every school on these boards follows. If you want the school's own view on subject choice, ask the school.

faqs.question: We are moving from the Malad campus to the Chembur campus in November. Do we have to change tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly yes for the in person sessions, and that is a scheduling fact rather than a judgement on your tutor. Malad sits on the Western Line and the Link Road; Chembur sits on the Harbour and Central lines with the SCLR and the Eastern Freeway. There is no direct train, so a tutor crossing for a weekday evening slot will start cancelling within a month. What you should not do is simply swap one tutor for another. Keep the Malad tutor online for three or four weeks of overlap while a Chembur based tutor starts in person, both working from one written plan.

faqs.question: What exactly should a handover note contain?
faqs.answer: Five things, and it should fit on one page. First, the specific defect in component terms, for example marks lost on unit conversion in multi step IGCSE Physics Paper 4 questions rather than weak at Physics. Second, past paper scores broken down by paper or criterion, with dates. Third, the stage of any coursework or Internal Assessment, including whether the research question is approved and what feedback has already been given. Fourth, what has been tried and did not work. Fifth, the school's internal deadlines for the coming term. Ask for it in writing before the new tutor's first session, not afterwards.

faqs.question: Which subjects transfer cleanly to a new tutor and which do not?
faqs.answer: Maths, Physics, Chemistry and Economics transfer cleanly because the skill ladder is explicit and a single diagnostic session exposes the gap. A new tutor can pick these up at the exact point the previous one left off. English Language and Literature, Business Management and second languages need a genuinely fresh diagnostic, because a large part of the mark depends on a style of response the previous tutor was coaching towards, and two competent tutors can coach towards different styles. Internal assessments sit in their own category: never reopen an approved topic. The new tutor reads the existing drafts and the marker's comments, then continues from there.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to our building in Malad West on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if we match a tutor who already works that corridor, and no reliably if we do not. This is why we filter by side of the city before anything else. A tutor living or teaching along the Western Line between Goregaon, Malad West, Malad East and Kandivali, with Metro Lines 2A and 7 above the Link Road as a fallback, will hold a 6.30pm or 7pm slot for a full term. A tutor coming from Chembur or Powai across the SCLR will manage it for a few weeks and then start asking to move the session. Book the corridor, not the resume.

faqs.question: Our society in Chembur requires a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work?
faqs.answer: Clear it once, as a standing weekly entry, rather than per visit. Most Mumbai societies will register a regular tutor for a fixed day and time if a resident requests it in writing at the office, and that single step removes the most common cause of a lost fifteen minutes. We ask tutors to carry photo identification to every session regardless. Tell us at the matching stage if your building requires prior approval for each visitor or restricts entry after a certain hour, because in Chembur, Govandi and Kurla that varies considerably between complexes and it changes which evening slots are realistic for your family.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five factors, and we will not quote a number because any figure here would be invented. Board and level: Diploma Programme Higher Level costs more than IGCSE Core. Subject scarcity: Higher Level Further Mathematics or a less common language has far fewer qualified teachers in the city than Maths or Biology. Travel distance and timing, since a tutor crossing the SCLR in the evening peak is spending time you are effectively paying for. Session length and frequency. And whether you need overlap weeks during a handover, which temporarily means two tutors. Ask for the rate per session and what happens to a cancelled session before you commit.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for an IGCSE science practical paper?
faqs.answer: For the alternative to practical and practical based written papers, yes, with one condition: the student must have the paper printed and in front of her. These components test whether a student can read a results table, spot the anomalous reading, describe a control variable and evaluate a method, and all of that can be taught over a screen share. What does not work online is diagnosing handwriting, working layout and the order in which a student attacks a paper, which is exactly what the first diagnostic session is for. That is a strong argument for running the diagnostic at home even when the weekly sessions will be online.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us in writing and we replace them, with no argument and no notice period beyond sessions already booked. Three sessions is a reasonable point to judge: by then you should have a written diagnosis, a changed homework pattern and a child who can describe what she is working on in component terms. The outgoing tutor writes a handover note as a condition of the placement, so the replacement does not start from zero. Say what specifically did not work, whether it was the explanation, the pace, the timing or simply the fit, because that is what lets us match differently rather than just match again.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the baseline and compare against it, rather than relying on impressions. At four weeks a mark should not necessarily have moved, so the question is whether the diagnosis exists and is specific. If the tutor can show you the week one timed paper, the written list of defects and this week's work targeting one of them, the placement is on track and you should give it a term. If there is no baseline paper and no written list, that is the actual problem, and no amount of extra sessions fixes it. Request a diagnostic in writing or ask us for a replacement.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IGCSE and IB for two children in the same family?
faqs.answer: Often in Maths and the sciences, rarely in languages and the arts. The content overlap between IGCSE Extended Maths and Diploma Programme Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is real, and a tutor who teaches both routinely can run back to back sessions in one visit, which is also the cheapest way to buy two children's tuition. Where it breaks down is the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay supervision, which demands familiarity with the specific criteria and the moderation culture around them. We will tell you honestly when two tutors are the better answer rather than stretch one across both boards.

faqs.question: Do you cover Govandi and Kurla, or only the larger suburbs?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and they matter specifically for the Chembur campus. Govandi sits on the Harbour Line between Chembur and Mankhurd, and Kurla is the Central Line junction where the SCLR meets the Eastern Express Highway, which makes both of them workable for tutors already teaching in Chembur or Wadala. The honest caveat is subject depth: for a scarce Higher Level subject the local pool in these areas is thinner than in Powai or Bandra, and an online match may be the realistic option. For mainstream IGCSE and Diploma Programme subjects, a home tutor in Govandi or Kurla is straightforward to arrange.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: what changes when you search near me in Mumbai?
paragraphs: The younger the child, the more nearby matters, and the relationship is close to linear. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child needs short, frequent, utterly reliable contact: two shorter sessions a week beat one long one, and both have to actually happen. That rules out any tutor whose attendance depends on a clear run down Ghodbunder Road. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student can absorb an occasional reschedule but still benefits from a tutor who treats this address as local, because MYP work is cumulative across criteria and a three-week gap undoes the pattern-building.

At Diploma Programme (DP) level the calculation changes. A DP student in the second year is working on Internal Assessment (IA) drafts, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) alongside Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) papers, and the single most valuable attribute in a tutor becomes depth in one specific subject rather than proximity. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist who comes once a week from Thane West and holds short online contact in between will outperform a nearer generalist by a distance. So near me matters most at the age when parents worry about it least, and matters least when they worry about it most.

This page covers the International Baccalaureate continuum, which runs PYP through MYP into DP. The continuum point is practical rather than academic: a family in this complex may be hiring for a Year 5 child now and for a DP1 student in six years, and the radius they should accept changes completely between those two moments. Treating near me as a fixed rule for the whole of a child's schooling is how families end up with an excellent PYP tutor still teaching a DP2 student badly.

The platform breadth behind all of this is wide: all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai families look for, alongside the full IB continuum from the early years to the final examinations. Breadth helps only in one specific way here. It means that when a subject turns out to be thinly served inside your travel ring, we can tell you so on the first call instead of sending a near-enough match and letting the first term discover the problem. Most of what we arrange across this part of Mumbai is home tuition at a standing weekly slot, and the request that arrives as an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Ashford Royale almost always turns out to mean exactly that.

sections.heading: Which IB subjects run short of nearby tutors in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Higher Level sciences, the less common language acquisition options, and Theory of Knowledge, in that order. That is the practical scarcity list for this corridor, and knowing it in advance changes how you search. Mathematics at both routes, the sciences at Standard Level, English A and Economics are all well served within a short run of this gate, and for those subjects you should hold firm on proximity. Higher Level Physics and Higher Level Chemistry thin out quickly, and a parent insisting on a fifteen-minute radius for them is choosing between a close generalist and nothing. For the well-served subjects, home tuition in Mumbai at a fixed weekly hour is both available and cheap to arrange from inside the ring.

The Mathematics request deserves unpacking because it is the most common one we receive and the least precise. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are different subjects with different demands, and a student placed in the wrong one spends two years paying for a decision made in a fortnight. A tutor who has taught both can usually tell which fits within a few sessions. That diagnostic ability is worth more than any claim on a profile, and it is available within the ring, so there is no reason to travel for it.

Theory of Knowledge is the oddity. Very few tutors teach it well, almost nobody specialises in it locally, and the students who need help with it need a particular kind of help: structuring an argument about knowledge claims rather than learning content. This is the one subject where we routinely suggest an online tutor from elsewhere in Mumbai or beyond, because the nearest available option is frequently a subject teacher improvising. The Extended Essay sits in similar territory, though a strong subject tutor in the relevant discipline usually handles the supervision gap adequately.

Internal Assessment work changes the proximity calculation again, because the useful contact is short and frequent rather than long and weekly. A twenty-minute conversation about one paragraph of a research question, three days before a school deadline, is worth more than a ninety-minute visit a week later. A tutor forty minutes away can give you the former over a video call and the latter in person, and the combination is often the best available arrangement. Parents here ask about all IB and IGCSE subjects and the tutor in Ashford Royale who covers a full DP slate alone is a fiction we will not sell you.

paragraphs: Three rings, and they are not concentric with the map. Ring one is Bhandup, a short run along LBS Marg, where a tutor can hold a 5pm or a 6pm weekday slot with almost no risk and will treat a reschedule as a minor inconvenience rather than a wasted evening. Ring two is Mulund West, barely further in kilometres and almost as reliable, with the added advantage that many of its tutors already teach children at the school most families from this complex attend. Ring three is Thane West, which contains the largest pool of the three and the least predictable journey.

Thane runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch is what makes ring three a gamble rather than an option. A run that takes twenty minutes in the middle of the day takes most of an hour in the evening peak, and a tutor based out towards Kasarvadavali who commits to 6:30pm twice a week is making a promise the road will break. Thane tutors generally serve Thane. Mulund tutors cross over readily. Bhandup tutors regard this address as their own neighbourhood. The Eastern Express Highway sits underneath all of it and swings between quick and unusable without much warning.

What the seam gives you in exchange is choice, and it is genuinely unusual. Ashford Royale sits where the Mulund tutor pool and the Thane tutor pool overlap, which means the honest answer to who is available is often two answers rather than one. A family at a more typical Mumbai address gets whatever the single local pool holds. A family here can weigh a shorter journey against a deeper subject background, and can ask for both lists. We make a point of showing both rather than presenting the convenient one, and both lists are lists of people who will come to your flat, because home classes in Mumbai are what this corridor actually runs on.

The practical rule we give parents: put core weekly subjects in rings one and two, and spend ring three only on scarcity or on weekends. A Saturday morning from Thane West is reliable because the road is. The Trans-Harbour Line to Vashi and the Thane–Borivali Tunnel corridor open up occasional specialists from further out, which is useful for a monthly review session and useless for a weekly one. Reliable IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ashford Royale is built ring by ring, and parents who set the radius themselves before shortlisting rarely have to renegotiate a slot in November.

Proximity requirements tighten and loosen across the Mumbai IB year. In June and July, when the year restarts and nothing is urgent, a longer journey is survivable and worth testing. From late August, when MYP criterion tasks and the first DP1 assessments arrive together, the cost of a missed session rises. October and November bring internal examinations. The January to February window is where distance becomes genuinely expensive: a DP2 student is handling final Internal Assessment submissions, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and mock examinations in the same few weeks, and a tutor who cannot reliably appear is worse than no tutor because the family has planned around them. By that stage an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Ashford Royale is not a convenience, and home tutoring that holds its hour through February is the difference between a plan and a hope.

A worked version from this corridor. Two tutors are offered for a DP1 student in September. One lives in Bhandup with three years at Diploma Programme level. One lives beyond Majiwada with nine years and strong Higher Level credentials. For a core weekly subject with assessments landing from August, the Bhandup tutor usually produces more actual teaching across the year. For a single Higher Level science heading into the January crunch, the Thane tutor is worth the journey if the weekly slot is moved to Saturday morning and midweek contact goes online. The answer depends on the month and the subject, which is why there is no single best IB and IGCSE tutor in Ashford Royale.

Sulochanadevi Singhania School, or with any other school named here, and the schools are mentioned so families can place themselves. We do not guarantee grades either. sections.heading: When is home tuition in Mumbai worth more than a closer tutor?
paragraphs: Almost always, because a tutor in the room is doing something a screen cannot, and the near me search is usually an attempt to get exactly that. Home tutoring lets a tutor watch the working rather than read the answer, interrupt a wrong method on the second line, and register the difference between a student thinking and a student waiting. For PYP and MYP children, that supervision is the greater part of what you are paying for. In a gated complex the travel risk is absorbed once at the entrance: a tutor cleared for a standing weekly slot walks in and begins. That is why home tuition across this part of Mumbai holds up better than the map suggests it should.

Online earns its place in three situations and is oversold in all the others. Scarcity is the first and strongest: an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Ashford Royale working from South Mumbai or outside the city beats the nearest available generalist for Theory of Knowledge or an uncommon Higher Level option, with no close second. Deadline triage is the next: short, frequent screen time around an Internal Assessment draft outperforms a scheduled visit three days later. Monsoon weeks are the third, when the honest alternative is a cancellation.

Online is the wrong choice for a Year 8 student who cannot yet work alone, and we say so rather than take the easier booking. A child who stops working the moment nobody is watching is not helped by a video call, however strong the tutor. We also keep the first month of any match in person regardless of the long-term plan, because the relationship that makes later online sessions productive gets built across a table. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Ashford Royale families keep for years almost always started in the flat.

Hybrid is where a near me search often lands once a parent accepts the radius logic, and it is worth designing rather than drifting into. Take the best tutor inside your ring for the weekly in-person anchor. Take the specialist outside the ring for a Saturday morning or for short online contact around deadlines. That arrangement gives you reliability and depth at once, which neither a purely local nor a purely distant choice manages. Families who plan it in July run it comfortably by October; families who improvise it in January are managing a crisis.

sections.heading: Checking a nearby IB home tutor in Mumbai before the first session
paragraphs: Four checks run before any profile reaches you: identity documents, qualifications, specific International Baccalaureate teaching experience at the programme level you asked for, and references from families or schools the tutor has worked with. The experience check carries the weight. Teaching a subject and teaching it inside the IB assessment model are different skills, and a strong graduate without programme experience will misread what an MYP criterion descriptor or a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment is actually asking for. We ask which years, which components taken end to end, and what they did when a student stalled. Every tutor we put forward for home classes in Mumbai has answered those questions in a conversation rather than on a form.

For a near me enquiry we add a fifth check that matters more here than at a compact address: can this tutor hold this slot, from where they live, at that hour, for the length of a school year. We ask for the route and for the evenings they would rather not commit to. A candidate who names a road and an honest exception has thought about it. A candidate who says traffic is manageable has not, and we treat that as a flag rather than as enthusiasm. An over-promised slot costs a family teaching hours they have already paid for.

Your own checking is the part that decides the match, and it takes one conversation. Ask the tutor to describe the structure of the component your child is working on in their own words. Ask what they would do in the first fortnight, and be sceptical of a syllabus list offered in place of a diagnosis. Ask how and how often they will report to you. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest tutor can offer one. Ask what they will not do, and listen for a clear line on coursework, which tutors question and critique but never write.

Then ask your child one question after the first session, and ask it when the tutor has left: did they explain it, or did they do it? A tutor who leaves behind a page of neat completed exercises is comfortable and ineffective. If something feels wrong, tell us in week one. A change then costs nothing; a change in week eight costs a term of momentum, which is exactly what a parent searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me Ashford Royale was trying to protect in the first place.

sections.heading: What does near me actually cost you in tutor quality?
paragraphs: Usually less than parents fear for core subjects, and more than they expect for scarce ones. Inside a fifteen-minute ring around this gate, covering Bhandup and most of Mulund West, the pool is deep enough that insisting on proximity for Mathematics, Standard Level sciences, English A or Economics costs you almost nothing in quality. Push the same insistence onto Higher Level Chemistry, Theory of Knowledge or an uncommon language and the cost becomes severe, because you are no longer choosing among good options. That asymmetry is the single most useful thing to understand before shortlisting, and it is why we ask for the subject before discussing the radius.

There is arithmetic worth doing. A weekly commitment runs for something close to forty teaching weeks across a school year. A tutor inside the ring will lose a handful of those to illness, travel and festivals. A tutor crossing from beyond Majiwada on a weekday evening will lose considerably more, and the losses cluster in exactly the months that matter, because monsoon and examination season both make the roads worse. Compare two tutors on teaching weeks delivered rather than on years of experience claimed, and the near option often wins outright even when the profile looks weaker. An IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Ashford Royale who delivers thirty-eight weeks of home tuition beats a stronger name who manages twenty-nine.

The in-building option deserves honest treatment, because near me searches in a tower complex often end with a neighbour's recommendation. Sharing a tutor between two flats can work well when the children are in the same year, the same subject and roughly the same place in it, and when both families accept a fixed slot neither can move. It works badly when one child is ahead, which produces one bored student and one lost one, and it is a poor idea for coursework-heavy DP work where the sessions need to be individual. It is also worth saying that a shared arrangement gives you less leverage to change tutor, because you are negotiating with your neighbour as well.

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one exam cycle: honest timelines in Ashford Royale
paragraphs: Four weeks in, judge the diagnosis rather than the marks. You want a tutor who can point at a specific weakness in your child's own written work and explain what they are doing about it. You want fewer homework arguments. You want a child who can say what they are working on without being asked twice. A tutor who still reports that your child is capable and needs confidence has assessed nothing in a month, and that is grounds to move rather than to be patient. We review every match at four sessions for this reason, and the review question is the same whether you hired an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Ashford Royale or brought a specialist in from across Mumbai for home tuition once a week.

A term in, the measurable thing is how work is produced rather than how it scores. In MYP that shows up inside criteria: a student moving from the middle to the top of a single criterion band has changed something real even when the reported level has not moved. In the Diploma Programme it shows up in drafts arriving earlier and needing fewer rounds. A first Internal Assessment draft needing three rewrites is normal. A third draft still needing three is a signal about the arrangement, not about the student. Marks commonly move last, and the family that changes tutor in month two over a flat test score throws away the only thing that was working.

Across a full examination cycle the truthful answer is a range. Consistent weekly teaching and a student who works between sessions moves most students meaningfully, sometimes a great deal where the original problem was one identifiable gap. Consistent teaching and a student who does nothing between sessions moves almost nobody, and no tutor fixes that alone. We do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rates, and we will not suggest a block of intensive sessions in April substitutes for a year of work. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families engage in the final weeks can still help, but the honest word for it is triage.

The limits are worth stating in a page about proximity, because proximity solves one problem only. A nearby tutor cannot repair a subject or route choice that was wrong from the start, though they can help a student argue for a change while a change is still possible. A nearby tutor cannot write coursework and should refuse to. A nearby tutor cannot generate motivation in a student who has decided not to engage, and that conversation belongs with the school. Home classes in Mumbai are a strong instrument for a student who is trying and stuck, and a weak one otherwise, whether the tutor lives ten minutes away or fifty.

faqs.question: What does a first session with a nearby tutor look like?
faqs.answer: It should look like an assessment, not a lesson. faqs.answer: We advise the opposite order, and will say so before taking the booking. After that, moving to a hybrid pattern is straightforward and very common here: one in-person anchor session plus short online contact around deadlines. Starting online and hoping to move in person later usually produces a match that never quite settles, particularly for students below the Diploma Programme who need someone in the room.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we replace them, with no justification required and no retention call. faqs.question: Which months are hardest to find a tutor near Ashford Royale?

A family calling in January is competing for whatever slots remain, often an 8:30pm weekday or a weekend morning. faqs.answer: One for an older student, two shorter ones for a younger child, and fewer subjects than most families begin with. A Year 10 or Diploma Programme student already spending hours on school transport across Mumbai has a limited number of productive evenings, and filling three of them produces attendance rather than learning. Start with the subject where the gap is widest, run it for six weeks, and add a second only if your child is absorbing rather than merely sitting through sessions. Primary Years Programme children are the exception: frequency matters more than length at that age.

sections.heading: IB and IGCSE side by side: what each board asks of a Mumbai student
paragraphs: The two systems differ most in what they treat as evidence. The International Baccalaureate (IB) asks a student to demonstrate a skill against published criteria, repeatedly, in work produced over weeks: the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through criterion-referenced tasks and the personal project, the Diploma Programme (DP) through the Internal Assessment (IA), the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) alongside terminal papers. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel ask a student to perform on a set of papers on a set of days. Neither is harder. They reward different temperaments, and a child can be badly suited to one and comfortable in the other.

That difference decides what tutoring looks like. An IB student needs a tutor who can work to a rubric and to a deadline calendar, because much of the grade is produced at home over months. An IGCSE student needs a tutor who can build examination technique for a fixed day in May. A good IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai will tell you plainly which of those two jobs they are better at, and the honest ones have a preference. Families with children on both boards in the same flat, which is common in these towers when siblings started at different schools, usually need two tutors rather than one flexible person.

Mumbai adds a specific complication: board switching. Children move between IB and IGCSE schools mid-stream here more often than in most cities, and the transition is where marks disappear quietly. A student arriving into Year 10 IGCSE from MYP has the content but has never sat a paper under those conditions. A student going the other way can write under pressure but has never been assessed on process. Covering all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 tutoring in Mumbai means being honest that this transition is a term of deliberate work, not a gap a summer course closes.

Take structure from your school, not from here. Both the IB and the examination boards revise subject guides on their own cycles, so component names, criteria strands, paper patterns and weightings shift between cohorts. Ask the IB coordinator or the examinations officer for the document that applies to your child's session and hand it to the tutor at the start. A tutor who does not want to read it is telling you something useful about how they plan.

sections.heading: Subjects, HL and SL, and the internal assessments that follow a child
paragraphs: Subject choice is the highest-leverage conversation a tutor has with a family, and it happens before any teaching. At IGCSE the live decisions are the tier entry in Mathematics, whether to carry triple science, and whether a second language is being taken at a level that suits the child or the parent. In the Middle Years Programme the equivalent decision is which subject groups to invest effort in, because MYP 5 evidence is what a Diploma Programme coordinator weighs when a student asks for three Higher Level sciences. Getting those wrong is more expensive than a weak term, because the correction costs a year.

Higher Level and Standard Level are not the same subject at two speeds, and this is the misunderstanding that produces the most Year 12 distress. Higher Level adds breadth of content and, more importantly, a different expectation of independence: more extended reasoning, more unfamiliar application, less scaffolding. A student who copes at Standard Level because the teaching is good can struggle at Higher Level for reasons that have nothing to do with ability. A tutor arranging all IB and IGCSE subjects tutoring in Godrej Platinum should be willing to say, in Year 11, that a proposed Higher Level choice is not supported by the evidence.

Internal assessment is where the boundary between help and misconduct sits, and it needs stating plainly. A tutor may teach the skill, rehearse it on a parallel task, and explain a rubric or mark scheme. A tutor may not draft, edit or substantially shape the submitted work, whether that is an IB Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an IGCSE coursework component. Any tutor who offers to improve the actual submission is creating a risk your child carries, not you. Ask the question directly on the first call and listen for how fast they answer.

Across both boards the scarce specialisms in Mumbai are consistent: Higher Level Economics and Business, Computer Science, Physics taught by someone who has marked, and the less common second languages. Scarcity limits your options rather than the quality on offer. For Mathematics, English, Biology and Chemistry this address has genuine depth to choose from, so sequence your search: fix the scarce subject first, then arrange the common ones around the slot you secured.

Online is the right answer in two cases and it is worth naming them exactly. Hybrid is the arrangement most families here converge on, and here it looks different from the usual split because of the short-notice option. paragraphs: A weekly visitor for three terms deserves more scrutiny than a one-off consultant, and the checks split between what we do and what only you can do. It tells you more than any certificate: you will see immediately whether they write to the child or to the parent, and whether their comments name a specific error or offer encouragement. Then ask what they would do in the week before a mock if the student were clearly unprepared. A tutor who says they would cut content and drill technique has thought about it. Access protocol is worth settling before the first visit, because a township entrance is not a single building lobby. A tutor who would prefer a closed door with a school-age child should be declined on the spot and reported to us, and we will act on it.

paragraphs: It buys responsiveness, and responsiveness is worth more than an extra credential. The second thing it buys is survival of the arrangement. Tutors are rational about their own time, and the slot they quietly release when their schedule fills is always the one with the worst travel. Families usually discover this in November, when the tutor who was excellent in August starts asking to move to Saturdays. Here the walk from the station means your slot is rarely the one under pressure, which is why matches at this address tend to run a full academic year rather than a term. Durability is not a nice side effect; it is most of what you are buying, because changing tutors costs a month of momentum.

The third thing, less obvious, is rescheduling without loss. School trips, sudden tests and illness move sessions constantly, and a tutor with a long commute can only offer you a cancellation. A tutor nearby can offer you Thursday instead of Wednesday. Over a year that difference is worth several sessions. So when a parent asks for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Godrej Platinum, the useful translation is the best tutor who can still be flexible with you in March, and those two descriptions point at different people more often than not.

None of this argues for accepting a weak tutor who happens to live nearby. It argues for a sequence: filter on genuine subject and board competence first, then among the people who clear that bar, choose the closest. Where no nearby candidate clears the bar, buy the distant specialist online and keep a nearby generalist for the in-person work. Families arranging all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Godrej Platinum often end up with exactly that pairing, and it is a better outcome than compromising on either axis alone.

sections.heading: Honest milestones across four weeks, a term and an exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks, you should be able to answer three questions yourself without asking the tutor. What is the one thing my child is working on right now? What changed in how they start homework? What has the tutor actually shown me from a marked script? If you can answer all three, the match is working even if no test score has moved yet. If you cannot answer any of them, the problem is not patience. Ask us for a different tutor that week, because the families who tell us they regret something almost always regret waiting. Those three questions are the whole of the week-four review for an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Godrej Platinum, and answering them takes five minutes.

Over a term, expect improvement to be lumpy and sequenced rather than steady, and expect a stretch that looks like stagnation. Once the mechanical losses are cleared, what remains are the marks that need judgement: choosing the right method on an unfamiliar question, structuring an extended response, knowing when an answer is finished. Those move slowly and they move last. A student whose score jumps and then sits still for six weeks is usually in exactly that phase. The way to check is to look at where the marks are now being lost, not at the total.

After a full examination cycle, assess it without rewriting the story. Some students gain substantially, some gain modestly, and some barely move because the real constraint was never the teaching: an impossible timetable, a subject chosen to satisfy somebody else, or chronic lack of sleep. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will never publish an average gain, because such a number would be meaningless applied to one child. A tutor who talks about a specific grade before seeing a term of work is describing an ambition, and the honest ones say so.

When you want a change, be concrete and we will be quick. Tell us whether the issue is the hour, the pace, the personality or the depth, and we rematch against that rather than starting from scratch. The incoming tutor receives a written handover covering what has been diagnosed and what has already been taught, so the first session is not a repeat of a diagnosis your child has already sat through. A second tutor is a normal event, not a failure, and the families who change early get a better year than the ones who hoped it would settle.

faqs.question: My children are on different boards. Can one tutor handle both?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and this comes up often in these towers because siblings frequently started at different schools. The IB asks a tutor to work to criteria and internal deadlines across weeks; Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel ask them to build technique for a fixed paper. Those are genuinely different skills and most good tutors are better at one. For the same subject at similar levels it can sometimes work with someone who has taught both and will say which they prefer. faqs.question: How do I judge a tutor before committing?
faqs.answer: Ask for two things on the first call. First, an example of written feedback they gave a student, with names removed: it shows whether they write to the child or to the parent, and whether their comments name a specific error or just encourage. Second, what they would do in the week before a mock with a clearly unprepared student. Cutting content and drilling technique is a considered answer; working harder is not. Those two answers separate an IB and IGCSE home tutor near me in Godrej Platinum who has genuinely taught these boards from one who has read about them. Be wary of anyone who volunteers a guaranteed grade, and decline a candidate who discusses outcomes before seeing marked work.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level the right choice if my child is coping at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the reason is independence rather than difficulty. Higher Level adds content but it mainly adds an expectation that the student handles unfamiliar application with less scaffolding. A child who does well at Standard Level because the teaching is strong can find Higher Level uncomfortable for reasons unrelated to ability. Ask a tutor to set unfamiliar application questions rather than revision questions and watch what happens. If your child stalls when the question is not recognisable, that is the signal, and it is far cheaper to learn it in Year 11 than in Year 12.

faqs.question: What happens if my child gets nothing out of the first month?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week four. We first separate two possibilities: a poor match, or a correct diagnosis of something tutoring cannot fix. A student on five hours of sleep with four co-curricular evenings does not need a fifth subject hour, and an honest tutor will have said so. If it is the match, we rematch against your specific complaint and the incoming tutor gets a written handover so the diagnosis is not repeated. One change is ordinary. The families who tell us they regret something are the ones who gave a bad match a second month.

faqs.question: Can sessions happen in the clubhouse study area instead of the flat?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is a sensible fallback during an older sibling's examination weeks or when the flat has one quiet room and two children needing it. Check your complex's rules first, because some require a resident present throughout and some limit booking hours. Arrange it with the tutor in advance rather than relocating on the evening, and keep it visible: a shared study space with other residents around is appropriate, a closed empty room is not. The flat stays the better default whenever it is genuinely available.

faqs.question: Do IB internal assessments mean the tutor helps with the actual work?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to is creating a risk your child carries. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, rehearse it on a parallel task with different data or a different text, explain the criteria, and help a student plan their own time. A tutor may not draft, rewrite or substantially shape an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an IGCSE coursework submission. Ask the question on the first call. The speed and clarity of the answer tells you most of what you need to know about the person.

faqs.answer: A few days for common subjects, longer for scarce ones. Mathematics, English, Biology and Chemistry can usually be rematched within a week at this address because the Central Line pool is deep for those. Higher Level Economics, Computer Science and the less common languages can take two or three weeks, and in those cases we would rather keep the existing tutor running while we search than leave a gap in term time. sections.heading: Two boards, and why the nearest home tutor is not always right
paragraphs: A tutor three buildings away who teaches the wrong board is further from you than a specialist in Mulund. This is the single most expensive mistake families in Hiranandani Estate make with a proximity search, because the two systems ask for different habits. International Baccalaureate (IB) work is criterion-referenced through the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and assessment-heavy through the Diploma Programme (DP), where Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices and internal assessments shape two years. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel qualifications are terminal written examinations with a Core or Extended tier decision behind them. Knowing which one your child is in is step zero.

The practical consequence shows up in what a session looks like. A good MYP tutor spends time on command terms and on having a student grade their own work against published criteria, because that is what the school will do. A good Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel tutor spends time on timed papers and on tracing a lost mark to a cause, because that is what the series rewards. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families imagine hiring in one person does exist at primary and lower-middle years, where the limiting skills are general. Beyond that point the boards diverge enough that a single generalist is doing two jobs averagely.

Families in the Estate often have both boards inside one flat, which is why this page exists at all. An older child may be on an IGCSE pathway at a Thane school while a younger one is in a Primary Years Programme (PYP) or MYP setting elsewhere in Mumbai. The two children do not need the same tutor, and trying to serve both with one person to save a slot usually costs the older one. Where it does work is logistics: one tutor taking two back-to-back hours in the same flat removes a second journey, and that is a real saving in a township where the journey is the hard part.

A student writing economics commentary work needs somebody who has marked it. An experienced tutor covering all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Hiranandani Estate families ask for can diagnose across the board, but when a specific internal assessment or a specific Extended paper is the problem, the person who has marked that exact thing is worth an extra twenty minutes of travel or a shift to a screen.

What a tutor should know is the shape of the assessment and the command words, and what they should ask for in the first week is the task sheet. Your own checks take ten minutes and are more predictive than anything on a profile. Ask which board and which syllabus version they last taught from, and what changed in it. Ask to see a piece of student work they marked themselves, with their own annotations on it. Ask what the first session will contain, and whether they want to see the last marked script. A tutor who asks for the script before the report card is a tutor who intends to diagnose.

IB Gram runs the checks and makes the introduction, and we do not guarantee grades. What we stand behind is that the person arriving at your door is who they said they were and has taught what they said they taught.

sections.heading: PYP to MYP to DP: where do IB transitions go wrong?
paragraphs: They go wrong at the two joins, not in the middle of any stage. A child can be entirely comfortable in the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and then struggle badly in the first year of the Middle Years Programme (MYP), because the work stops being judged on effort and curiosity and starts being judged against published criteria with specific strands. The second join is harder still: the Diploma Programme (DP) adds Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices and a core of extra work on top of a timetable that already felt full.

The Primary Years Programme ends with the Exhibition, which is the first time many children are asked to run a long piece of work themselves. Help at that point is almost never subject coaching. It is teaching a ten-year-old to turn a vague interest into a question that can actually be investigated, to find a source that is not the top search result, and to work to a plan that spans weeks. Parents in Hiranandani Gardens often book a mathematics tutor and discover within two sessions that the real gap was planning.

Moving into the Middle Years Programme, the first reports frequently shock families whose children had always been praised. The marks have not fallen because the child got worse; they reflect a criterion the child did not address because nobody explained that addressing it was the task. A tutor who has taught this stage opens the task sheet before the textbook, reads the strands aloud, and makes the student point at where in their own draft each one is answered. That habit is worth more over a year than extra content.

The Diploma Programme join is a scheduling problem as much as an academic one. Subject lessons, an Internal Assessment (IA) in most subjects, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity and service commitment all run at once. The students who cope are not the cleverest ones; they are the ones who were taught to work to a calendar in the Middle Years Programme. Starting home tuition in the year before the Diploma Programme rather than in the middle of it is the single most useful decision we see parents here make.

paragraphs: Send four things and the shortlist will be worth reading: the programme stage and year group, the subjects where the problem is real rather than suspected, a photograph of one recently marked piece of work or a criterion grid with the teacher's comments on it, and the afternoon hour you can actually hold every week. The marked work carries most of the diagnostic load. Five minutes of a teacher's annotations tell an experienced tutor more than twenty minutes of parental description.

The first visit has a predictable shape. The tutor spends the opening stretch establishing what the student thinks the problem is, which is frequently not the problem. A short piece of work or a task sheet is then attempted in front of them. Then they talk to you about what they found and what the first month will target, and they put it in writing. If the written version does not match the phone conversation, go back to the shortlist then rather than in March.

Protect the hour more fiercely than you protect the person. Arrangements in this neighbourhood rarely fail because of the wrong specialist; they fail because the slot moves every week for a school event, a cousin's birthday or a bad evening on JVLR. The great advantage of living a short walk from school is that a four o'clock hour is genuinely protectable here in a way it is not in most of Mumbai. Use that advantage, register the tutor once at the visitor desk, and give the arrangement a full month before forming a view.

One note on scope. This page covers the International Baccalaureate stages, from the Primary Years Programme through the Middle Years Programme to the Diploma Programme. We arrange shortlists spanning all IB and IGCSE subjects for home classes in Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, and if your child is on the Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel route our separate IGCSE page for this area is the one that will give you the right names. faqs.question: Can a tutor realistically reach our tower by 4pm on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are already working inside Powai, Chandivali or near Kanjurmarg that afternoon. A four o'clock start is actually easier here than a six o'clock one, because JVLR and the Eastern Express Highway are still moving at three thirty and are not by half past five.
