faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor in Kandivali West do in the first session?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic, not a lesson, and that is true of every maths match we make in Mumbai. The tutor works through two or three questions from your child's most recent marked paper, asks them to talk while solving, removes the calculator for part of it, and watches where the method breaks down. By the end they should name the first three topics to work on and say whether the problem is algebraic fluency, command words, unwritten method, calculator dependence or interpretation. Expect a short message from them afterwards describing what they found. A first session spent teaching a topic nobody diagnosed is a wasted hour.

faqs.question: My child gets correct answers but the report says show more working. Why does that cost marks?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded for visible reasoning, not for the final answer. A student who does three steps mentally and writes one line has given the examiner nothing to credit if the answer turns out wrong, and in a long question that can forfeit most of the available marks. It is a technique problem rather than a laziness problem, and it is fixed by a tutor who refuses to accept an unwritten step for about two weeks until writing the middle line becomes automatic. It is the most common reason parents here call us.

faqs.question: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: how do we choose?
faqs.answer: Start with the university courses on the shortlist, because some require the first route explicitly. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches suits engineering, physics, computer science and competitive economics, and it demands secure algebra. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation suits business, design, psychology and life sciences, and it demands comfort with data, modelling and technology. Neither is the easy option. If your child is strong at spotting patterns in real data and hesitant with algebraic manipulation, the second route often produces a better grade and a happier two years.

faqs.question: How early should a DP1 student start work on the mathematical exploration?
faqs.answer: September of DP1, well before the school's internal deadline. The marks that students lose on the exploration are mostly decided by the topic choice, and a question that is too broad cannot be rescued by later polishing. A good tutor spends a full session letting the student talk themselves out of two or three unworkable ideas and into one narrow question they can genuinely go deep on. Students who begin in January take whatever topic is still available, which is how a capable mathematician ends up with a thin piece of work.

faqs.answer: Usually not, and we will say so rather than sell you the cheaper option. A Year 9 student who cannot yet work unsupervised needs an adult who can see the page as it is being written, because maths goes wrong mid-line and a video call only shows the finished attempt. Online works well for a DP2 student who already works independently, for a scarce Higher Level specialist, and for short exploration conversations. For MYP fluency work, a weekly home visit does something a screen share cannot.

A tutor diagnoses which by setting a timed mixed-topic paper in week two rather than more exercises on the current chapter. The fix is practice conditions, not more content teaching.

Is it Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL)? And which year: Middle Years Programme (MYP), Diploma Programme year one, or year two with an exploration in progress? sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
paragraphs: They are two different subjects that share a name, and choosing wrongly costs more than any tutor can recover. Analysis and Approaches is built around algebraic fluency, proof and calculus, and rewards a student who enjoys manipulating expressions and following an argument to a conclusion. Applications and Interpretation is built around modelling, statistics and the use of technology, and rewards a student who can interpret a context and judge whether an answer is sensible. A student with weak algebra placed in Analysis and Approaches HL will struggle in a way no amount of extra hours fixes comfortably, and a student who likes structure and dislikes open-ended modelling can be equally unhappy in the other.

The level decision sits on top of that. Higher Level adds depth and additional content rather than simply more questions, and in HL the extra material arrives in the second year when the exploration and other deadlines are already competing for the same evenings. Most of the requests IB Gram sees for IB home tuition in Kanjurmarg in Mathematics come from DP1 students around the first proper assessment, which is exactly the right moment: the course has declared its real demands, the exploration has not started, and there is time to rebuild algebra if that is what the paper shows.

In the MYP the picture is different and often misread. MYP Mathematics is assessed against criteria, so a student can compute correctly and still score moderately for never communicating the reasoning or investigating the pattern the task asked about. Parents sometimes hire a Mathematics tutor in Kanjurmarg expecting content coaching when what the child needs is to learn to write mathematics as an argument. That skill is also the single best preparation for the DP, because the exploration and the longer examination questions both reward communication. This page covers the IB only; IGCSE Mathematics is a different course with a different tier structure and a sibling page owns it.

sections.heading: Where IB Mathematics marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Open a marked DP Mathematics paper and the losses sit in five recognisable places. The first is algebraic slips under time pressure: a sign error in a differentiation, a mishandled fraction, a bracket expanded wrongly in line two that makes every subsequent line unmarkable. The second is a show that question answered by working backwards from the given answer, which collects almost nothing. The third is reasoning not written down, where a student states a conclusion the mark scheme wanted justified. The fourth is the calculator: a graphic display calculator used as an answer machine on a paper that expects the method, or not used at all on a paper where it saves four minutes.

The fifth is command terms, and in Mathematics they are more precise than students assume. Hence means use what you just proved; otherwise means do not. Deduce, show that, verify and determine ask for different amounts of working, and a student who treats them identically donates marks in every paper they sit. A good IB maths home tutor in Kanjurmarg will spend part of an early session on nothing but these words and a stack of past questions, because the return is immediate and does not depend on learning any new mathematics. Parents often find this the most visible early change.

Diagnosis should be mechanical rather than impressionistic. A reasonable first session is a short set of questions spread across algebra, functions, trigonometry and calculus, chosen so that each one fails in a different way, with the tutor watching rather than helping. From that the tutor can usually say whether the problem is foundations from MYP Years 4 and 5, fluency at speed, communication, or technology, and those four need different terms of work. Ask any candidate to describe that diagnostic set on the call. A tutor who answers by naming topics they will teach has not understood the question. Mathematics home classes in Kanjurmarg that start with a textbook chapter rather than a diagnosis usually spend six weeks teaching the wrong thing.

sections.heading: Does maths tutoring work online, or does it need a table?
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where in-person has the clearest mechanical advantage, and the reason is the page. A tutor sitting beside a student sees the working as it is produced, spots the sign error in the line where it happened rather than three lines later, and can point at the page instead of describing a location. The second is marking between sessions: a student photographs a worked set on Wednesday and gets it back annotated on Thursday, which is worth more than waiting for Saturday. Online is the wrong primary mode for an MYP student who still needs someone to notice that the pen has stopped.

Most Mathematics families in this corridor end up with one visit plus one short online review each week, and setting that up at the start works better than drifting into it. Ask which course and level they taught most recently and in which year. Ask how they handle the exploration, and whether they would read a draft or only talk about it. Warning signs are the same in Mathematics as elsewhere but easier to spot. sections.heading: What does the mathematical exploration actually need from a tutor?
paragraphs: It needs a reader, a question-asker and a deadline enforcer, and nothing beyond that. The exploration is the student's own piece of mathematics on a topic they choose, assessed on criteria that include personal engagement and mathematical communication as well as the mathematics itself, so a tutor who supplies the topic has already damaged two of those. What a tutor can legitimately do is a great deal: push back on a topic that is too broad or too thin, ask whether the mathematics is actually at course level, point out where the write-up states results without justifying them, and insist that the student explain their own reasoning out loud before writing it down.

The most common failure IB Gram hears about is a topic chosen for interest with no mathematics in it, discovered three weeks before the draft. A tutor who sees the proposal early prevents that at the cost of one conversation. The second most common is a strong piece of mathematics written up as a set of results with no argument connecting them, which loses marks in communication regardless of how good the work is. Both are fixable, and both are much cheaper to fix at proposal stage than at draft stage, which is why the exploration dates belong in the first session rather than in month three.

Check the current subject guide or your school's Diploma coordinator for which criteria apply to your child's cohort and how the school sequences the drafts, rather than taking any weighting or word figure from a tutor or from this page; the IB revises its guides on its own cycle. What a tutor should give you instead is a plain account of where your child's draft currently stands against each criterion and what the next fortnight will address. A home tutor for Mathematics Mumbai parents hire specifically for exploration support should be able to give that account in two sentences after reading the draft once.

sections.heading: What four weeks of maths home classes in Mumbai should change
paragraphs: In Mathematics the four-week evidence is unusually concrete, which makes this an easy arrangement to judge. You should see a written diagnosis naming which of algebra, fluency, communication or technology is the real problem. You should see the student's working become longer and more legible, because that is what the fix looks like on paper. And you should see one marked set where the tutor's comments sit next to the school's. A grade is not on the list; school assessments arrive on the school's calendar. If none of the three exists at four weeks, nobody is measuring anything and another month will not produce it.

The realistic arc over a term depends on which of the four problems you have. Command terms and calculator discipline move fast, often within a fortnight, because they are habits rather than knowledge. Fluency at speed takes six to eight weeks of consistent practice, since it is built by repetition that has to actually happen between sessions. Foundational algebra from MYP Years 4 and 5 takes a term or more, because the tutor is rebuilding while the school advances into calculus, and the first visible gain may come after the next assessment rather than before it. Over a full DP, weekly teaching plus the student's own practice is a reasonable bet on improvement. It is not a promise, and we do not guarantee grades.

Two honest limits. Mathematics improves through problems the student works alone, so a tutor whose sessions consist of worked examples the student watches will produce a child who understands everything in the lesson and nothing in the test. Ask what is set between sessions and whether it gets marked. And there are cases for hiring nobody: a DP2 student scoring near target six weeks from final papers usually needs a revision timetable rather than a new adult, and a student whose difficulty is anxiety around assessment needs that addressed first, because Mathematics tutoring layered on top of it reinforces the fear rather than reducing it.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Mathematics: three different jobs
paragraphs: In the Primary Years Programme the work is conceptual and almost never looks like a worksheet of sums. A PYP child in Kasarvadavali is asked to explain why a strategy works, to represent the same quantity three ways, and to carry number sense into a unit of inquiry about markets or measurement. The common parent complaint at this stage is that there is no visible arithmetic practice to check. A tutor here spends most of the hour on fluency and mental method, then connects it back to whatever the class is inquiring into, so the child is not living in two unrelated mathematical worlds.

The Middle Years Programme is where Mathematics starts to be assessed on criteria rather than on right answers alone. An MYP student can produce a correct solution and still lose ground because the reasoning was never written down, the pattern was never generalised into a rule, or the real-life application at the end was two lines long. MYP4 and MYP5 also set the direction of travel: this is when a student discovers whether they can hold algebraic manipulation in their head or need it written out every time, and that discovery drives the route choice two years later.

The Diploma Programme is where the pressure becomes visible. Mathematics is compulsory, so every DP student is sitting one of the two routes at either Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL), alongside the mathematical exploration they write themselves. A great deal of IB home tuition in Mumbai starts in DP1 for exactly one reason: the student coasted through MYP on quick recall and has met a subject that now wants proof, structure and a graphic display calculator used properly. Our Mathematics IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai pool exists because families often need the same specialist to follow a child across two of these stages, not just one.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
paragraphs: Choose Analysis and Approaches if your child enjoys algebraic manipulation and wants engineering, physics, computer science or economics at a competitive university; choose Applications and Interpretation if they think better with data, modelling and context. That is the short version, and it is the decision most DP1 families in Kasarvadavali get wrong in one direction: they pick Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level because it sounds stronger on a transcript, then spend DP1 drowning in proof and calculus. The route is not a ranking. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is a demanding course with heavy statistics and modelling, and it is the better fit for a large number of capable students.

Across both routes the examined papers are structured around short response and extended response work, with a third paper at Higher Level that asks students to work through an unfamiliar investigation under time pressure. The skills that separate grades are consistent. Reasoning marks are given for stated method, not for the final number. Command words matter: show that, hence, deduce and justify each demand a different kind of writing, and a student who treats all four as solve will leave marks on the table in every paper they ever sit.

The graphic display calculator is the other quiet divider. Students who learned it from a classmate can plot a graph but cannot find an intersection, solve numerically, run a regression or check a result they obtained by hand. In Applications and Interpretation that is fatal, and in Analysis and Approaches it costs the verification step that catches careless algebra. A good tutor spends part of an early session purely on calculator discipline, which parents often find an odd use of an hour until the first paper comes back with four more marks on it. sections.heading: Home tuition or online classes for Mathematics in Kasarvadavali?
paragraphs: Start with home tuition for any student below DP2, and treat online as the fallback rather than the default. Mathematics is a subject learned at the point of the pen. A tutor sitting beside a student in Kasarvadavali sees the hesitation before a substitution, the sign error written confidently, the line skipped because it was done in the head. On screen, a tutor sees a finished answer and has to reconstruct the thinking that produced it. For MYP students and for DP1 students who have not yet learned to sit alone with a hard question, that difference is the whole value of the hour.

Online becomes genuinely competitive in two situations. The first is a DP2 student working on a narrow technical target, such as Paper 3 investigation technique or a single topic in the Analysis and Approaches calculus sequence, where a shared screen and a scanned script are enough. The second is scarcity: if your child needs Higher Level Applications and Interpretation, the Mathematics specialist who teaches that route may simply not live within reach of Ghodbunder Road, and an IB online tutor in Kasarvadavali who knows the route beats a nearby generalist who does not. Online is the wrong choice for a Year 8 student who cannot yet work unsupervised for ten minutes, and no amount of software fixes that.

Hybrid is what most families here settle into by the second term, and it is usually the right answer rather than a compromise. One home session a week carries the teaching and the accountability; a shorter online session mid-week handles a specific question set or a check on exploration progress without anyone crossing Ghodbunder Road at seven in the evening. The home classes we arrange in Mumbai are normally the anchor slot, with the online session moving around school commitments. An IB maths tutor in Kasarvadavali who refuses to work this way is usually protecting their own schedule rather than your child's.

sections.heading: Where do IB Mathematics students in Kasarvadavali actually lose marks?
paragraphs: The marks go in four predictable places, and none of them is the hard topic a parent expects. The first is unstated method. A student who writes the answer to a differentiation question without the line showing the chain rule applied has surrendered the reasoning marks before anyone assesses whether they understood. The second is command word blindness: show that wants a demonstration ending at the given result, hence wants the previous part used, and a student who solves from scratch each time runs out of time and loses the link marks. The third is calculator misuse, either over-reliance when exact form was required or under-use when a numerical check would have caught an error.

The fourth is the mathematical exploration, and it is the one where a tutor earns their fee most clearly. The exploration is a piece of independent mathematical writing on a topic the student chooses, and the marks reward personal engagement, genuine mathematical communication, reflection and correct use of mathematics at a level appropriate to the course. The failure pattern is almost always the same: a topic chosen because it sounded impressive, mathematics copied in at a level the student cannot explain, and reflection written in the last two days as a paragraph of feelings. A student in Kasarvadavali who picks the traffic flow on Ghodbunder Road, collects their own timing data across a week and models it has a stronger exploration than one who downloads a cryptography topic they do not understand.

A tutor's real job on the exploration is supervision discipline, not writing. They help narrow a topic to something small enough to do properly, insist that the mathematics is at the right level for the route, make the student explain every step out loud before it is written, and keep the reflection running through the piece rather than bolted on at the end. Plenty of families book Mathematics home classes Kasarvadavali specifically for this one piece of work, and then keep the slot for paper technique once it is submitted. The school supervises formally; a tutor keeps the week-to-week momentum between those meetings.

sections.heading: What progress looks like, and what no tutor in Mumbai can promise
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see changed behaviour, not a changed grade. The student attempts the harder questions in a problem set instead of stopping at the easy ones. They write more lines of method. They can tell you what a question is asking before they try to answer it. They stop saying they are bad at Mathematics and start naming a specific topic they find hard, which is the single most reliable early signal that the teaching is landing. If none of that has shifted in a month, something is wrong with the match and you should say so rather than wait politely for a term to end.

At one term you should see it in school assessments, though unevenly. Topics taught since the tutor arrived will look better than topics assumed from two years ago, and a report can still read as mixed while the underlying position improves. By one full examination cycle, a student who has had consistent weekly home tuition and who has done the practice between sessions usually sits papers differently: timing is managed, method is shown, and the questions that used to be skipped are attempted. That is the realistic arc, and it depends far more on the work between sessions than on the sessions themselves.

We are an independent tutor-matching platform, not a coaching chain, and we are not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate Organization or with any school named on this page. What we can state plainly is the limit of the service: a tutor cannot create two years of missing foundation in six weeks, cannot make a student practise, and cannot substitute for attending class. A tutor can diagnose accurately, teach the specific gap, and hold a teenager to a weekly standard, which is usually enough.

faqs.question: Should my child take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches if they enjoy algebra and proof and want engineering, physics, mathematics or competitive economics; Applications and Interpretation if they reason better with data, modelling and context. The choice should follow how the student actually thinks, not how the course title reads on a transcript. Look at Middle Years Programme work: a student who can hold three steps of algebraic manipulation mentally usually belongs in Analysis and Approaches, and a student who understood statistics faster than factorising usually belongs in Applications and Interpretation. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator has the current entry requirements and timetable constraints, which vary between schools in Mumbai.

faqs.question: My daughter did well in MYP5 but is struggling in DP1 Mathematics. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma Programme asks for written reasoning and sustained manipulation, while the Middle Years Programme often rewards a correct answer reached quickly. Students who relied on mental method and good recall meet a subject that wants method shown, exact forms kept, command words obeyed and a calculator used deliberately. This is the most common reason families in Kasarvadavali start Mathematics home classes in DP1. It is a fixable transition problem rather than a ceiling, and it is far cheaper to fix in August than in January, when mock examinations and the exploration deadline arrive in the same fortnight.

faqs.question: How many home classes a week does DP Mathematics need?
faqs.answer: Most Diploma Programme students here start with one weekly session and move to two during the mock season or while the exploration is being written. One session a week is enough if the student does the set work between visits, and two sessions a week with no practice in between achieves less than one session with practice. For Higher Level students carrying Paper 3 investigation work, a second shorter slot mid-week is often more useful than a longer single session. Decide after four weeks with the tutor rather than committing to a frequency on day one.

faqs.question: Does online Mathematics tuition work as well as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For a focused DP2 student working on a narrow target, yes. For a Middle Years Programme student or an unsupervised younger child, no, and we will say so. Mathematics teaching depends on watching the pen hesitate, and a screen shows a finished answer instead of the thinking that produced it. Where online wins outright is route scarcity: if your child needs Higher Level Applications and Interpretation and no specialist lives within reach of Ghodbunder Road, an online specialist beats a nearby generalist. Many families in Kasarvadavali end up hybrid, with the home session as the anchor.

faqs.question: What does a tutor actually do about the mathematical exploration?

A tutor helps narrow the topic to something small enough to finish properly, checks the mathematics is at the right level for the route, makes the student explain each step aloud before writing it, and keeps reflection running through the piece instead of appearing at the end. They do not write it, and a tutor who offers to is a problem for the student's academic honesty record. faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. Should we change tutor?
